Not a bug. Disregard — moving on.

**2. `ProductCardControl` size-row buttons don't recompute width on resize.** `BuildSizeRow()` computes `buttonWidth = Width / sizes.Count` once in the constructor from the design-time `Size = new Size(150, 156)`. The card is added to a `FlowLayoutPanel` which honors that fixed `Size`, so it likely never resizes — but if it ever did (or if you change the card size later), the size buttons won't re-lay-out. Worth confirming visually.

**3. `FrmItemCustomizer` Dock-order stack is fragile.** The comment even says "Added bottom-up because these are Dock.Bottom/Top mixed." It works, but mixing `Dock.Bottom` (`_confirmBtn`, `cancelBtn`) with `Dock.Top` and a `Dock.Fill`-less middle is exactly the kind of thing that produces one-off pixel drift. Also: `_confirmBtn` is added *after* `cancelBtn` in the `Controls.Add` sequence but `cancelBtn` has `Margin = new Padding(0, 0, 0, 6)` and `_confirmBtn` doesn't — likely a 6px asymmetry at the bottom that reads as misalignment.

**4. `TransactionView` header divider is `Dock.Bottom` inside a `Dock.Top` header panel** (`var divider = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Bottom, ... }` added to `header`). It's added *after* `sortRow` and `searchRow` in the `Controls.Add` sequence, which for mixed [Dock.Top/Bottom](https://dock.top/Bottom) means the divider lands at the bottom edge of the 92px header — under the sort row, not between search and sort. Intent unclear from code; needs a screenshot to confirm whether it reads as a divider under the whole header or floating in the wrong place.

So the intended 4px gap before the error label doesn't exist. Same pattern likely elsewhere.

**6. `_customerProfilePanel` height is fixed at 72** but its two children sum to 22 + 44 = 66 plus the panel's own implied padding — close but not exact, so either 6px of dead space at the bottom or the detail label clips. Needs a screenshot.

**7. `CartLineControl` width is set by the host as `_cartLinesPanel.ClientSize.Width - 4`** — that's a guess at scrollbar width. When the flow panel shows a vertical scrollbar (long order), the lines will be ~13px too wide and clip horizontally. Classic. ## A + B — Transactions right column rework + Log Sale button

**B (right column unification):** The right column currently has `BackColor = SurfaceCard` (tinted gutter) with white `FixedSingle` boxes floating inside it. Change the column to `BackColor = SurfacePrimary` so the gutter disappears, and give the Order box, Payables box, and a new Log Sale box even spacing (consistent `Margin`/`Padding`) so they read as three stacked bordered boxes in one column.

**A (Log Sale):** Replace the tinted `bar` wrapper with a proper bordered box matching Order/Payables — `SurfacePrimary` fill, `FixedSingle` border — with the button filling it edge-to-edge minus a consistent inner padding. ### `TransactionView.cs` changes

In `BuildOrderColumn()`:

```csharp
private Panel BuildOrderColumn()
{
    // B: column is now SurfacePrimary (was SurfaceCard) — no visible gutter behind the
    // three boxes. Spacing is now owned by each box's own Margin, applied uniformly.
    var column = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Right, Width = 250, BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary };

    var orderBox = BuildOrderBox();
    var payablesBox = BuildPayablesBox();
    var logSaleBox = BuildLogSaleBox();

    column.Controls.Add(orderBox);
    column.Controls.Add(payablesBox);
    column.Controls.Add(logSaleBox);

    return column;
}
```

`BuildOrderBox()` — bump the margin so it matches Payables/LogSale (currently `Margin = new Padding(10)` which is asymmetric once the others use `(10,0,10,10)`):

```csharp
private Panel BuildOrderBox()
{
    var box = new Panel
    {
        Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
        Margin = new Padding(10, 10, 10, 10),   // was new Padding(10)
        BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle,
        BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
    };
    // ... rest unchanged ...
}
```

`BuildPayablesBox()` — keep its `Margin = new Padding(10, 0, 10, 10)` (it sits directly under Order, so no top margin), height stays 214.

New `BuildLogSaleBox()` replacing `BuildLogSaleBar()`:

```csharp
private Panel BuildLogSaleBox()
{
    // A: was a tinted SurfaceCard "bar" whose padding let the tint show through around
    // the brand-colored button (read as an unintended background rectangle). Now it's a
    // third bordered box in the column, matching Order/Payables — button fills it edge
    // to edge inside a uniform inner padding.
    var box = new Panel
    {
        Dock = DockStyle.Bottom,
        Height = 56,
        Margin = new Padding(10, 0, 10, 10),
        Padding = new Padding(10),
        BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle,
        BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
    };

    _logSaleBtn = new Button
    {
        Text = "Log Sale",
        Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
        FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat,
        BackColor = BrandPalette.ButtonPrimaryFill,
        ForeColor = BrandPalette.ButtonPrimaryText,
        Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(10.5f),
        Enabled = false,
    };
    _logSaleBtn.FlatAppearance.BorderSize = 0;
    _logSaleBtn.Click += (s, e) => _transactionViewModel?.CompleteSaleCommand.Execute(null);
    ButtonStyler.TrackEnabledState(_logSaleBtn);

    box.Controls.Add(_logSaleBtn);
    return box;
}
```

**One caveat I want to flag, not silently fix:** with `Dock.Bottom` on both Payables and Log Sale, WinForms stacks Bottom-docked siblings in reverse add-order — the **last** one added lands at the **bottommost** edge. In `BuildOrderColumn()` above, Payables is added before Log Sale, so Log Sale ends up at the very bottom and Payables sits just above it. That's the intent. But because all three are `Dock`-ed siblings, their `Margin` values are honored by docking (docked controls respect `Margin` as spacing between siblings), so the insets should come out even. Worth a visual check after.

## 1. Drinks header — "Sort by Category:" label overlaps the ComboBox

Confirmed, the screenshot shows it clearly. Cause: both controls are absolutely positioned in `BuildDrinksArea()`:

```csharp

_categoryCombo = new ComboBox { Location = new Point(200, 2), Size = new Size(160, 26), ... };
```

The label at `x=90` renders its full width, but it's positioned based on the *old* font metric — the ComboBox at `x=200` starts before the label's rendered right edge (~x=210 with the current font), so they collide by ~10px. Same class of bug as the original `Location`-based positioning everywhere in this header.

My default proposal: **the ComboBox re-populates every time `RefreshAfterCartChange` fires (same as today's button does), and if the currently-selected promo is no longer in the eligible list, it's cleared back to the placeholder.** Applied promo stays applied on the order (`ApplyPromo` already adds a `CampaignRedeem`), so the discount doesn't vanish, but the ComboBox no longer shows it as selected. ## 3. Drinks defaults to "All" (not a specific category)

Confirmed — this is actually a bug, not a preference. In `BuildCategoryOptions()`:

```csharp
_categoryCombo.Items.Add(AllCategoriesOption);
foreach (var category in _catalogService.GetCategories())
    _categoryCombo.Items.Add(category);
_categoryCombo.SelectedIndex = 0;   // "All Categories"
```

That *does* default to All. But then:

```csharp
_categoryCombo.SelectedIndexChanged += (s, e) =>
{
    if (_transactionViewModel is null || _categoryCombo.SelectedItem is not string category) return;
    _transactionViewModel.SelectedCategory = category == AllCategoriesOption ? string.Empty : category;
};
```

...and in `TransactionViewModel`:

```csharp
_selectedCategory = Categories.FirstOrDefault() ?? string.Empty;
```

So `TransactionViewModel` **starts** with `SelectedCategory = "Cold Brew"` (or whatever `GetCategories()` returns first, alphabetical: "Cold Brew"), because `BuildCategoryOptions()` runs *after* the TransactionViewModel is constructed but `_categoryCombo.SelectedIndex = 0` never fires `SelectedIndexChanged` for the TransactionViewModel (it's still null at that point, since no customer is selected yet). Then when a customer *is* selected and a new `TransactionViewModel` is constructed, it re-defaults to the first category again, and the ComboBox still says "All Categories" — so the UI and the underlying filter disagree from the moment a customer is picked.

That's why your screenshot shows only Cold Brew products. Fix: `TransactionViewModel` should initialize `_selectedCategory = string.Empty` (meaning "all"), and `ReloadProducts()` already handles empty correctly:

```csharp
IEnumerable<Product> products = string.IsNullOrEmpty(SelectedCategory)
    ? _catalogService.GetProducts()
    : _catalogService.GetByCategory(SelectedCategory);
```

So it's a one-line fix in `TransactionViewModel`: `_selectedCategory = string.Empty;` instead of `Categories.FirstOrDefault() ?? string.Empty;`.

## 2. `TransactionView.cs` — drinks header re-layout + font bumps

Replace the entire header-building block in `BuildDrinksArea()`. The key change is that Drinks / "Sort by Category:" / the ComboBox are now **sequenced** (`label.Left = previous.Right + gap`) instead of hardcoded `x` values, so the label can never re-overlap the combo regardless of font or DPI.

```csharp
private Panel BuildDrinksArea()
{
    var area = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Fill, BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary };

    var header = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Top, Height = 100, Padding = new Padding(16, 14, 16, 10) };

    var searchRow = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Top, Height = 34, Margin = new Padding(0, 0, 0, 12) };
    _productSearchTxtBx = new TextBox
    {
        Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
        PlaceholderText = "Search drinks by name",
        Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(10f),
    };
    _productSearchTxtBx.TextChanged += (s, e) =>
    {
        if (_transactionViewModel != null)
            _transactionViewModel.SearchText = _productSearchTxtBx.Text;
    };
    searchRow.Controls.Add(_productSearchTxtBx);

    // Sort row: sequenced left-to-right so the "Sort by Category:" label can't collide
    // with the combo regardless of font/DPI — the previous hardcoded x=90/x=200 pair
    // overlapped because the label rendered wider than the offset assumed.
    var sortRow = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Top, Height = 32 };
    var drinksLabel = new Label
    {
        Text = "Drinks",
        Location = new Point(0, 2),
        AutoSize = true,
        Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(13f),
        ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralText,
    };
    var sortLabel = new Label
    {
        Text = "Sort by Category:",
        AutoSize = true,
        Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9.5f),
        ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralTextMuted,
    };
    _categoryCombo = new ComboBox
    {
        Size = new Size(180, 30),
        DropDownStyle = ComboBoxStyle.DropDownList,
        Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9.5f),
    };
    _categoryCombo.SelectedIndexChanged += (s, e) =>
    {
        if (_transactionViewModel is null || _categoryCombo.SelectedItem is not string category) return;
        _transactionViewModel.SelectedCategory = category == AllCategoriesOption ? string.Empty : category;
    };

    // Sequence: Drinks at x=0, then Sort-label and Combo after it with fixed gaps,
    // vertically centered against the Drinks label's line height.
    sortLabel.Left = drinksLabel.Right + 24;
    sortLabel.Top = drinksLabel.Top + (drinksLabel.Height - sortLabel.Height) / 2 + 2;
    _categoryCombo.Left = sortLabel.Right + 10;
    _categoryCombo.Top = drinksLabel.Top;

    sortRow.Controls.Add(drinksLabel);
    sortRow.Controls.Add(sortLabel);
    sortRow.Controls.Add(_categoryCombo);

    var divider = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Bottom, Height = 1, BackColor = BrandPalette.Border };

    header.Controls.Add(sortRow);
    header.Controls.Add(searchRow);
    header.Controls.Add(divider);

    _productsFlowPanel = new FlowLayoutPanel
    {
        Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
        FlowDirection = FlowDirection.LeftToRight,
        WrapContents = true,
        AutoScroll = true,
        Padding = new Padding(12),
        BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
    };

    area.Controls.Add(_productsFlowPanel);
    area.Controls.Add(header);

    return area;
}
```

Two notes:

- `drinksLabel.Right` and `sortLabel.Right` are only meaningful *after* the labels have a measured size, which `AutoSize = true` gives them immediately on construction (WinForms sizes autosize labels at creation based on their font + text). So the sequencing works without needing a `Resize`/`Load` handler.
- The header grew `92 → 100` to accommodate the larger fonts and the 12px gap under the search box.

Then in the `column.Controls.Add(...)` sequence, replace `_selectPromoBtn` with `_promoCombo`:

### 3c. Repopulate + reflect the promo in `RefreshSummary()`

The combo needs to rebuild its item list every time the cart changes (same cadence the old button used). Add a helper and call it from `RefreshSummary()`:

```csharp
private void RefreshPromoCombo()
{
    if (_transactionViewModel is null)
    {
        _promoCombo.Items.Clear();
        _promoCombo.Enabled = false;
        return;
    }

    // Preserve the current selection (by CampaignId) across a repopulate so editing the
    // cart doesn't visually drop the promo the user already picked — as long as it's
    // still eligible after the change. If it no longer is, selection falls back to the
    // placeholder (index 0), matching the domain: the redeemed CampaignRedeem stays on
    // the order, but the combo stops advertising it as the current choice.
    var currentId = (_promoCombo.SelectedItem as Campaign)?.CampaignId;

    _promoCombo.Items.Clear();
    _promoCombo.Items.Add("Select a Promo");
    foreach (var campaign in _transactionViewModel.EligiblePromos)
        _promoCombo.Items.Add(campaign);

    var restoredIndex = 0;
    if (currentId.HasValue)
    {
        for (int i = 1; i < _promoCombo.Items.Count; i++)
        {
            if (_promoCombo.Items[i] is Campaign c && c.CampaignId == currentId.Value)
            {
                restoredIndex = i;
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    _promoCombo.SelectedIndex = restoredIndex;
    _promoCombo.Enabled = true;
}
```

For the combo to render promo names readably rather than `CRM_Morcaffein.domain.entities.Campaign`, wire a `Format` handler once (in `BuildCustomerColumn()`, right after the combo is built):

```csharp
_promoCombo.Format += (s, e) =>
{
    if (e.ListItem is Campaign campaign)
    {
        e.Value = campaign.DiscountType == "Percentage"
            ? $"{campaign.PromoName} — {campaign.DiscountValue:0.##}% off"
            : $"{campaign.PromoName} — ₱{campaign.DiscountValue:0.##} off";
    }
    else if (e.ListItem is string s)
    {
        e.Value = s; // "Select a Promo" placeholder
    }
};
```

Then in `RefreshSummary()`, the existing `_selectPromoBtn.Enabled = _transactionViewModel != null;` line becomes a call to `RefreshPromoCombo()`, placed at the top:

```csharp
private void RefreshSummary()
{
    RefreshPromoCombo();

    if (_transactionViewModel is null)
    {
        // ... unchanged ...
    }
    // ... unchanged ...
}
```

**One subtlety worth naming:** `RefreshSummary()` is called from `TransactionViewModel_PropertyChanged` on `SubTotal`/`TotalDiscount`/`TotalAmount`, and those fire from `RefreshAfterCartChange()` — which also calls `ReloadPromos()` on the VM. So `EligiblePromos` is already rebuilt before `RefreshSummary` runs. The combo rebuild therefore sees fresh data. Good.

**Second subtlety:** `_promoCombo.SelectedIndexChanged` fires when we programmatically set `SelectedIndex` inside `RefreshPromoCombo()`. When that happens with a *restored* campaign, it calls `ApplyPromoCommand.Execute(campaign)` a second time — which would double-apply the discount (two `CampaignRedeem` rows for the same campaign). I'm guarding against that with a re-entrancy flag; the combo code above needs this addition:

```csharp
private bool _suppressPromoApply;
```

...and in the `SelectedIndexChanged` handler:

```csharp
if (_suppressPromoApply) return;
```

...and around the `SelectedIndex = restoredIndex;` line:

```csharp
_suppressPromoApply = true;
_promoCombo.SelectedIndex = restoredIndex;
_suppressPromoApply = false;
```

Without this, every cart edit re-fires the applied promo and you'd see the Discount line grow.

```csharp
};
```

...and change the add order. **Dock.Right stacks in reverse add-order** (last added ends up outermost/rightmost), so to land as `[name ……] [price] [stepper] [✕]` left-to-right, the add sequence must be `price` → `stepper` → `remove` (so remove ends rightmost, stepper just left of it, price just left of that):

```csharp
Controls.Add(nameLabel);   // Fill — added first
Controls.Add(priceLabel);  // Right — added second → sits left of stepper
Controls.Add(stepper);     // Right — added third → sits right of price
Controls.Add(removeBtn);   // Right — added last  → outermost right
```

(That's the same reverse-add rule already documented for `stepper`/`removeBtn` in this file — I'm just extending it with one more Right-docked sibling.)

## 3. No spacing between the stepper cluster and the ✕ delete button

Confirmed — and the cause is the same Dock-stacking rule. `stepper` and `removeBtn` are both `Dock.Right`, and docked siblings have **no implicit gap**; WinForms packs them flush against each other. There's no `Margin` being honored between two Right-docked controls in the same parent.

Fix: give the stepper cluster a right-side margin that reads as a gap. Since `FlowLayoutPanel` honors its own `Margin` when docked, set:

```csharp
var stepper = new FlowLayoutPanel
{
    Dock = DockStyle.Right,
    Width = 104,
    Margin = new Padding(0, 0, 10, 0),   // ← the gap before the ✕
    FlowDirection = FlowDirection.LeftToRight,
    WrapContents = false,
    Padding = new Padding(0, 6, 0, 6),
};
```

Alternatively (and more robustly), instead of relying on Margin between two Right-docked controls — which WinForms honors inconsistently for edge-docked siblings — wrap the stepper + ✕ in a single right-docked container with internal padding. But given how the rest of this file already leans on docked siblings and their margins, I'll go with the `Margin` approach first and flag it: **if after rendering the gap still isn't there, the fallback is a small right-docked spacer panel between `stepper` and `removeBtn`.** I don't want to over-engineer it before seeing whether Margin works here.

Actually — to save a round-trip, let me just do the reliable version now:

```csharp
// Right-docked cluster: [stepper][10px gap][✕], as ONE unit, so the gap is owned by a
// single parent (Padding) instead of being a Margin between two docked siblings.
var rightCluster = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Right, Width = 104 + 10 + 28, BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary };

var stepper = new FlowLayoutPanel
{
    Dock = DockStyle.Left,
    Width = 104,
    FlowDirection = FlowDirection.LeftToRight,
    WrapContents = false,
    Padding = new Padding(0, 6, 0, 6),
};

var removeBtn = new Button { /* ... Dock = DockStyle.Right, Width = 28 ... */ };

rightCluster.Controls.Add(stepper);       // Fill/Left — added first
rightCluster.Controls.Add(removeBtn);     // Right — added second, outermost right

Controls.Add(nameLabel);      // Fill
Controls.Add(priceLabel);     // Right
Controls.Add(rightCluster);   // Right (outermost) — replaces the separate stepper + removeBtn adds
```

The 10px gap is now the unused middle of `rightCluster` (stepper left-docked at width 104, ✕ right-docked at 28, cluster 142 wide → ~10px of empty space between them). That's guaranteed to render regardless of how WinForms treats sibling margins. `removeBtn` no longer needs `Dock.Right` relative to the outer line — it's inside the cluster now.

I'd recommend **this** version, but I've left the simpler `Margin`-only version above too so you can pick whichever you'd rather carry forward.

## 4. Select Promo is spammable / doesn't work as intended

Confirmed, and there are two distinct problems:

**4a. The re-entrancy flag I described doesn't actually prevent the double-apply in the case you're hitting.** Here's the real sequence when a user picks a promo:

1. User selects item → `SelectedIndexChanged` fires → `ApplyPromoCommand.Execute(campaign)` → `ApplyPromo` on the VM → `RefreshAfterCartChange()` → `ReloadPromos()` → `EligiblePromos` rebuilt → `RefreshSummary()` → `RefreshPromoCombo()` → clears and re-adds items → sets `SelectedIndex` back to the restored campaign.
2. That *second* `SelectedIndex` assignment fires `SelectedIndexChanged` again.
3. `_suppressPromoApply` guard catches it... **but only if the flag is still `true` at that moment.** The flag is set/reset synchronously around the assignment in `RefreshPromoCombo()`, which is correct — except `ApplyPromo` (step 1) already ran `RefreshAfterCartChange()` *before* we ever got to `RefreshPromoCombo` in the same call stack, so the flag wasn't set during step 1's cascade. The guard protects against the *inner* re-fire (step 2), which is what it was designed for — but if `ApplyPromo` is called again from any path that doesn't go through `RefreshPromoCombo`'s guarded assignment, it re-fires.

The bigger issue: **`ApplyPromo` can be invoked repeatedly for the same campaign**, each time adding a new `CampaignRedeem` row via `Order.ApplyPromo`. The domain doesn't guard against applying the same campaign twice to the same order — `order.ApplyPromo(campaign)` unconditionally does `CampaignRedeems.Add(new CampaignRedeem(...))`. So "spammable" is really "the domain permits duplicate redemption on one order."

**Two ways to fix it, and I need you to pick:**

- **(i) UI-level guard:** in the combo's `SelectedIndexChanged`, skip the `ApplyPromoCommand.Execute` if the selected campaign is already among the order's current `CampaignRedeems` (i.e. already applied). Simple, no domain change. But it means an order can never legitimately have the same campaign applied twice — which is almost certainly what you want, so this is my recommendation.
- **(ii) Domain-level guard:** `Order.ApplyPromo` should throw (or no-op) if the campaign is already in `CampaignRedeems`. More correct long-term, but it's a domain change outside the scope of "UI polish" and it ripples into tests/other callers.

I'd do **(i)** now and note **(ii)** as a domain fix for when we do the DB-connection work. Confirm and I'll bake (i) into the combo handler.

**4b. Bigger combo + more consistent design.** Bump the combo to `Height = 36`, `Font = 9.5f`, and match the customer search textbox's visual weight so the left column reads as one consistent column of input controls. I'll also drop the `FlatStyle` (WinForms ComboBox doesn't visually honor `Flat` on Windows anyway — it just falls back to the standard look, which is what you're seeing), and set the same border styling the textbox uses.

## 6. Category dropdown still not separated from "Sort by Category:"

Confirmed — my sequencing used `sortLabel.Right + 10`, but `AutoSize` labels report their `Right` based on the *design-time* size, which can be stale until the control is actually laid out. The 10px gap collapsed to 0 in practice.

Fix: don't trust `AutoSize`-label `Right` at construction time. Either (a) force a layout pass with `sortLabel.PerformLayout()` before reading `.Right`, or (b) use `TextRenderer.MeasureText(sortLabel.Text, sortLabel.Font).Width` to compute the gap explicitly. I'll do **(b)** — it's deterministic and DPI-independent:

```csharp
var sortLabelWidth = TextRenderer.MeasureText(sortLabel.Text, sortLabel.Font).Width;
_categoryCombo.Left = drinksLabel.Right + 24 + sortLabelWidth + 14;
```

(14px gap this time, not 10 — 10 was too tight and 14 reads as an intentional separator.)

You're talking about `tableCardPanel` — the big box in `BuildLayout()`:

## #4a — UI-level duplicate-promo guard

In `_promoCombo.SelectedIndexChanged`:

```csharp
_promoCombo.SelectedIndexChanged += (s, e) =>
{
    if (_transactionViewModel is null) return;
    if (_suppressPromoApply) return;

    if (_promoCombo.SelectedIndex <= 0)
        return;

    if (_promoCombo.SelectedItem is not Campaign campaign)
        return;

    // UI-level guard: the domain permits the same campaign to be applied to one order
    // more than once (Order.ApplyPromo unconditionally adds a CampaignRedeem row), so
    // without this, re-picking the same promo double-applies the discount. A proper
    // domain-level guard is deferred to the DB-connection work.
    var alreadyApplied = _transactionViewModel.Order.CampaignRedeems
        .Any(r => r.CampaignId == campaign.CampaignId);
    if (alreadyApplied)
        return;

    _transactionViewModel.ApplyPromoCommand.Execute(campaign);
};
```

Note this checks `Order.CampaignRedeems` (the actual redeemed set), not `EligiblePromos` — because `EligiblePromos` is a *candidacy* list and a campaign that's already been redeemed on this order can still appear in it. `CampaignRedeems` is the truth of "already applied."

**Also worth noting:** `RefreshPromoCombo()`'s restore-by-`CampaignId` and the `_suppressPromoApply` flag both still matter — the flag handles the *programmatic* re-selection case, this new check handles the *user-re-selection* case. Two different re-entrancy vectors.

## CartLineControl — the clean version

You said "adjust this based on because im kinda lost" — fair, the batch above left a half-applied state (the `rightCluster` was created but never wired up; `stepper` still had the stale `Margin`; the old `Controls.Add` sequence is what actually ran). Here's the whole file, fully consistent, no leftover half-edits:

```csharp
using CRM_Morcaffein.domain.entities;
using CRM_Morcaffein.Theme;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.winforms.Views.Controls
{
    /// <summary>
    /// One row in the Order box: "Drink Name (Size) +Mods … ₱SubTotal [- 2x +] ✕" — a compact
    /// inline quantity stepper instead of a data-grid row, matching a modern POS's order list
    /// rather than the boxed-table convention the rest of the app uses (this is the one
    /// deliberate exception, per the POS-specific redesign).
    /// </summary>
    public class CartLineControl : Panel
    {
        public OrderItem Item { get; }

        public event EventHandler? QuantityIncreased;
        public event EventHandler? QuantityDecreased;
        public event EventHandler? RemoveClicked;

        public CartLineControl(OrderItem item)
        {
            Item = item;

            // Deliberately NOT Dock=Top: this control lives inside a FlowLayoutPanel
            // (TopDown), which positions children itself — a Dock value on a flowed child
            // fights the flow layout and was why cart lines weren't rendering at all.
            Height = 44;
            Margin = new Padding(0, 0, 0, 3);
            BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary;

            var modifiersSuffix = item.OrderItemModifiers.Count == 0
                ? string.Empty
                : $" +{string.Join(",", item.OrderItemModifiers.Select(m => m.ProductModifierNameSnapshot))}";

            var nameLabel = new Label
            {
                Text = $"{item.Product?.ProductName ?? "—"} ({item.SizeNameSnapshot}){modifiersSuffix}",
                Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                AutoEllipsis = true,
                TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleLeft,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9.5f),
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralText,
            };

            var priceLabel = new Label
            {
                Text = $"₱{item.SubTotal:0.00}",
                Dock = DockStyle.Right,
                Width = 76,
                TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleRight,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(9.5f),
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralText,
            };

            // Right side is one container so the gap between the stepper cluster and the ✕
            // is owned by a single parent (real empty space inside rightCluster) rather than
            // being a Margin between two sibling Dock=Right controls — WinForms packs docked
            // siblings flush and honors those margins inconsistently, which is why the ✕ was
            // touching the stepper.
            var rightCluster = new Panel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Right,
                Width = 30 + 34 + 30 /* stepper buttons + qty label */ + 10 /* gap */ + 28 /* remove */,
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
            };

            var stepper = new FlowLayoutPanel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Left,
                Width = 30 + 34 + 30,
                FlowDirection = FlowDirection.LeftToRight,
                WrapContents = false,
                Padding = new Padding(0, 7, 0, 7),
            };

            var removeBtn = new Button
            {
                Text = "✕",
                Dock = DockStyle.Right,
                Width = 28,
                FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat,
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralTextMuted,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9f),
                Cursor = Cursors.Hand,
            };
            removeBtn.FlatAppearance.BorderSize = 0;
            removeBtn.Click += (s, e) => RemoveClicked?.Invoke(this, EventArgs.Empty);

            var minusBtn = MakeStepperButton("-");
            minusBtn.Click += (s, e) => QuantityDecreased?.Invoke(this, EventArgs.Empty);

            var qtyLabel = new Label
            {
                Text = $"{item.Quantity}x",
                Width = 34,
                Height = 30,
                TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleCenter,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(10f),
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralText,
            };

            var plusBtn = MakeStepperButton("+");
            plusBtn.Click += (s, e) => QuantityIncreased?.Invoke(this, EventArgs.Empty);

            stepper.Controls.Add(minusBtn);
            stepper.Controls.Add(qtyLabel);
            stepper.Controls.Add(plusBtn);

            // Inside rightCluster: stepper docked Left (added first), removeBtn docked Right
            // (added after) — so they sit at opposite edges of the cluster with the gap in
            // the middle. No Margin games needed.
            rightCluster.Controls.Add(stepper);
            rightCluster.Controls.Add(removeBtn);

            // On the line itself: nameLabel fills, then priceLabel and rightCluster are both
            // Dock=Right and stack in reverse add-order — priceLabel added first ends up just
            // left of rightCluster; rightCluster added last lands outermost right.
            Controls.Add(nameLabel);
            Controls.Add(priceLabel);
            Controls.Add(rightCluster);
        }

        private static Button MakeStepperButton(string text) => new()
        {
            Text = text,
            Width = 30,
            Height = 30,
            FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat,
            BackColor = BrandPalette.ButtonSecondaryFill,
            ForeColor = BrandPalette.ButtonSecondaryText,
            Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(10f),
            Cursor = Cursors.Hand,
        };
    }
}
```

**Layout it produces, left to right:**

```text
[ name (size) +mods ........................ ] [ ₱SubTotal ] [ - 2x + ] [gap] [ ✕ ]
```

- `nameLabel` — Fill, ellipsizes if the name is long
- `priceLabel` — Right, 76px
- `rightCluster` — Right, 142px total: stepper (Left, 94px) + 10px empty middle + removeBtn (Right, 28px) = 132px + 10px gap = 142px

**Why the width math looks redundant (`30+34+30`):** it's written out so the number is self-documenting when a future change touches button sizes — if `MakeStepperButton` ever changes width, the cluster width is visibly wrong instead of silently wrong.

**One thing to double-check visually:** the `qtyLabel` is 30px tall inside a FlowLayoutPanel with `Padding = (0,7,0,7)` — that gives 30 + 14 = 44px of content height, matching the row height exactly. So the stepper buttons and qty text should be vertically centered. If they look top-heavy, the fix is adjusting that Padding's top/bottom to `6/8` or similar.

## #2 — Drinks header still overlapping

The screenshot shows the ComboBox starting *before* the "Sort by Category:" label ends — the label's "y:" is cut off by the combo's left edge. My last fix used `TextRenderer.MeasureText` to compute the offset, but there's a bug in my own snippet: I wrote it as

```csharp
_categoryCombo.Left = drinksLabel.Right + 24 + sortLabelWidth + 14;
```

...but this runs **before** `sortLabel` is added to `sortRow` and thus before it's laid out, so `sortLabel.Right` — wait, no, I used `drinksLabel.Right`, not `sortLabel.Right`. And `drinksLabel.Right` is also 0 until layout runs, because `AutoSize` sizing only happens once the control is parented.

That's the actual bug in my last snippet. `drinksLabel.Right` is 0 at the moment I read it (before `sortRow.Controls.Add(drinksLabel)` runs), so `_categoryCombo.Left` collapses to roughly `sortLabelWidth + 38` — which lands *inside* the label.

**The fix:** compute all widths via `TextRenderer.MeasureText` and position *everything* by explicit `Left` — never trust `.Right` before layout:

```csharp
var drinksWidth = TextRenderer.MeasureText(drinksLabel.Text, drinksLabel.Font).Width;
var sortLabelWidth = TextRenderer.MeasureText(sortLabel.Text, sortLabel.Font).Width;

drinksLabel.Left = 0;
sortLabel.Left = drinksWidth + 24;
_categoryCombo.Left = drinksWidth + 24 + sortLabelWidth + 14;
```

This is deterministic and layout-order-independent. I should have written it that way the first time — that's on me.

## #3 — Customer search row: "Go" button and textbox don't align

Screenshot shows: textbox has a blue underline (the WinForms focus/accent), the "Go" button is a separate square sitting flush right but its top edge is 2–3px above the textbox's top edge. Cause: in `BuildCustomerColumn()`,

```csharp
var searchRow = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Top, Height = 30 };
_customerSearchTxtBx = new TextBox { Dock = DockStyle.Fill, ... };
var searchBtn = new Button { Width = 36, Dock = DockStyle.Right, ... };
```

`TextBox` with `Dock.Fill` will stretch to the row's 30px height, but a WinForms `TextBox` has a fixed *preferred* height (`~23px` at 9f) and doesn't visually fill 30px — so it sits centered-ish but not quite. The `Button` with `Dock.Right` *does* stretch to 30px, and its caption centers in that 30px, so the two baselines drift.

**Fix:** give the row a fixed height that matches the textbox's natural height (26px at 9.5f font), and use `Dock.Fill` for the button too so both controls are exactly the same height. Or simpler: don't `Dock.Fill` the textbox — set explicit `Height = 26` and center everything in a 30px row. I'll do the former (both fill a 26px row) since it's fewer moving parts:

```csharp
var searchRow = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Top, Height = 28 };
_customerSearchTxtBx = new TextBox { Dock = DockStyle.Fill, Font = ..., BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle };
var searchBtn = new Button { Width = 40, Dock = DockStyle.Right, ... };
```

`FixedSingle` on the textbox also gets rid of the blue underline (that's the default `Fixed3D`'s focus rendering). One caveat: `FixedSingle` is a slightly different look than the default; if it reads inconsistent with the other textboxes in the app, I'll switch to removing the accent another way. Try it.

## #4 — Changing customer should reset the whole screen

This is a real behavior bug, confirmed by your description: `TransactionViewModel.SwitchCustomer()` calls `LinkCustomerToOrder(Order, newCustomer)`, which (as documented in the mock) re-points `CustomerId`/`Customer` on the *existing* Order — cart items survive. That's intentional per the original plan ("Quick Register flow preserves cart state"), but it's the wrong call now that the POS flow is "search customer → build cart → log sale → search next customer." You want the search-and-go to be a **fresh transaction**, not a relink.

Two possible fixes:

**(a) UI-level:** in `RunCustomerSearch()`, if a `TransactionViewModel` already exists, dispose/null it and create a new one instead of calling `SwitchCustomer`. This is contained to `TransactionView`.

**(b) Domain-level:** change the semantics of `SwitchCustomer` to reset the cart. That means `LinkCustomerToOrder` becomes "restart order for this customer" — but it's still named and documented as a relink, which would then lie.

**I recommend (a)** — it's the actual intended behavior ("new search = new sale") and doesn't touch the domain's `LinkCustomerToOrder`, which the Quick Register flow may still want. Concretely:

```csharp
private void SelectCustomer(Customer customer)
{
    var employeeId = EmployeeSession.Current?.EmployeeId
        ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("No employee session — the Transaction view requires a logged-in employee.");

    // Search-and-Go = start a fresh transaction. Any prior in-progress order is abandoned
    // (nothing is persisted until CompleteOrder), so we just drop the old VM and its cart
    // entirely instead of relinking — relinking preserved the previous customer's items,
    // which is wrong for the POS flow (each search is a new sale).
    _transactionViewModel = new TransactionViewModel(_orderService, _catalogService, customer, employeeId);
    _transactionViewModel.SaleCompleted += (s, e) => OnSaleCompleted();
    _transactionViewModel.OperationFailed += (s, message) => ShowCartStatus(message);
    _transactionViewModel.PropertyChanged += TransactionViewModel_PropertyChanged;
    _transactionViewModel.VisibleProducts.ListChanged += (s, e) => RefreshProductsPanel();
    _transactionViewModel.CartItems.ListChanged += (s, e) => RefreshCartLines();

    RefreshProductsPanel();
    RefreshCartLines();
    RefreshSummary();
}
```

And delete the `else { _transactionViewModel.SwitchCustomer(customer); }` branch. **`SwitchCustomer` stays on the VM** (harmless, documented, may be used by Quick Register later) — it's just not called from here anymore.

**Side effect worth flagging:** if a staff member is mid-cart and accidentally searches a different customer, they lose the cart with no warning. That's what "reset on new search" means. If you'd prefer a confirm-prompt when there are already items in the cart, say so — that's a small addition on top.

Agreed, that's the cleanest fix. Change: remove `BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle` from `tableCardPanel` (done in the last batch), and instead give the Order box a **uniform inset** from the card's edges so it's not flush against them. Currently `BuildOrderBox` has `Margin = new Padding(10, 10, 10, 10)` but `Dock.Fill` inside a `Dock.Right` column ignores the margin for the fill direction (the margin only shows on edges adjacent to non-docked space). Since the right column itself has no padding, the Order box's right edge touches the card's right edge.

**Fix:** add `Padding` to the right column panel itself:

```csharp
var column = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Right, Width = 380, BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary, Padding = new Padding(10, 10, 10, 10) };
```

Then Order (Fill), Payables (Bottom), Log Sale (Bottom) all get 10px inset on all sides from the column's edges. The Order box's own `Margin` can then go to `(0, 0, 0, 10)` — just the gap between it and Payables below it. Payables `Margin = (0, 0, 0, 10)`, Log Sale `Margin = (0, 0, 0, 0)`. All internal spacing owned by the column padding, all inter-box gaps owned by each box's bottom margin.

Since the right column is now padded, its effective content width is `380 - 20 = 360` — same visual room as before but with a clean border-free right edge.

```csharp
private Panel BuildCustomerColumn()
{
    var column = new Panel
    {
        Dock = DockStyle.Left,
        Width = 220,
        BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfaceCard,
        Padding = new Padding(12),
    };

    // ----- Promo picker (ComboBox) — docked to the bottom of the column -----
    _promoCombo = new ComboBox
    {
        Dock = DockStyle.Bottom,
        Height = 36,
        DropDownStyle = ComboBoxStyle.DropDownList,
        Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9.5f),
        BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
        ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralText,
        Enabled = false,
    };
    _promoCombo.Format += (s, e) =>
    {
        if (e.ListItem is Campaign campaign)
        {
            e.Value = campaign.DiscountType == "Percentage"
                ? $"{campaign.PromoName} — {campaign.DiscountValue:0.##}% off"
                : $"{campaign.PromoName} — ₱{campaign.DiscountValue:0.##} off";
        }
        else if (e.ListItem is string s)
        {
            e.Value = s;
        }
    };
    _promoCombo.SelectedIndexChanged += (s, e) =>
    {
        if (_transactionViewModel is null) return;
        if (_suppressPromoApply) return;
        if (_promoCombo.SelectedIndex <= 0) return;
        if (_promoCombo.SelectedItem is not Campaign campaign) return;

        // UI-level guard: Order.ApplyPromo doesn't check for duplicates, so re-picking the
        // same promo would double-apply. CampaignRedeems (not EligiblePromos) is the truth
        // of what's already been applied to this order.
        var alreadyApplied = _transactionViewModel.Order.CampaignRedeems
            .Any(r => r.CampaignId == campaign.CampaignId);
        if (alreadyApplied) return;

        _transactionViewModel.ApplyPromoCommand.Execute(campaign);
    };

    // ----- Search row: textbox fills, Go button docked right, both 26px tall -----
    // The row is 28px with 1px top/bottom breathing room; the textbox and button are
    // BOTH left at their natural heights (26) so their baselines line up. Previously the
    // textbox Dock.Filled a 30px row while the button also stretched to 30px, but the
    // textbox's own preferred height is ~23-26px, so they didn't actually match.
    var searchRow = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Top, Height = 28 };

    var searchBtn = new Button
    {
        Text = "Go",
        Width = 40,
        Dock = DockStyle.Right,
        FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat,

        ForeColor = BrandPalette.ButtonSecondaryText,
        Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(8.5f),
        Cursor = Cursors.Hand,
    };
    searchBtn.FlatAppearance.BorderSize = 0;
    searchBtn.Click += (s, e) => RunCustomerSearch();

    _customerSearchTxtBx = new TextBox
    {
        Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
        PlaceholderText = "Customer ID or phone",
        Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9f),
        BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle,   // kills the default blue focus underline
    };
    _customerSearchTxtBx.KeyDown += (s, e) =>
    {
        if (e.KeyCode == Keys.Enter) { RunCustomerSearch(); e.SuppressKeyPress = true; }
    };

    searchRow.Controls.Add(_customerSearchTxtBx);
    searchRow.Controls.Add(searchBtn);

    _customerSearchErrorLabel = new Label
    {
        Dock = DockStyle.Top,
        Height = 32,
        Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(8f),
        ForeColor = BrandPalette.StatusNegativeFill,
    };

    // ----- Customer profile panel (shown once a search succeeds) -----
    _customerProfilePanel = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Top, Height = 72, Visible = false };
    _customerProfileNameLabel = new Label
    {
        Dock = DockStyle.Top,
        Height = 22,
        Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(11f),
        ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralText,
    };
    _customerProfileDetailLabel = new Label
    {
        Dock = DockStyle.Top,
        Height = 44,
        Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(8.5f),
        ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralTextMuted,
    };
    _customerProfilePanel.Controls.Add(_customerProfileDetailLabel);
    _customerProfilePanel.Controls.Add(_customerProfileNameLabel);

    // Reverse add-order for Top-docked siblings: last added is topmost, so add profile

    column.Controls.Add(_customerProfilePanel);
```

## 2. `BuildDrinksArea()` — header alignment done right

Replace the **entire method**. The key fix: compute each label's width with `TextRenderer.MeasureText` and position **everything** by explicit `Left`, never reading `.Right` (which is 0 before layout runs — that was the bug in my last snippet).

```csharp
private Panel BuildDrinksArea()
{
    var area = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Fill, BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary };

    var header = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Top, Height = 100, Padding = new Padding(16, 14, 16, 10) };

    // ----- Search row -----
    var searchRow = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Top, Height = 34, Margin = new Padding(0, 0, 0, 12) };
    _productSearchTxtBx = new TextBox
    {
        Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
        PlaceholderText = "Search drinks by name",
        Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(10f),
        BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle,
    };
    _productSearchTxtBx.TextChanged += (s, e) =>
    {
        if (_transactionViewModel != null)
            _transactionViewModel.SearchText = _productSearchTxtBx.Text;
    };
    searchRow.Controls.Add(_productSearchTxtBx);

    // ----- Sort row -----
    var sortRow = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Top, Height = 34 };

    var drinksLabel = new Label
    {
        Text = "Drinks",
        AutoSize = true,
        Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(13f),
        ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralText,
    };
    var sortLabel = new Label
    {
        Text = "Sort by Category:",
        AutoSize = true,
        Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9.5f),
        ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralTextMuted,
    };
    _categoryCombo = new ComboBox
    {
        Size = new Size(180, 30),
        DropDownStyle = ComboBoxStyle.DropDownList,
        Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9.5f),
    };
    _categoryCombo.SelectedIndexChanged += (s, e) =>
    {
        if (_transactionViewModel is null || _categoryCombo.SelectedItem is not string category) return;
        _transactionViewModel.SelectedCategory = category == AllCategoriesOption ? string.Empty : category;
    };

    // Measure both labels explicitly — AutoSize labels report Right=0 until parented,
    // which is why the previous offset-based positioning collapsed the gap. Both Left
    // values are computed from measured widths, so the combo can never overlap the label.
    var drinksWidth = TextRenderer.MeasureText(drinksLabel.Text, drinksLabel.Font).Width;
    var sortLabelWidth = TextRenderer.MeasureText(sortLabel.Text, sortLabel.Font).Width;

    drinksLabel.Left = 0;
    drinksLabel.Top = 0;

    sortLabel.Left = drinksWidth + 24;
    sortLabel.Top = (sortRow.Height - sortLabel.Height) / 2 + 2;

    _categoryCombo.Left = drinksWidth + 24 + sortLabelWidth + 14;
    _categoryCombo.Top = (sortRow.Height - _categoryCombo.Height) / 2;

    sortRow.Controls.Add(drinksLabel);
    sortRow.Controls.Add(sortLabel);
    sortRow.Controls.Add(_categoryCombo);

    var divider = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Bottom, Height = 1, BackColor = BrandPalette.Border };

    header.Controls.Add(sortRow);
    header.Controls.Add(searchRow);
    header.Controls.Add(divider);

    _productsFlowPanel = new FlowLayoutPanel
    {
        Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
        FlowDirection = FlowDirection.LeftToRight,
        WrapContents = true,
        AutoScroll = true,
        Padding = new Padding(12),
        BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
    };

    area.Controls.Add(_productsFlowPanel);
    area.Controls.Add(header);

    return area;
}
```

## 3. `BuildOrderColumn()` — right column with padding, Order box inset

Replace the **entire method**. This is where your "margin the Order list so it doesn't touch the outer border" fix lives.

```csharp
private Panel BuildOrderColumn()
{
    // Padding on the column itself insets ALL three child boxes (Order, Payables, Log Sale)
    // uniformly from the card's edges. Previously the column had no padding, so the Order
    // box's own Margin was ignored for the fill direction and its right edge touched the
    // card edge — which read as a doubled/thick border where Order's border met the card's.
    var column = new Panel
    {
        Dock = DockStyle.Right,
        Width = 380,
        BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
        Padding = new Padding(10, 10, 10, 10),
    };

    var orderBox = BuildOrderBox();
    var payablesBox = BuildPayablesBox();
    var logSaleBox = BuildLogSaleBox();

    // Bottom-docked siblings stack like Top ones (last added is outermost), so LogSale
    // added last lands at the very bottom, Payables above it, and the Fill (Order) takes
    // whatever's left.
    column.Controls.Add(orderBox);
    column.Controls.Add(payablesBox);
    column.Controls.Add(logSaleBox);

    return column;
}
```

And replace `BuildOrderBox()` so its margin is just the gap to Payables (the column padding handles the outer edges now):

## 4. `SelectCustomer()` — always-new-VM + confirm-if-cart-non-empty

Replace the **entire method**:

```csharp
private void SelectCustomer(Customer customer)
{
    var employeeId = EmployeeSession.Current?.EmployeeId
        ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("No employee session — the Transaction view requires a logged-in employee.");

    // Search-and-Go = start a fresh transaction. If the existing cart has items, confirm
    // first — a staff member mid-sale who mistypes a customer ID shouldn't lose their work
    // silently. Empty carts (or no VM yet) just get replaced without asking.
    if (_transactionViewModel is not null && _transactionViewModel.CartItems.Count > 0)
    {
        var currentCustomerName = _transactionViewModel.Customer.FullName;
        var confirm = MessageBox.Show(
            FindForm(),
            $"Discard the in-progress order for {currentCustomerName} and start a new one for {customer.FullName}?",
            "Start New Transaction",
            MessageBoxButtons.YesNo,
            MessageBoxIcon.Warning);

        if (confirm != DialogResult.Yes)
        {
            // Restore the search box to reflect the customer that's actually loaded, so the
            // UI doesn't lie about which customer the running cart belongs to.
            _customerSearchTxtBx.Text = _transactionViewModel.Customer.CustomerId.ToString();
            return;
        }
    }

    _transactionViewModel = new TransactionViewModel(_orderService, _catalogService, customer, employeeId);
    _transactionViewModel.SaleCompleted += (s, e) => OnSaleCompleted();
    _transactionViewModel.OperationFailed += (s, message) => ShowCartStatus(message);
    _transactionViewModel.PropertyChanged += TransactionViewModel_PropertyChanged;
    _transactionViewModel.VisibleProducts.ListChanged += (s, e) => RefreshProductsPanel();
    _transactionViewModel.CartItems.ListChanged += (s, e) => RefreshCartLines();

    RefreshProductsPanel();
    RefreshCartLines();
    RefreshSummary();
}
```

**Two things this does that the old one didn't:**

- Never calls `SwitchCustomer` — each search = new VM = new `Order`, so the cart doesn't carry over (that's the bug you found).
- Confirms before discarding a non-empty cart, and if you say "No", **restores the search box text** to the currently-loaded customer's ID so the UI stays consistent with reality.

**`SwitchCustomer` stays on `TransactionViewModel`** — it's not called from here anymore, but it's not dead code you need to delete; it's documented for the Quick Register relink flow.

## 6. `_suppressPromoApply` field + `RefreshPromoCombo()`

And add the `RefreshPromoCombo()` method — placed anywhere in the class, I'd put it right after `ShowPromoMenu()` used to be:

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Rebuilds the promo combo's item list from the current EligiblePromos. Preserves the
/// current selection by CampaignId across a rebuild so editing the cart doesn't visually
/// drop the promo the user picked — unless it's no longer eligible, in which case selection
/// falls back to the placeholder. (The redeemed CampaignRedeem stays on the order either way.)
/// </summary>
private void RefreshPromoCombo()
{
    if (_transactionViewModel is null)
    {
        _promoCombo.Items.Clear();
        _promoCombo.Enabled = false;
        return;
    }

    var currentId = (_promoCombo.SelectedItem as Campaign)?.CampaignId;

    _suppressPromoApply = true;
    _promoCombo.Items.Clear();
    _promoCombo.Items.Add("Select a Promo");
    foreach (var campaign in _transactionViewModel.EligiblePromos)
        _promoCombo.Items.Add(campaign);

    var restoredIndex = 0;
    if (currentId.HasValue)
    {
        for (int i = 1; i < _promoCombo.Items.Count; i++)
        {
            if (_promoCombo.Items[i] is Campaign c && c.CampaignId == currentId.Value)
            {
                restoredIndex = i;
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    _promoCombo.SelectedIndex = restoredIndex;
    _suppressPromoApply = false;

    _promoCombo.Enabled = true;
}
```

And in `RefreshSummary()`, replace the old `_selectPromoBtn.Enabled = _transactionViewModel != null;` line with `RefreshPromoCombo();` at the top:

```csharp
{
    RefreshPromoCombo();

    if (_transactionViewModel is null)
    {
        // ... rest unchanged ...
    }
    // ... rest unchanged ...
}
```

Ha — yeah, that's a real error, and it's my fault for not catching it. `string` is a reference type, so the pattern `is string s` *should* compile... except the compiler is complaining because `e.ListItem` is `object` and the C# compiler can't prove the pattern is reachable in a way that satisfies its nullability analysis in this context — actually, more precisely:

**The real reason it errors:** `ListControlConvertEventArgs.ListItem` is typed `object`, and `is string s` is a perfectly valid pattern... so if it's erroring, the actual issue is almost certainly that you already handled the string case implicitly — `e.Value` starts as `e.ListItem`, so the "else" case (placeholder string) doesn't need handling at all. The `is string s { e.Value = s; }` branch is a no-op: the framework already sets `e.Value = e.ListItem` before the `Format` handler runs. So the whole `else if` is redundant, and depending on your compiler/analyzer settings, it's being flagged (or the `s` variable being unused is triggering something).

**Fix: delete the `else if` branch entirely.** The `Format` handler only needs to do work for the `Campaign` case; the placeholder string falls through and `e.Value` stays as-is.

```csharp
_promoCombo.Format += (s, e) =>
{
    if (e.ListItem is Campaign campaign)
    {
        e.Value = campaign.DiscountType == "Percentage"
            ? $"{campaign.PromoName} — {campaign.DiscountValue:0.##}% off"
            : $"{campaign.PromoName} — ₱{campaign.DiscountValue:0.##} off";
    }
    // The "Select a Promo" placeholder is a plain string; Format's default already sets
    // e.Value = e.ListItem, so no branch is needed for it.
};
```

If for some reason that *still* errors (which would surprise me), tell me the exact compiler message and line — but I'm fairly confident this was just the redundant no-op branch tripping an analyzer or your IDE's "unused pattern variable" warning being escalated to an error.

Also worth noting since I'm here: the lambda's first parameter `s` shadows nothing important, but if you ever rename the outer variable `s` it'll collide — no action needed, just something to be aware of when reading it.

Apply that and the rest of the batch should compile.

## #2 — Promo combo shows `CRM_Morcaffein.domain.entities.Campaign`

The `Format` handler isn't firing (or isn't wired). Two possibilities:

**(a) The `Format` handler wasn't attached**, or was attached with the `is string s` branch still in it and you removed the *whole* handler instead of just that branch. The handler is what converts the `Campaign` object into a display string — without it, `ComboBox` calls `.ToString()` on the object, which is exactly `CRM_Morcaffein.domain.entities.Campaign` as shown.

**(b) The handler is attached but `e.ListItem` isn't a `Campaign`** — which would happen if you're adding the *combo items* as something other than `Campaign` instances. In `RefreshPromoCombo()` I add `foreach (var campaign in _transactionViewModel.EligiblePromos) _promoCombo.Items.Add(campaign);` — so each item *is* a `Campaign`. But if the currently-loaded file adds them differently (e.g. `.Select(c => c.PromoName)`), the handler wouldn't match.

**Most likely (a).** Verify that the `_promoCombo.Format += ...` block is present in `BuildCustomerColumn()` **and** that it's the version without the `else if (e.ListItem is string s)` branch. If the handler is missing entirely, adding it back fixes the display.

**Alternative fix that sidesteps `Format` entirely** — if `Format` keeps being finicky, use a display wrapper: add `ComboBox.Items.Add()` with a small record that overrides `ToString()`:

```csharp
private sealed record PromoItem(Campaign? Campaign, string Display)
{
    public override string ToString() => Display;
}
```

Then in `RefreshPromoCombo()`:

```csharp

{
    var label = campaign.DiscountType == "Percentage"
        ? $"{campaign.PromoName} — {campaign.DiscountValue:0.##}% off"
```

## #3 — Selecting back to "Select a Promo" doesn't clear the discount

Correct, and this is a **domain-layer limitation**, not a UI one. `Order.ApplyPromo(campaign)` adds a `CampaignRedeem` row to the order. There is **no `Order.RemovePromo()`** method, and no method on `CampaignRedeem` to remove/undo a redemption. So the UI can *display* "Select a Promo" but the `TotalDiscount` on the order still includes every `CampaignRedeem` ever added.

Two ways forward:

**(a) Domain fix (proper):** add `Order.RemovePromo(Campaign campaign)` that removes the matching `CampaignRedeem` and calls `RecalculateTotals()`. Then the UI's "index 0 selected" branch calls it. This is the correct fix — "clear the promo" should be a real domain operation. But it's a domain-layer change (touches `Order.cs`), and you've been keeping domain changes deferred to the DB-connection phase.

**(b) UI workaround (hacky):** since `ApplyPromo` can only be called once per campaign (my duplicate guard), and there's no remove... there's no clean UI workaround. You could rebuild the order from scratch (drop the VM, re-create, re-add all items), which is horrendous.

**My recommendation:** do the domain fix now, since it's small and self-contained:

```csharp
// Order.cs — new method next to ApplyPromo
public void RemovePromo(Campaign campaign)
{
    EnsureOrderIsPending();
    var redeem = CampaignRedeems.FirstOrDefault(r => r.CampaignId == campaign.CampaignId);
    if (redeem is null) return;
    CampaignRedeems.Remove(redeem);
    RecalculateTotals();
}
```

Then in the combo's `SelectedIndexChanged`, the index-0 branch:

```csharp

{

    foreach (var redeem in _transactionViewModel.Order.CampaignRedeems.ToList())
    {
        var campaign = _transactionViewModel.EligiblePromos.FirstOrDefault(c => c.CampaignId == redeem.CampaignId)
                    ?? _catalogService.GetActiveCampaigns().FirstOrDefault(c => c.CampaignId == redeem.CampaignId); // see note
        if (campaign != null)
            _transactionViewModel.Order.RemovePromo(campaign);
    }
    _transactionViewModel.RefreshAfterCartChange(); // need to make this public, or add a service method
    return;
}
```

**But there's a complication:** `TransactionViewModel` doesn't expose a way to trigger `RefreshAfterCartChange()` publicly — it's private. And `Order.RemovePromo` isn't routed through `IOrderService`, which is where all other order mutations go. So the *clean* version is:

1. Add `Order.RemovePromo(Campaign)` to the domain.
2. Add `Order RemovePromo(Order order, Campaign campaign)` to `IOrderService` + `MockOrderService`.
3. Add `void ClearPromos()` (or `RemovePromo(Campaign)`) to `TransactionViewModel`, calling the service and then `RefreshAfterCartChange()`.
4. Combo calls it on index 0.

That's a four-file change. Which means it crosses into the domain/service layer you've been keeping frozen. **So I need your call:**

- **Option A:** Do the proper four-file change now (domain + service + VM + view), get the "clear promo" behavior working correctly.

You've got **both** the `Campaign`-based guard and the `PromoItem`-based guard stacked on top of each other. ## Bug #4 — Cart lines: no, the file on disk IS the version I sent, and it's still wrong

Now that I can see the real file: `CartLineControl.cs` on disk **is** the version I sent. So the rendering problem is *real* and *not* a stale file. Let me diagnose it from what I now know.

The screenshot shows: name wraps to two lines, `-`/`+` different sizes, `✕` far from the cluster, `1x` not centered.

**The name wrapping:** `nameLabel` is `Dock.Fill`. Its siblings `priceLabel` (Right, 76) and `rightCluster` (Right, 142) are both `Dock.Right`. In WinForms, `Dock.Fill` receives whatever's left **after** all `Dock.Right`/`Dock.Left` siblings are placed — but **only if the Fill control is added FIRST in the z-order**. It is. So the name should get `Width - 76 - 142 = whatever's left`. If the containing panel is ~300px wide, the name gets ~80px, and `AutoEllipsis` should kick in.

**But `AutoEllipsis` only works when `AutoSize = false` AND the label has a real width constraint.** With `Dock.Fill` inside a Panel, the label's width IS constrained. So it should ellipsize.

**UNLESS** — and I think this is it — **the `CartLineControl` itself is being sized wrong by `RefreshCartLines()`:**

```csharp
var line = new CartLineControl(item) { Width = _cartLinesPanel.ClientSize.Width - 4 };
```

At the moment `RefreshCartLines()` runs, `_cartLinesPanel` may not have its final width yet — because we're adding controls to a `FlowLayoutPanel` inside a `Dock.Fill` inside a `Dock.Right` column, and WinForms doesn't always settle the layout in one pass. If `ClientSize.Width` is small (e.g. 0 or 100 during the first layout pass), then `line.Width` is tiny, and:

- `nameLabel` gets `tiny - 76 - 142 = negative` → **renders at 0 or wraps**
- `priceLabel` (76) and `rightCluster` (142) get **priority** because they're `Dock.Right`, so they squeeze the name to nothing
- the stepper buttons get squeezed, hence `+` clipping

**That's the bug.** It's not `CartLineControl` — it's `RefreshCartLines()` setting `Width` too early. The `- 4` fudge is also wrong because it doesn't account for the vertical scrollbar width when the list is long enough to need one.

**Fix:** don't set `Width` at creation. Let the FlowLayoutPanel size the line, and instead make `CartLineControl` respond to its parent's resize by re-laying out its children. Or, simpler and more reliable: set the line's `Width` **after** it's added to the panel, in a `Layout` event or on the panel's `ClientSizeChanged`.

Actually the cleanest fix: **make `_cartLinesPanel` a `TableLayoutPanel`** instead of a `FlowLayoutPanel`, with `AutoSize = true`, `GrowStyle = AddRows`, one column, and each `CartLineControl` set to `Dock.Fill` / `Anchor = Left|Right` in its cell. Then the width is owned by the table, not guessed at.

But that's a bigger refactor. The **minimal fix** is:

```csharp
private void RefreshCartLines()
{
    _cartLinesPanel.Controls.Clear();

    if (_transactionViewModel is null || _transactionViewModel.CartItems.Count == 0)
    {
        _cartLinesPanel.Controls.Add(_cartEmptyLabel);
        return;
    }

    // Reserve room for the vertical scrollbar unconditionally, so lines don't get clipped
    // when the list grows past the box height. Computing this per-line from the current
    // ClientSize fails because the FlowLayoutPanel hasn't settled its final width at the
    // moment the first line is added.
    var lineWidth = _cartLinesPanel.ClientSize.Width - SystemInformation.VerticalScrollBarWidth - 4;

    foreach (var item in _transactionViewModel.CartItems)
    {
        var line = new CartLineControl(item) { Width = Math.Max(120, lineWidth) };
        line.QuantityIncreased += (s, e) => ChangeQuantity(item, +1);
        line.QuantityDecreased += (s, e) => ChangeQuantity(item, -1);
        line.RemoveClicked += (s, e) => _transactionViewModel!.RemoveItemCommand.Execute(item);
        _cartLinesPanel.Controls.Add(line);
    }
}
```

**Plus** — and this is important — the cart lines panel needs to **re-lay-out when the box is resized** (window resize, or drawer state change). Add to `BuildOrderBox()`:

```csharp
_cartLinesPanel.ClientSizeChanged += (s, e) => RefreshCartLines();
```

Hmm, but that would infinite-loop (resizing lines changes layout, which changes ClientSize, which fires the event). Let me use `Resize` instead, and add a re-entry guard. Actually — cleanest: don't re-layout on resize at all for now; a staff member doesn't resize mid-sale. Just fix the initial width calculation.

**Actually, the real question is: is the cart line in the screenshot drawn with `Width = something small`?** The screenshot shows the line taking up most of the Order box width (name on the left, price in the middle, stepper on the right). So the line IS wide. So my "too-narrow at creation" theory is wrong.

OK — so the name is wrapping despite having room. **The other possibility: `_cartLinesPanel` is a `FlowLayoutPanel` with `WrapContents = false` and `FlowDirection.TopDown`, and its `AutoScroll = true`.** When `AutoScroll` is on and the content exceeds the visible area, the panel adds scrollbars. But more importantly — `FlowLayoutPanel` respects each child's `Margin` AND the child's **own `Width` is not auto-managed** unless the child is set to `Anchor` (which does nothing in FlowLayoutPanel) — FlowLayoutPanel uses the child's `Width` as-is. So setting `Width` at creation *should* work.

Unless... the `CartLineControl` I sent has **`Height = 44` set but NOT `Width`**, and `Width` is set externally. That's what your file shows. So the width comes from `RefreshCartLines()`. And the screenshot shows it's roughly correct.

So — **why is the name wrapping?** Let me look at the file once more...

`nameLabel.Dock = DockStyle.Fill` — but the parent `CartLineControl` has **`Height = 44` and its children are added in order: `nameLabel`, `priceLabel`, `rightCluster`.** In WinForms, **`Dock.Fill` only respects the space left by *earlier-added* docked siblings** — later-added docked siblings **overlap** it, not push it. Wait, no — WinForms docks in **reverse z-order**: the LAST-added control gets docked FIRST (outermost), and Fill gets whatever's left. So the add order `nameLabel → priceLabel → rightCluster` means `rightCluster` docks first (outermost right), then `priceLabel` (inner right), then `nameLabel` fills the rest. That's correct.

Hmm. So the name SHOULD be getting the remaining width. And `AutoEllipsis` should ellipsize.

**Oh.** I see it now. `AutoEllipsis` on a `Label` with `TextAlign = MiddleLeft` **works when the text is a single line and the label width is smaller than the rendered text**. But the label's **`Height`** matters too: if the label is 44px tall and the text would wrap to two lines at that width, the label renders two lines and `AutoEllipsis` doesn't kick in — `AutoEllipsis` only ellipsizes when the text would *otherwise be clipped horizontally on one line*, not when it would wrap.

**The name label has `Height` inherited from `Dock.Fill` = 44px minus nothing = 44px.** At 9.5f font, two lines of text need ~34px, which fits in 44. So the label happily wraps to two lines instead of ellipsizing.

**The fix:** constrain the name label's height to a single line so `AutoEllipsis` is forced to kick in. Set `nameLabel.AutoSize = false` (it isn't, but be explicit) and either:

**The reliable fix:** wrap the name label in a `Panel` that's `Dock.Fill`, then inside that panel the label is `Dock.Top` with `Height = 22` and `AutoEllipsis = true`. The 22px height forces single-line rendering, and `AutoEllipsis` then ellipsizes when the width is insufficient.

Or — simpler — set the label's `MaximumSize = new Size(0, 22)`, which forces the label to a max height of 22 regardless of docking. Actually `MaximumSize` on a docked control is honored. Let me use that.

Actually, the simplest reliable fix: **set the label's `Height` to a single line after docking by not letting it fill vertically.** Use `Dock = DockStyle.Left` with a fixed width computed at construction, plus vertical centering. But width isn't known at construction.

**Cleanest solution: don't use Dock at all for the name — use `Anchor = Left | Right` on all three, positioned manually.** Or use a `TableLayoutPanel` for the row.

## 1. `CartLineControl.cs` — full file replacement

TableLayoutPanel-based so the name cell actually ellipsizes instead of wrapping, buttons sit at a fixed size, and the gap between stepper and ✕ is real.

```csharp
using CRM_Morcaffein.domain.entities;
using CRM_Morcaffein.Theme;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.winforms.Views.Controls
{
    /// <summary>
    /// One row in the Order box: "Drink Name (Size) +Mods … ₱SubTotal [- 2x +] ✕" — a compact
    /// inline quantity stepper instead of a data-grid row, matching a modern POS's order list
    /// rather than the boxed-table convention the rest of the app uses (this is the one
    /// deliberate exception, per the POS-specific redesign).
    ///
    /// Layout uses a TableLayoutPanel (not Dock-based) because the name cell needs to ellipsize
    /// on one line rather than wrap when narrow — a Dock.Fill label at 44px tall will wrap to
    /// two lines before AutoEllipsis kicks in, since AutoEllipsis only elides when the text
    /// would otherwise be horizontally clipped on ONE line.
    /// </summary>
    public class CartLineControl : Panel
    {
        public OrderItem Item { get; }

        public event EventHandler? QuantityIncreased;
        public event EventHandler? QuantityDecreased;
        public event EventHandler? RemoveClicked;

        private const int RowHeight = 44;
        private const int NameColumnHeight = 22;
        private const int StepperButtonSize = 30;
        private const int QtyLabelWidth = 34;
        private const int PriceWidth = 76;
        private const int RemoveWidth = 28;
        private const int GapBeforeRemove = 10;

        public CartLineControl(OrderItem item)
        {
            Item = item;

            // Deliberately NOT Dock=Top: this control lives inside a FlowLayoutPanel
            // (TopDown), which positions children itself — a Dock value on a flowed child
            // fights the flow layout and was why cart lines weren't rendering at all.
            Height = RowHeight;
            Margin = new Padding(0, 0, 0, 3);
            BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary;

            var modifiersSuffix = item.OrderItemModifiers.Count == 0
                ? string.Empty
                : $" +{string.Join(",", item.OrderItemModifiers.Select(m => m.ProductModifierNameSnapshot))}";

            // ----- Name (single-line, ellipsized) -----
            // Wrapped in a Dock.Fill host panel so the label itself can be pinned to a
            // single-line height and vertically centered, instead of stretching to the
            // full row height and wrapping.
            var nameHost = new Panel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
            };

            var nameLabel = new Label
            {
                Text = $"{item.Product?.ProductName ?? "—"} ({item.SizeNameSnapshot}){modifiersSuffix}",
                Dock = DockStyle.Top,
                Height = NameColumnHeight,
                AutoEllipsis = true,
                TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleLeft,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9.5f),
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralText,
            };
            nameHost.Controls.Add(nameLabel);

            // ----- Price -----
            var priceLabel = new Label
            {
                Text = $"₱{item.SubTotal:0.00}",
                Width = PriceWidth,
                TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleRight,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(9.5f),
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralText,
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
            };

            // ----- Stepper + remove, as one cluster -----
            // One container so the gap between stepper and ✕ is real empty space inside a
            // single parent, not a Margin between two docked siblings (WinForms packs those
            // flush and honors their margins inconsistently).
            var rightCluster = new Panel
            {
                Width = StepperButtonSize + QtyLabelWidth + StepperButtonSize + GapBeforeRemove + RemoveWidth,
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
            };

            var stepper = new FlowLayoutPanel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Left,
                Width = StepperButtonSize + QtyLabelWidth + StepperButtonSize,
                FlowDirection = FlowDirection.LeftToRight,
                WrapContents = false,
                Padding = new Padding(0, 7, 0, 7),
            };

            var removeBtn = new Button
            {
                Text = "✕",
                Dock = DockStyle.Right,
                Width = RemoveWidth,
                FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat,
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralTextMuted,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9f),
                Cursor = Cursors.Hand,
            };
            removeBtn.FlatAppearance.BorderSize = 0;
            removeBtn.Click += (s, e) => RemoveClicked?.Invoke(this, EventArgs.Empty);

            var minusBtn = MakeStepperButton("-");
            minusBtn.Click += (s, e) => QuantityDecreased?.Invoke(this, EventArgs.Empty);

            var qtyLabel = new Label
            {
                Text = $"{item.Quantity}x",
                Width = QtyLabelWidth,
                Height = StepperButtonSize,
                TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleCenter,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(10f),
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralText,
            };

            var plusBtn = MakeStepperButton("+");
            plusBtn.Click += (s, e) => QuantityIncreased?.Invoke(this, EventArgs.Empty);

            stepper.Controls.Add(minusBtn);
            stepper.Controls.Add(qtyLabel);
            stepper.Controls.Add(plusBtn);

            // Inside rightCluster: stepper docked Left (added first), removeBtn docked Right
            // (added after) — opposite edges, gap in the middle.
            rightCluster.Controls.Add(stepper);
            rightCluster.Controls.Add(removeBtn);

            // ----- Compose: three columns, row fills width -----
            var layout = new TableLayoutPanel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                ColumnCount = 3,
                RowCount = 1,
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
                Margin = new Padding(0),
                Padding = new Padding(0),
            };
            layout.ColumnStyles.Add(new ColumnStyle(SizeType.Percent, 100f));       // name (fills)
            layout.ColumnStyles.Add(new ColumnStyle(SizeType.Absolute, PriceWidth)); // price
            layout.ColumnStyles.Add(new ColumnStyle(SizeType.Absolute, rightCluster.Width)); // cluster

            nameHost.Dock = DockStyle.Fill;
            nameHost.Margin = new Padding(0, (RowHeight - NameColumnHeight) / 2, 0, 0); // vertically center single-line label
            priceLabel.Dock = DockStyle.Fill;
            priceLabel.Margin = new Padding(0);
            rightCluster.Dock = DockStyle.Fill;
            rightCluster.Margin = new Padding(0);

            layout.Controls.Add(nameHost, 0, 0);
            layout.Controls.Add(priceLabel, 1, 0);
            layout.Controls.Add(rightCluster, 2, 0);

            Controls.Add(layout);
        }

        private static Button MakeStepperButton(string text) => new()
        {
            Text = text,
            Width = StepperButtonSize,
            Height = StepperButtonSize,
            FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat,
            BackColor = BrandPalette.ButtonSecondaryFill,
            ForeColor = BrandPalette.ButtonSecondaryText,
            Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(10f),
            Cursor = Cursors.Hand,
        };
    }
}
```

**Why this actually fixes the screenshot:**

- Name cell is `TableLayoutPanel` cell with `Percent(100)` — gets whatever's left after the two absolute columns, guaranteed.
- `nameLabel` is pinned to `Height = 22` (single line), so `AutoEllipsis` fires when the width is insufficient, instead of wrapping to two lines.
- `rightCluster` width is computed from constants, so `-`, `1x`, `+` are all exactly `StepperButtonSize` tall — they can't render at different sizes.
- The 10px gap between stepper and ✕ is real empty space (cluster is wider than stepper + remove combined by exactly `GapBeforeRemove`).

## 2. `Order.cs` — add `RemovePromo`

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Removes an applied promo from a still-Pending order. Counterpart to ApplyPromo —
/// CampaignRedeems has no other way to be unwound, so this is the only supported path for
/// "the customer changed their mind / staff picked the wrong promo". No-op if the campaign
/// wasn't actually applied.
/// </summary>
public void RemovePromo(Campaign campaign)
{
    if (campaign == null) throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(campaign));

    EnsureOrderIsPending();

    var redeem = CampaignRedeems.FirstOrDefault(r => r.CampaignId == campaign.CampaignId);
    if (redeem is null)
        return;

    CampaignRedeems.Remove(redeem);
    RecalculateTotals();
}
```

No other change to `Order.cs`.

### 6b. Fix `RefreshPromoCombo()`

Replace the whole method:

```csharp
private void RefreshPromoCombo()
{
    if (_transactionViewModel is null)
    {
        _promoCombo.Items.Clear();
        _promoCombo.Enabled = false;
        return;
    }

    // Read the current selection from PromoItem (not Campaign — the items ARE PromoItem now).
    var currentId = (_promoCombo.SelectedItem as PromoItem)?.Campaign?.CampaignId;

    _suppressPromoApply = true;

    _promoCombo.Items.Clear();
    _promoCombo.Items.Add(new PromoItem(null, "Select a Promo"));
    foreach (var campaign in _transactionViewModel.EligiblePromos)
    {
        var label = campaign.DiscountType == "Percentage"
            ? $"{campaign.PromoName} — {campaign.DiscountValue:0.##}% off"
            : $"{campaign.PromoName} — ₱{campaign.DiscountValue:0.##} off";
        _promoCombo.Items.Add(new PromoItem(campaign, label));
    }

    var restoredIndex = 0;
    if (currentId.HasValue)
    {
        for (int i = 1; i < _promoCombo.Items.Count; i++)
        {
            if (_promoCombo.Items[i] is PromoItem pi && pi.Campaign?.CampaignId == currentId.Value)
            {
                restoredIndex = i;
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    _promoCombo.SelectedIndex = restoredIndex;
    _suppressPromoApply = false;
    _promoCombo.Enabled = true;
}
```

**Two bugs fixed here:** `currentId` now reads from `PromoItem` (was `Campaign`, always null → selection never restored), and the restore loop now matches `PromoItem` too.
