```csharp
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(11.5f),
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralText,
            };

            _cartStatusLabel = new Label
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Top,
                Height = 20,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(8.5f),
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.StatusNegativeFill,
            };

            var summaryTable = new TableLayoutPanel { Dock = DockStyle.Fill, ColumnCount = 2, RowCount = 5 };
            summaryTable.ColumnStyles.Add(new ColumnStyle(SizeType.Percent, 55f));
            summaryTable.ColumnStyles.Add(new ColumnStyle(SizeType.Percent, 45f));

            Label MakeCaption(string text) => new() { Text = text, Dock = DockStyle.Fill, Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9.5f), ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralTextMuted, TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleLeft };
            Label MakeValue() => new() { Text = "₱0.00", Dock = DockStyle.Fill, Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(11f), ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralText, TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleRight };

            _subTotalValueLabel = MakeValue();
            _discountValueLabel = MakeValue();
            _vatValueLabel = MakeValue();
            _pwdSeniorValueLabel = MakeValue();
            _totalValueLabel = MakeValue();
            _totalValueLabel.ForeColor = BrandPalette.Brand;
            _totalValueLabel.Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(15f);

            summaryTable.Controls.Add(MakeCaption("Subtotal"), 0, 0);
            summaryTable.Controls.Add(_subTotalValueLabel, 1, 0);
            summaryTable.Controls.Add(MakeCaption("Discount"), 0, 1);
            summaryTable.Controls.Add(_discountValueLabel, 1, 1);
            summaryTable.Controls.Add(MakeCaption("VAT (12%)"), 0, 2);
            summaryTable.Controls.Add(_vatValueLabel, 1, 2);
            summaryTable.Controls.Add(MakeCaption("PWD/Senior Disc."), 0, 3);
            summaryTable.Controls.Add(_pwdSeniorValueLabel, 1, 3);
            summaryTable.Controls.Add(MakeCaption("Total"), 0, 4);
            summaryTable.Controls.Add(_totalValueLabel, 1, 4);

            box.Controls.Add(summaryTable);
            box.Controls.Add(_cartStatusLabel);
            box.Controls.Add(header);

            return box;
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // CUSTOMER SELECTION (API-backed)
        // =====================================================================

        private async void RunCustomerSearch()
        {
            var query = _customerSearchTxtBx.Text.Trim();
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(query))
                return;

            try
            {
                var customerApi = new CustomerApi();
                var match = await customerApi.FindCustomerAsync(query);

                if (match is null)
                {
                    _customerSearchErrorLabel.Text = $"No customer found for \"{query}\".";
                    _customerProfilePanel.Visible = false;
                    return;
                }

                _customerSearchErrorLabel.Text = string.Empty;
                ShowCustomerProfile(match);
                await SelectCustomerAsync(match);
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                _customerSearchErrorLabel.Text = ex.Message;
                _customerProfilePanel.Visible = false;
            }
        }

        private void ShowCustomerProfile(CustomerResponseDto customer)
        {
            _customerProfileNameLabel.Text = customer.FullName;
            _customerProfileDetailLabel.Text = $"{customer.Tier} Tier   •   {customer.PointsBalance} pts\n{customer.ContactNumber}";
            _customerProfilePanel.Visible = true;
        }

        private async Task SelectCustomerAsync(CustomerResponseDto dto)
        {
            var employeeId = EmployeeSession.Current?.EmployeeId
                ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("No employee session — the Transaction view requires a logged-in employee.");

            if (_controller is not null && _controller.CartItems.Count > 0)
            {
                var currentCustomerName = _controller.Customer.FullName;
                var confirm = MessageBox.Show(
                    FindForm(),
                    $"Discard the in-progress order for {currentCustomerName} and start a new one for {dto.FullName}?",
                    "Start New Transaction",
                    MessageBoxButtons.YesNo,
                    MessageBoxIcon.Warning);

                if (confirm != DialogResult.Yes)
                {
                    _customerSearchTxtBx.Text = _controller.Customer.CustomerId.ToString();
                    return;
                }
            }

            // Convert DTO -> entity for the still-mock-backed TransactionController.
            var entity = new Customer
            {
                CustomerId = dto.CustomerId,
                FirstName = dto.FirstName,
                LastName = dto.LastName,
                ContactNumber = dto.ContactNumber,
                Email = dto.Email,
                Birthday = dto.Birthday,
                LastVisitDate = dto.LastVisitDate,
                PointsBalance = dto.PointsBalance,
                IsActive = dto.IsActive,
            };

            // Fetch active campaigns from the API before constructing the controller.
            var campaignApi = new CampaignApi();
            var campaignDtos = await campaignApi.GetActiveCampaignsAsync();
            var campaigns = campaignDtos.Select(MapToCampaignEntity).ToList();

            _controller = new TransactionController(_orderService, _catalogService, campaigns, entity, employeeId);

            RefreshProductsPanel();
            RefreshCartLines();
            RefreshSummary();
        }

        private static Campaign MapToCampaignEntity(CampaignResponseDto dto) => new()
        {
            CampaignId = dto.CampaignId,
            PromoName = dto.PromoName,
            PromoCategory = dto.PromoCategory,
            DiscountType = dto.DiscountType,
            DiscountValue = dto.DiscountValue,
            TargetTier = dto.TargetTier,
            MinPurchaseAmount = dto.MinPurchaseAmount,
            MaxDiscountAmount = dto.MaxDiscountAmount,
            MaxRedemptionsPerCustomer = dto.MaxRedemptionsPerCustomer,
            StartDate = dto.StartDate,
            EndDate = dto.EndDate,
            IsActive = dto.IsActive,
        };

        // =====================================================================
        // PROMO
        // =====================================================================

        private void ShowPromoMenu()
        {
            if (_controller is null)
                return;

            var menu = new ContextMenuStrip();

            if (_controller.Order.CampaignRedeems.Count > 0)
            {
                var clear = menu.Items.Add("Clear applied promo");
                clear.Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(9f);
                clear.Click += (s, e) =>
                {
                    _controller.ClearPromos();
                    RefreshSummary();
                    RefreshPromoButton();
                };
                menu.Items.Add(new ToolStripSeparator());
            }

            var eligiblePromos = _controller.GetEligiblePromos();
            if (eligiblePromos.Count == 0)
            {
                var none = menu.Items.Add("No promos available for this order");
                none.Enabled = false;
            }
            else
            {
                foreach (var campaign in eligiblePromos)
                {
                    var alreadyApplied = _controller.Order.CampaignRedeems
                        .Any(r => r.CampaignId == campaign.CampaignId);

                    var label = campaign.DiscountType == "Percentage"
                        ? $"{campaign.PromoName} — {campaign.DiscountValue:0.##}% off"
                        : $"{campaign.PromoName} — ₱{campaign.DiscountValue:0.##} off";
                    if (alreadyApplied)
                        label += "  (applied)";

                    var item = menu.Items.Add(label);
                    item.Enabled = !alreadyApplied;
                    item.Click += (s, e) =>
                    {
                        try
                        {
                            _controller.ApplyPromo(campaign);
                            RefreshSummary();
                            RefreshPromoButton();
                        }
                        catch (Exception ex)
                        {
                            ShowCartStatus(ex.Message);
                        }
                    };
                }
            }

            menu.Show(_promoMenuBtn, new Point(0, -menu.PreferredSize.Height));
        }

        private void RefreshPromoButton()
        {
            if (_controller is null)
            {
                _promoMenuBtn.Text = "Select a Promo ▾";
                _promoMenuBtn.Enabled = false;
                return;
            }

            var applied = _controller.Order.CampaignRedeems.FirstOrDefault();

            if (applied is null)
            {
                _promoMenuBtn.Text = "Select a Promo ▾";
            }
            else
            {
                // Look up the display name from the controller's already-fetched campaign list.
                var campaign = _controller.GetEligiblePromos()
                                   .FirstOrDefault(c => c.CampaignId == applied.CampaignId);

                var name = campaign?.PromoName ?? $"Promo #{applied.CampaignId}";
                _promoMenuBtn.Text = $"{name} ▾";
            }

            _promoMenuBtn.Enabled = true;
        }

        private void RefreshSummary()
        {
            RefreshPromoButton();

            if (_controller is null)
            {
                _subTotalValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
                _discountValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
                _vatValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
                _pwdSeniorValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
                _totalValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
                _logSaleBtn.Enabled = false;
                return;
            }

            _subTotalValueLabel.Text = $"₱{_controller.SubTotal:0.00}";
            _discountValueLabel.Text = $"₱{_controller.TotalDiscount:0.00}";
            _vatValueLabel.Text = $"₱{_controller.TotalAmount * VatRate:0.00}";
            _pwdSeniorValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
            _totalValueLabel.Text = $"₱{_controller.TotalAmount:0.00}";
            _logSaleBtn.Enabled = _controller.HasItems;
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // DRINKS / CART
        // =====================================================================

        private void BuildCategoryOptions()
        {
            _categoryCombo.Items.Clear();
            _categoryCombo.Items.Add(AllCategoriesOption);
            foreach (var category in _catalogService.GetCategories())
                _categoryCombo.Items.Add(category);
            _categoryCombo.SelectedIndex = 0;
        }

        private void RefreshProductsPanel()
        {
            _productsFlowPanel.Controls.Clear();
            if (_controller is null) return;

            var products = _controller.GetProducts(_selectedCategory, _productSearchTxtBx.Text);
            foreach (var product in products)
            {
                var card = new ProductCardControl(product);
                card.CardClicked += (s, e) => OpenCustomizerForNewItem(product);
                card.SizeQuickAdded += (s, size) => QuickAddToCart(product, size);
                _productsFlowPanel.Controls.Add(card);
            }
        }

        private void QuickAddToCart(Product product, ProductSize size)
        {
            if (_controller is null)
            {
                ShowCartStatus("Pick a customer on the left first.");
                return;
            }

            try
            {
                _controller.AddItemToCart(product, size, 1, Enumerable.Empty<ProductModifier>());
                RefreshCartLines();
                RefreshSummary();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                ShowCartStatus(ex.Message);
            }
        }

        private void OpenCustomizerForNewItem(Product product)
        {
            if (_controller is null)
            {
                ShowCartStatus("Pick a customer on the left first.");
                return;
            }

            using var form = new FrmItemCustomizer(product, _controller.GetModifiers());

            if (form.ShowDialog(FindForm()) == DialogResult.OK)
            {
                try
                {
                    _controller.AddItemToCart(product, form.SelectedSize, form.Quantity, form.SelectedModifiers);
                    RefreshCartLines();
                    RefreshSummary();
                }
                catch (Exception ex)
                {
                    ShowCartStatus(ex.Message);
                }
            }
        }

        private void RefreshCartLines()
        {
            _cartLinesPanel.Controls.Clear();

            if (_controller is null || _controller.CartItems.Count == 0)
            {
                _cartLinesPanel.Controls.Add(_cartEmptyLabel);
                return;
            }

            var lineWidth = Math.Max(200,
                _cartLinesPanel.ClientSize.Width - SystemInformation.VerticalScrollBarWidth - 8);

            foreach (var item in _controller.CartItems)
            {
                var line = new CartLineControl(item) { Width = lineWidth };
                line.QuantityIncreased += (s, e) => ChangeQuantity(item, +1);
                line.QuantityDecreased += (s, e) => ChangeQuantity(item, -1);
                line.RemoveClicked += (s, e) => RemoveFromCart(item);
                _cartLinesPanel.Controls.Add(line);
            }
        }

        private void RemoveFromCart(OrderItem item)
        {
            if (_controller is null) return;

            _controller.RemoveItem(item);
            RefreshCartLines();
            RefreshSummary();
        }

        private void ChangeQuantity(OrderItem item, int delta)
        {
            if (_controller is null || item.Product is null) return;

            var newQuantity = item.Quantity + delta;
            if (newQuantity <= 0)
            {
                RemoveFromCart(item);
                return;
            }

            var size = item.Product.ProductSizes.First(s => s.ProductSizeId == item.ProductSizeId);
            var modifiers = _controller.GetModifiers()
                .Where(m => item.OrderItemModifiers.Any(om => om.ProductModifierId == m.ProductModifierId));

            try
            {
                _controller.UpdateCartItem(item, size, newQuantity, modifiers);
                RefreshCartLines();
                RefreshSummary();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                ShowCartStatus(ex.Message);
            }
        }

        private void ShowCartStatus(string message) => _cartStatusLabel.Text = message;

        private void CompleteSale()
        {
            if (_controller is null) return;

            try
            {
                var customerName = _controller.Customer.FullName;
                var order = _controller.CompleteSale();

                MessageBox.Show(FindForm(),
                    $"Sale completed. {order.PointsEarned} points awarded to {customerName}.",
                    "Sale Complete", MessageBoxButtons.OK, MessageBoxIcon.Information);

                _controller = null;
                _customerProfilePanel.Visible = false;
                _customerSearchErrorLabel.Text = string.Empty;
                _customerSearchTxtBx.Text = string.Empty;
                RefreshProductsPanel();
                RefreshCartLines();
                RefreshSummary();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                ShowCartStatus(ex.Message);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

**What changed:**

- Removed `ICampaignService` field and constructor param.
- `SelectCustomer` → `SelectCustomerAsync`, now fetches campaigns from `CampaignApi` and passes them to `TransactionController`.
- Added `MapToCampaignEntity` helper.
- `RunCustomerSearch` now `await SelectCustomerAsync(match)`.
- `RefreshPromoButton` no longer references `_campaignService.GetById` — falls back to `Promo #{id}` if the promo isn't in the eligible list.

# `TransactionController.cs` — full replacement

```csharp
using CRM_Morcaffein.domain.entities;
using CRM_Morcaffein.Services;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.Controllers
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Controller for the Transactions/POS tab (MVC). One instance represents a single
    /// in-progress sale for one customer. Owns every business rule for the cart/promo/
    /// checkout flow — cart-item pricing, discount calculation, promo eligibility,
    /// points-earned math.
    ///
    /// Order, OrderItem, Product, and ProductModifier are still mock-backed via
    /// IOrderService / IProductCatalogService until the Orders feature area migrates.
    /// Campaigns come in as a pre-fetched list from the View (which pulls them from the
    /// API), because cart mutations are synchronous and can't await an HTTP call.
    /// </summary>
    public class TransactionController
    {
        private readonly IOrderService _orderService;
        private readonly IProductCatalogService _catalogService;
        private readonly IReadOnlyList<Campaign> _activeCampaigns;

        public Order Order { get; private set; }
        public Customer Customer { get; private set; }

        public IReadOnlyList<string> Categories { get; }

        public decimal SubTotal => Order.SubTotal;
        public decimal TotalDiscount => Order.TotalDiscount;
        public decimal TotalAmount => Order.TotalAmount;
        public bool HasItems => Order.OrderItems.Count > 0;
        public IReadOnlyList<OrderItem> CartItems => Order.OrderItems.ToList();

        public TransactionController(
            IOrderService orderService,
            IProductCatalogService catalogService,
            IReadOnlyList<Campaign> activeCampaigns,
            Customer customer,
            int createdByEmployeeId)
        {
            _orderService = orderService;
            _catalogService = catalogService;
            _activeCampaigns = activeCampaigns;
            Customer = customer;
            Order = _orderService.StartOrder(customer.CustomerId, createdByEmployeeId);
            Categories = _catalogService.GetCategories();
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Re-points the SAME in-progress order at a different customer (Quick Register
        /// relink flow). Not used by the main POS flow — search-and-Go there starts a fresh
        /// Controller/Order instead (see TransactionView.SelectCustomer).
        /// </summary>
        public void SwitchCustomer(Customer newCustomer)
        {
            Order = _orderService.LinkCustomerToOrder(Order, newCustomer);
            Customer = newCustomer;
        }

        public IReadOnlyList<Product> GetProducts(string category, string searchText)
        {
            IEnumerable<Product> products = string.IsNullOrEmpty(category)
                ? _catalogService.GetProducts()
                : _catalogService.GetByCategory(category);

            if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(searchText))
                products = products.Where(p => p.ProductName.Contains(searchText, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));

            return products.ToList();
        }

        public IReadOnlyList<ProductModifier> GetModifiers() => _catalogService.GetModifiers();

        public void AddItemToCart(Product product, ProductSize size, int quantity, IEnumerable<ProductModifier> modifiers)
        {
            EnsurePending();
            if (quantity <= 0)
                throw new ArgumentException("Quantity must be greater than zero.");

            var existing = Order.OrderItems.FirstOrDefault(i => i.ProductSizeId == size.ProductSizeId);
            if (existing != null)
            {
                existing.Quantity += quantity;
                RecalculateItemPricing(existing);
            }
            else
            {
                var item = _orderService.CreateOrderItem(Order, product, size, quantity);
                foreach (var modifier in modifiers)
                    _orderService.AddModifierToItem(item, modifier);
                RecalculateItemPricing(item);
            }

            RecalculateOrderTotals();
        }

        public void UpdateCartItem(OrderItem item, ProductSize newSize, int newQuantity, IEnumerable<ProductModifier> newModifiers)
        {
            EnsurePending();
            if (newQuantity <= 0)
                throw new ArgumentException("Quantity must be greater than zero.");

            if (item.ProductSizeId == newSize.ProductSizeId)
            {
                item.Quantity = newQuantity;
                item.OrderItemModifiers.Clear();
                foreach (var modifier in newModifiers)
                    _orderService.AddModifierToItem(item, modifier);
                RecalculateItemPricing(item);
                RecalculateOrderTotals();
            }
            else
            {
                _orderService.RemoveOrderItem(Order, item);
                AddItemToCart(item.Product!, newSize, newQuantity, newModifiers);
            }
        }

        public void RemoveItem(OrderItem item)
        {
            _orderService.RemoveOrderItem(Order, item);
            RecalculateOrderTotals();
        }

        public IReadOnlyList<Campaign> GetEligiblePromos() =>
            _activeCampaigns.Where(c => CanRedeem(c, Customer, Order)).ToList();

        public void ApplyPromo(Campaign campaign)
        {
            EnsurePending();
            var discount = CalculateDiscount(campaign, Order.SubTotal);
            _orderService.CreateCampaignRedeem(Order, campaign, discount);
            RecalculateOrderTotals();
        }

        public void RemovePromo(Campaign campaign)
        {
            var redeem = Order.CampaignRedeems.FirstOrDefault(r => r.CampaignId == campaign.CampaignId);
            if (redeem is null) return;

            _orderService.RemoveCampaignRedeem(Order, redeem);
            RecalculateOrderTotals();
        }

        public void ClearPromos()
        {
            foreach (var redeem in Order.CampaignRedeems.ToList())
                _orderService.RemoveCampaignRedeem(Order, redeem);

            RecalculateOrderTotals();
        }

        public Order CompleteSale()
        {
            EnsurePending();
            if (Order.OrderItems.Count == 0)
                throw new InvalidOperationException("Order cannot be empty.");

            Order.Status = "Completed";
            Order.PointsEarned = (int)(Order.TotalAmount / 10m);

            if (Order.PointsEarned > 0)
            {
                Customer.PointsBalance += Order.PointsEarned;
                Customer.LastVisitDate = DateTime.UtcNow;
                Customer.PointLedgers.Add(new PointLedger
                {
                    CustomerId = Customer.CustomerId,
                    PointsChange = Order.PointsEarned,
                    Type = "Earned",
                    Reason = $"Order #{Order.OrderId} Spend",
                    OrderId = Order.OrderId,
                    Timestamp = DateTime.UtcNow,
                });
            }

            _orderService.CompleteOrder(Order);
            return Order;
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // BUSINESS RULES
        // =====================================================================

        private void EnsurePending()
        {
            if (!Order.Status.Equals("Pending", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Order cannot be modified in '{Order.Status}' state.");
        }

        private static void RecalculateItemPricing(OrderItem item)
        {
            item.UnitPrice = item.BaseSizePrice + item.OrderItemModifiers.Sum(m => m.UnitPrice);
            item.SubTotal = item.Quantity * item.UnitPrice;
        }

        private void RecalculateOrderTotals()
        {
            Order.SubTotal = Order.OrderItems.Sum(i => i.SubTotal);

            decimal totalDiscount = 0m;
            foreach (var redeem in Order.CampaignRedeems)
            {
                var campaign = redeem.Campaign ?? _activeCampaigns.FirstOrDefault(c => c.CampaignId == redeem.CampaignId);
                var discount = campaign != null ? CalculateDiscount(campaign, Order.SubTotal) : redeem.DiscountUsed;
                redeem.DiscountUsed = discount;
                totalDiscount += discount;
            }
            Order.TotalDiscount = totalDiscount;

            Order.TotalAmount = Math.Max(0m, Order.SubTotal - Order.TotalDiscount);
        }

        private static bool IsCurrentlyActive(Campaign campaign)
        {
            var now = DateTime.UtcNow;
            return campaign.IsActive && now >= campaign.StartDate && now <= campaign.EndDate;
        }

        private static bool CanRedeem(Campaign campaign, Customer customer, Order order)
        {
            if (!IsCurrentlyActive(campaign)) return false;

            if (campaign.MinPurchaseAmount.HasValue && order.SubTotal < campaign.MinPurchaseAmount.Value)
                return false;

            if (!campaign.TargetTier.Equals("All", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) &&
                !PointsToTier(customer.PointsBalance).Equals(campaign.TargetTier, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                return false;

            if (campaign.PromoCategory.Equals("Birthday", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) && !IsBirthdayToday(customer))
                return false;

            if (campaign.PromoCategory.Equals("Inactive", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) && !IsInactive(customer))
                return false;

            var previousRedemptions = campaign.CampaignRedeems.Count(r => r.Order != null && r.Order.CustomerId == customer.CustomerId);
            return previousRedemptions < campaign.MaxRedemptionsPerCustomer;
        }

        private static string PointsToTier(int pointsBalance) => pointsBalance switch
        {
            >= 500 => "Gold",
            >= 200 => "Silver",
            _ => "Regular",
        };

        private static bool IsBirthdayToday(Customer customer) =>
            customer.Birthday?.Month == DateTime.UtcNow.Month && customer.Birthday?.Day == DateTime.UtcNow.Day;

        private static bool IsInactive(Customer customer) => (DateTime.UtcNow - customer.LastVisitDate).Days > 20;

        private static decimal CalculateDiscount(Campaign campaign, decimal orderTotal)
        {
            if (orderTotal <= 0) return 0m;
            if (campaign.MinPurchaseAmount.HasValue && orderTotal < campaign.MinPurchaseAmount.Value) return 0m;

            decimal discount;
            if (campaign.DiscountType.Equals("Percentage", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
            {
                discount = orderTotal * (campaign.DiscountValue / 100m);
                if (campaign.MaxDiscountAmount.HasValue && discount > campaign.MaxDiscountAmount.Value)
                    discount = campaign.MaxDiscountAmount.Value;
            }
            else
            {
                discount = campaign.DiscountValue;
            }

            return discount > orderTotal ? orderTotal : discount;
        }
    }
}
```

## Where to put the product images

**The `LocalImagePath` field on `Product` is the answer.** From the entity:

```csharp
public string? ImageUrl { get; set; }
public string? LocalImagePath { get; set; }
```

Two fields, two purposes:

- **`ImageUrl`** — the URL where the image lives (your menu context has these)
- **`LocalImagePath`** — where the image file lives on the machine running the app (your downloaded files)

Since the app is a **desktop WinForms app running locally**, `LocalImagePath` is what actually matters for displaying product photos. `ImageUrl` is metadata.

### Where to physically put the files

**Recommendation: inside the WinForms project, in a folder that gets copied to the output directory.**

```text
CRM_Morcaffein.winforms/
├── Resources/
│   └── Products/
│       ├── matcha-latte.png
│       ├── americano.png
│       ├── caramel-macchiato.png
│       └── ... (one file per product)
```

**Then set each image's build action.** In Visual Studio:

1. Right-click an image in Solution Explorer
2. Properties
3. **Copy to Output Directory** = `Copy if newer` (or `PreserveNewest`)
4. **Build Action** = `Content`

That way, when the app runs, the images are at `<app folder>/Resources/Products/matcha-latte.png`, and the code can load them by relative path.

### How the code will use them

When the Products migration runs, `LocalImagePath` in the DB will be stored as a **relative path** like `Resources/Products/matcha-latte.png` (or an absolute one, but relative is better for a desktop app). The `ProductCardControl` will do something like:

```csharp
var fullPath = Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, product.LocalImagePath);
if (File.Exists(fullPath))
    // load and draw the image
```

`AppContext.BaseDirectory` resolves to the folder the .exe runs from — which is where the `Copy to Output Directory` setting puts the files.

### Naming convention for the files

Since `LocalImagePath` is stored per-product, **name the files to match the product code** — the `ProductCode` field exists on the entity for exactly this kind of thing:

- Product code `MATCHA-LATTE` → file `matcha-latte.png`
- Product code `AMER-001` → file `amer-001.png`

Lowercase, dashes instead of spaces, `.png` or `.jpg` consistently.

**(C) Skip Products migration entirely for now** — move to Feedback next (which doesn't need the DB seeded — Feedback is empty and that's fine), and do Products last with proper seeding.

**My recommendation: (C).** Do Feedback next. It doesn't require DB seeding — an empty Feedback table just shows an empty grid, which is *correct* because no one has logged feedback yet. Products needs seeding because the POS needs a menu to be usable. So do the seeding work in a dedicated step when you get to Products, rather than tacking it onto Feedback.

# File 3 — `CRM_Morcaffein.api/Controllers/FeedbackController.cs`

```csharp
using CRM_Morcaffein.api.DTOs;
using CRM_Morcaffein.domain.entities;
using CRM_Morcaffein.infrastructure.services;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.api.Controllers
{
    [ApiController]
    [Route("api/tenant/{companyId:int}/feedback")]
    public class FeedbackController : ControllerBase
    {
        private readonly ITenantDbContextFactory _tenantFactory;

        public FeedbackController(ITenantDbContextFactory tenantFactory)
        {
            _tenantFactory = tenantFactory;
        }

        // GET api/tenant/{companyId}/feedback?search=...
        // Returns all tickets (newest first), optionally filtered by customer name,
        // category, status, or exact ticket ID.
        [HttpGet]
        public async Task<ActionResult<List<FeedbackResponseDto>>> GetTickets(
            int companyId,
            [FromQuery] string? search)
        {
            await using var tenant = await _tenantFactory.CreateAsync(companyId);

            var query = tenant.Feedbacks
                .AsNoTracking()
                .Where(f => f.IsActive);

            if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(search))
            {
                var term = search.Trim();
                var asInt = int.TryParse(term, out var parsed) ? parsed : (int?)null;

                query = query.Where(f =>
                    (f.Customer != null && (f.Customer.FirstName + " " + f.Customer.LastName).Contains(term)) ||
                    f.Category.Contains(term) ||
                    f.Status.Contains(term) ||
                    (asInt.HasValue && f.TicketId == asInt.Value));
            }

            var tickets = await query
                .OrderByDescending(f => f.DateLogged)
                .Select(f => new FeedbackResponseDto
                {
                    TicketId = f.TicketId,
                    CustomerId = f.CustomerId,
                    CustomerName = f.Customer != null
                        ? (f.Customer.FirstName + " " + f.Customer.LastName).Trim()
                        : "—",
                    LoggedBy = f.LoggedBy,
                    LoggedByName = f.LoggedByEmployee != null
                        ? (f.LoggedByEmployee.FirstName + " " + f.LoggedByEmployee.LastName).Trim()
                        : "—",
                    Rating = f.Rating,
                    Category = f.Category,
                    StaffNotes = f.StaffNotes,
                    Status = f.Status,
                    DateLogged = f.DateLogged,
                    DecidedBy = f.DecidedBy,
                    DecidedAt = f.DecidedAt,
                    DecisionNotes = f.DecisionNotes
                })
                .ToListAsync();

            return Ok(tickets);
        }

        // GET api/tenant/{companyId}/feedback/{id}
        [HttpGet("{id:int}")]
        public async Task<ActionResult<FeedbackResponseDto>> GetTicket(int companyId, int id)
        {
            await using var tenant = await _tenantFactory.CreateAsync(companyId);

            var ticket = await tenant.Feedbacks
                .AsNoTracking()
                .Where(f => f.TicketId == id)
                .Select(f => new FeedbackResponseDto
                {
                    TicketId = f.TicketId,
                    CustomerId = f.CustomerId,
                    CustomerName = f.Customer != null
                        ? (f.Customer.FirstName + " " + f.Customer.LastName).Trim()
                        : "—",
                    LoggedBy = f.LoggedBy,
                    LoggedByName = f.LoggedByEmployee != null
                        ? (f.LoggedByEmployee.FirstName + " " + f.LoggedByEmployee.LastName).Trim()
                        : "—",
                    Rating = f.Rating,
                    Category = f.Category,
                    StaffNotes = f.StaffNotes,
                    Status = f.Status,
                    DateLogged = f.DateLogged,
                    DecidedBy = f.DecidedBy,
                    DecidedAt = f.DecidedAt,
                    DecisionNotes = f.DecisionNotes
                })
                .FirstOrDefaultAsync();

            if (ticket is null)
                return NotFound();

            return Ok(ticket);
        }

        // POST api/tenant/{companyId}/feedback
        [HttpPost]
        public async Task<ActionResult<FeedbackResponseDto>> LogFeedback(
            int companyId,
            LogFeedbackRequest request)
        {
            // ---- Server-side validation ----
            if (request.CustomerId <= 0)
                return BadRequest(new { message = "Customer is required." });
            if (request.LoggedBy <= 0)
                return BadRequest(new { message = "Logged-by employee is required." });
            if (request.Rating < 1 || request.Rating > 5)
                return BadRequest(new { message = "Rating must be between 1 and 5 stars." });
            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(request.Category))
                return BadRequest(new { message = "Category is required." });

            await using var tenant = await _tenantFactory.CreateAsync(companyId);

            // Verify the customer and employee exist (FK safety + clear error)
            var customerExists = await tenant.Customers.AnyAsync(c => c.CustomerId == request.CustomerId);
            if (!customerExists)
                return BadRequest(new { message = "Customer not found." });

            var employeeExists = await tenant.Employees.AnyAsync(e => e.EmployeeId == request.LoggedBy);
            if (!employeeExists)
                return BadRequest(new { message = "Employee not found." });

            var feedback = new Feedback
            {
                CustomerId = request.CustomerId,
                LoggedBy = request.LoggedBy,
                Rating = request.Rating,
                Category = request.Category.Trim(),
                StaffNotes = request.StaffNotes?.Trim() ?? string.Empty,
                Status = "Pending",
                DateLogged = DateTime.UtcNow,
                IsActive = true,
                CreatedAt = DateTime.UtcNow,
                UpdatedAt = DateTime.UtcNow,
            };

            tenant.Feedbacks.Add(feedback);

            try
            {
                await tenant.SaveChangesAsync();
            }
            catch (DbUpdateException ex)
            {
                return Conflict(new { message = ex.InnerException?.Message ?? ex.Message });
            }

            // Reload with the joined names for the response
            var result = await tenant.Feedbacks
                .AsNoTracking()
                .Where(f => f.TicketId == feedback.TicketId)
                .Select(f => new FeedbackResponseDto
                {
                    TicketId = f.TicketId,
                    CustomerId = f.CustomerId,
                    CustomerName = f.Customer != null
                        ? (f.Customer.FirstName + " " + f.Customer.LastName).Trim()
                        : "—",
                    LoggedBy = f.LoggedBy,
                    LoggedByName = f.LoggedByEmployee != null
                        ? (f.LoggedByEmployee.FirstName + " " + f.LoggedByEmployee.LastName).Trim()
                        : "—",
                    Rating = f.Rating,
                    Category = f.Category,
                    StaffNotes = f.StaffNotes,
                    Status = f.Status,
                    DateLogged = f.DateLogged,
                    DecidedBy = f.DecidedBy,
                    DecidedAt = f.DecidedAt,
                    DecisionNotes = f.DecisionNotes
                })
                .FirstAsync();

            return Ok(result);
        }
    }
}
```

**Notes:**

- Routes under `api/tenant/{companyId}/feedback` — matches the pattern.
- The `search` filter checks customer name, category, status, or exact ticket ID (mirrors what the mock did).
- On write, it validates and joins names for the response.
- No resolve/dismiss endpoints here. Feedback is log + view only in the staff app; resolving lives on a future manager surface. When we build that, we'll add the endpoints then.

```csharp
using System.Net;
using System.Net.Http.Json;
using CRM_Morcaffein.api.DTOs;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.winforms.Services.Api
{
    public class FeedbackApi
    {
        private readonly HttpClient _http;

        public FeedbackApi()
        {
            _http = new HttpClient { BaseAddress = new Uri(ApiConfig.BaseUrl) };
        }

        // GET api/tenant/{companyId}/feedback?search=...
        public async Task<List<FeedbackResponseDto>> GetTicketsAsync(string? search = null)
        {
            var url = $"api/tenant/{ApiConfig.CompanyId}/feedback";
            if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(search))
                url += $"?search={Uri.EscapeDataString(search)}";

            var response = await _http.GetAsync(url);
            await EnsureSuccess(response);

            var result = await response.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync<List<FeedbackResponseDto>>();
            return result ?? new List<FeedbackResponseDto>();
        }

        // GET api/tenant/{companyId}/feedback/{id}
        public async Task<FeedbackResponseDto?> GetTicketAsync(int ticketId)
        {
            var response = await _http.GetAsync($"api/tenant/{ApiConfig.CompanyId}/feedback/{ticketId}");
            if (response.StatusCode == HttpStatusCode.NotFound)
                return null;
            await EnsureSuccess(response);
            return await response.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync<FeedbackResponseDto>();
        }

        // POST api/tenant/{companyId}/feedback
        public async Task<FeedbackResponseDto> LogFeedbackAsync(LogFeedbackRequest request)
        {
            var response = await _http.PostAsJsonAsync(
                $"api/tenant/{ApiConfig.CompanyId}/feedback", request);
            await EnsureSuccess(response);

            var result = await response.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync<FeedbackResponseDto>();
            return result ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("API returned an empty feedback ticket.");
        }

        private static async Task EnsureSuccess(HttpResponseMessage response)
        {
            if (response.IsSuccessStatusCode) return;

            var body = await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync();
            var message = TryExtractMessage(body) ?? $"API returned {(int)response.StatusCode}.";
            throw new InvalidOperationException(message);
        }

        private static string? TryExtractMessage(string body)
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(body)) return null;

            const string marker = "\"message\":\"";
            var idx = body.IndexOf(marker, StringComparison.Ordinal);
            if (idx < 0) return null;

            var start = idx + marker.Length;
            var end = body.IndexOf('"', start);
            if (end < 0) return null;

            return body.Substring(start, end - start);
        }
    }
}
```

```csharp
namespace CRM_Morcaffein.winforms.Views

        private async void SubmitBtn_Click(object? sender, EventArgs e)
        {
            if (_selectedCustomer is null) return;

            try

                errorLabel.Text = string.Empty;
                submitBtn.Enabled = false;

                CreatedFeedback = await _controller.LogFeedbackAsync(
                    _selectedCustomer.CustomerId,
                    _loggedByEmployeeId,
                    _rating,
                    _category,
                    staffNotesTxtBx.Text);

                DialogResult = DialogResult.OK;
                Close();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                errorLabel.Text = ex.Message;
            }
            finally
            {
                submitBtn.Enabled = true;
            }
        }

        private void ShowPickCustomerStep()
        {
            customerPickPanel.Visible = true;
            detailsPanel.Visible = false;
            cancelBtn.Visible = true;
            nextBtn.Visible = true;
            backBtn.Visible = false;
            submitBtn.Visible = false;
            stepSubtitleLabel.Text = "Step 1 of 2 — Find Customer";
        }

        private void ShowDetailsStep()
        {
            customerPickPanel.Visible = false;
            detailsPanel.Visible = true;
            cancelBtn.Visible = false; // step 2 offers Back instead — Cancel would just duplicate it
            nextBtn.Visible = false;
            backBtn.Visible = true;
            submitBtn.Visible = true;
            stepSubtitleLabel.Text = "Step 2 of 2 — Feedback Details";
        }
    }
}
```

Yes — that's the search's actual behavior. It's not a bug in the code we just wrote; it's how the search endpoint is designed.

Look at the API's `GetCustomers` filter in `CustomerController.cs`:

```csharp
query = query.Where(c =>
    (c.FirstName + " " + c.LastName).Contains(term) ||
    c.ContactNumber.Contains(term) ||
    c.CustomerId.ToString() == term);
```

That's an **OR**. So searching "3" matches any customer whose:

- Name contains "3" (nobody)
- **Contact number contains "3"** ← this is what's happening
- CustomerId is exactly "3"

Your seeded customers have phone numbers like `09171110001`, `09171110002`, `09171110003` — wait, those actually all end in different digits. Hmm.

Let me look at what you actually seeded. From your earlier screenshot, the customers are:

- Janjan Lascuna — 09171110001
- Pids Celendro — 09171110002
- Mina San — 09171110003
- Join Relove — 09171110004
- Jhon Themasc — 09171110005

If you searched "3", the phone filter `ContactNumber.Contains("3")` matches **none** of these (all contain `0917111000X` where X is 1-5 — so "3" appears in... actually none of them have "3" in the visible digits). Hmm.

Wait — did you change the phone numbers? Or do you have different customers?

**Actually, I need to see which two customers showed up when you searched "3".** That'll tell me exactly which filter matched them.

But the **behavior** is what I described: the search is an OR across name/phone/ID, so "3" can match by phone even if the exact ID "3" is a different customer.

---

## The question: what do you want the search to do?

Three possibilities:

**Option A — exact ID match first, then fall back to contains-search.** If "3" is a valid CustomerId, return only that customer. Only if no exact ID match, do a name/phone contains-search.

**Option B — exact ID match only, no contains on ID.** If the search term is all digits AND a customer with that exact ID exists, return only that one. Otherwise, do name/phone contains. (This is essentially Option A.)

**Option C — current behavior: OR everything.** Which means "3" matches any customer whose phone contains "3". This is what you have.

---

## My recommendation: Option A

If the user types something that looks like an ID (all digits, short), and there's an exact ID match, **return only that customer**. Otherwise fall back to the fuzzy search.

Concretely, change `CustomerController.GetCustomers` to:

```csharp
if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(search))
{
    var term = search.Trim();

    // If the term is a plain integer and matches an exact CustomerId, return just that one.
    if (int.TryParse(term, out var exactId))
    {
        var exactMatch = await tenant.Customers
            .AsNoTracking()
            .Where(c => c.CustomerId == exactId && c.IsActive)
            .Select(c => new CustomerResponseDto { /* ... */ })
            .ToListAsync();

        if (exactMatch.Any())
            return Ok(exactMatch);
    }

    // Otherwise, fall back to fuzzy name/phone/ID search.
    query = query.Where(c =>
        (c.FirstName + " " + c.LastName).Contains(term) ||
        c.ContactNumber.Contains(term) ||
        c.CustomerId.ToString() == term);
}
```

**Effect:** search "3" → if customer 3 exists, return only them. Search "Juan" → no exact ID match, falls through to fuzzy. Search "0917" → falls through to fuzzy (matches by phone).

---

## But there's another question: what does the POS customer-search do?

The POS uses `/customers/find` (single-result), which already does **ID first, then phone**. That's Option A behavior. So the POS is fine.

It's the **Customers tab grid** search (`/customers?search=...`) that's the fuzzy one. That's what you're hitting.

**Do you want the grid search to behave like the POS search (exact ID first), or leave it as fuzzy?**

- **Exact-ID-first** — predictable, "search 3 = customer 3". Recommended.
- **Fuzzy** — current. Searching "3" can match by phone, which is what surprised you.

**Tell me which you prefer and I'll write the fix.** Or paste the two customers that came back when you searched "3" — that'll confirm which filter matched them, and whether it's the phone filter or something else.

Got it — that's the same "single-row auto-select" issue we hit on the Customers tab. It's a WinForms DataGridView behavior, not a bug in our code: when the grid has exactly one row, WinForms sets it as `CurrentRow` automatically, so `SelectionChanged` fires and the row paints as selected. Clicking it produces no event because it's already the current row.

Same fix pattern as the Customers tab: **decide whether you want the row auto-selected on load or not, and handle it explicitly.**

---

## If you want it to load with NO row selected (so you can click it)

In `FeedbackManagementView.ReloadTicketsAsync()`, after binding the data source, clear the auto-selection:

```csharp
private async Task ReloadTicketsAsync()
{
    var previousId = _selectedTicket?.TicketId;
    var tickets = await _controller.GetTicketsAsync(searchTxtBx.Text);
    _ticketsBindingSource.DataSource = tickets;

    // Clear any auto-selection so the user has to click a row to open the drawer.
    ticketsGrid.ClearSelection();
    ticketsGrid.CurrentCell = null;

    var stillPresent = previousId.HasValue
        ? tickets.FirstOrDefault(t => t.TicketId == previousId.Value)
        : null;

    if (stillPresent != null)
    {
        SelectTicketRowById(stillPresent.TicketId);
    }
    else
    {
        _selectedTicket = null;
        RefreshDrawer();
    }
}
```

**Result:** grid loads with nothing highlighted, drawer shows the empty state. You click the row → drawer populates. Same behavior you now have on Customers (assuming you applied the same fix there).

**Caveat:** `ticketsGrid.CurrentCell = null;` sometimes throws if the grid isn't in a state where a null current cell is allowed. If it errors, the fix is:

```csharp
try { ticketsGrid.CurrentCell = null; } catch { /* ignore */ }
```

Or just drop the `CurrentCell = null` line and keep `ClearSelection()` — that clears the highlight but might leave a hidden current row. Try the full version first.

---

## If you want it to auto-select the first row (drawer populated on load)

That's the earlier behavior on Customers — you said it "accidentally also shows the approve request" there, which is now fixed. If you want the Feedback drawer to auto-populate with the first ticket, use:

```csharp
private async Task ReloadTicketsAsync()
{
    var previousId = _selectedTicket?.TicketId;
    var tickets = await _controller.GetTicketsAsync(searchTxtBx.Text);
    _ticketsBindingSource.DataSource = tickets;

    var stillPresent = previousId.HasValue
        ? tickets.FirstOrDefault(t => t.TicketId == previousId.Value)
        : null;

    if (stillPresent != null)
    {
        SelectTicketRowById(stillPresent.TicketId);
    }
    else if (tickets.Count > 0)
    {
        SelectTicketRowById(tickets[0].TicketId);
    }
    else
    {
        _selectedTicket = null;
        RefreshDrawer();
    }
}
```

**But confirm:** on the Customers tab, which behavior did you end up with? The last I saw, we changed it to auto-select the first row (so the drawer populates on landing). If you want **Consistency** between the two tabs, tell me which behavior you prefer for both, and I'll make sure they match.

- **Feedback tab:** no auto-select. Users click a ticket to see details. Empty drawer on landing is fine.
- **Customers tab:** no auto-select. Users click a customer to see details. Empty drawer on landing is fine.

## Edit 1 — `FeedbackManagementView.cs`

Find `ReloadTicketsAsync()` and replace it with:

```csharp
private async Task ReloadTicketsAsync()
{
    var previousId = _selectedTicket?.TicketId;
    var tickets = await _controller.GetTicketsAsync(searchTxtBx.Text);
    _ticketsBindingSource.DataSource = tickets;

    // Clear any auto-selection so the user has to click a row to open the drawer.
    // WinForms auto-selects the single row when the grid has exactly one, which
    // otherwise makes that row feel "already clicked" and unresponsive.
    ticketsGrid.ClearSelection();
    try { ticketsGrid.CurrentCell = null; } catch { /* not always allowed; ignore */ }

    var stillPresent = previousId.HasValue
        ? tickets.FirstOrDefault(t => t.TicketId == previousId.Value)
        : null;

    if (stillPresent != null)
    {
        SelectTicketRowById(stillPresent.TicketId);
    }
    else
    {
        _selectedTicket = null;
        RefreshDrawer();
    }
}
```

**What changed:** added the `ClearSelection()` + `CurrentCell = null` lines right after binding the data source. That kills the auto-select.

---

## Edit 2 — `CustomerManagementView.cs`

Find `ReloadCustomersAsync()` and replace it with:

```csharp
private async Task ReloadCustomersAsync()
{
    var previousId = _selectedCustomer?.CustomerId;
    var results = await _controller.SearchAsync(searchTxtBx.Text);
    _customersBindingSource.DataSource = results;

    // Clear any auto-selection so the user has to click a row to open the drawer.
    // WinForms auto-selects the single row when the grid has exactly one, which
    // otherwise makes that row feel "already clicked" and unresponsive.
    customersGrid.ClearSelection();
    try { customersGrid.CurrentCell = null; } catch { /* not always allowed; ignore */ }

    var stillPresent = previousId.HasValue
        ? results.FirstOrDefault(c => c.CustomerId == previousId.Value)
        : null;

    if (stillPresent != null)
    {
        SelectCustomerRowById(stillPresent.CustomerId);
    }
    else
    {
        _selectedCustomer = null;
        await RefreshDrawerAsync();
    }
}
```

**Note:** this drops the "select first row on load" behavior we added earlier (`else if (results.Count > 0) SelectCustomerRowById(results[0].CustomerId);`). Now the grid loads with no selection, drawer shows the empty state, and clicking a row opens it. That's what you asked for.

**One behavior change to be aware of:** the auto-selection we added earlier was there because you said "the profile itself doesn't load when I log in the landing page." With this change, **the drawer will be empty on landing** and only populate on click. That's the intentional trade-off — you get clickability of single rows, at the cost of no auto-populated drawer. If it turns out you want the drawer populated on landing again, tell me and we'll find a middle ground (e.g., keep auto-select but add a "click anywhere on the row to refresh" handler).

---

## If `CurrentCell = null` throws anyway

I wrapped it in try/catch, so even if the grid state doesn't allow it, the app won't crash. If the try/catch is what makes the build feel wrong (e.g., linter complains), swap it for a simpler form:

```csharp
customersGrid.ClearSelection();
```

Just the clear-selection alone often suffices — it removes the visual highlight even if the grid still considers a row "current." Test it, and if a single row still shows the highlight, keep the try/catch version.

## Before we start

**Two things to confirm:**

**1.** Have you set the build actions on the 20 JPGs (`Content` / `Copy if newer`)? If not, do that first — otherwise the images won't be present in the app's output directory when it runs, and the `ProductCardControl` won't find them.

**2.** The `TransactionController` currently takes `IProductCatalogService` in its constructor, and `TransactionView` calls `_catalogService.GetCategories()`, `_catalogService.GetProducts()`, `_catalogService.GetByCategory()`, `_catalogService.GetModifiers()` synchronously. Migrating to the API means those become **async fetches at construction time**, stored as lists.

Concretely: `TransactionView` will fetch the full product catalog **once** when it loads (or when a customer is selected) via `ProductApi`, cache it in memory, and pass it to `TransactionController`. That way the cart operations (which are synchronous) can still filter/search locally without hitting the API on every keystroke.

**Is that acceptable?** The alternative is calling the API on every product search / category filter change — which is slower but always fresh. My recommendation is the **fetch-once, cache** approach — matches how the current mock works and keeps the POS responsive.

**Confirm both, and I'll start with the API side.**

# File 4 — `CRM_Morcaffein.api/Controllers/ProductController.cs`

```csharp
using CRM_Morcaffein.api.DTOs;
using CRM_Morcaffein.infrastructure.services;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.api.Controllers
{
    [ApiController]
    [Route("api/tenant/{companyId:int}/products")]
    public class ProductController : ControllerBase
    {
        private readonly ITenantDbContextFactory _tenantFactory;

        public ProductController(ITenantDbContextFactory tenantFactory)
        {
            _tenantFactory = tenantFactory;
        }

        // GET api/tenant/{companyId}/products
        // Returns all active, available products with their sizes nested.
        [HttpGet]
        public async Task<ActionResult<List<ProductResponseDto>>> GetProducts(int companyId)
        {
            await using var tenant = await _tenantFactory.CreateAsync(companyId);

            var products = await tenant.Products
                .AsNoTracking()
                .Where(p => p.IsActive && p.IsAvailable)
                .OrderBy(p => p.ProductId)
                .Select(p => new ProductResponseDto
                {
                    ProductId = p.ProductId,
                    ProductCode = p.ProductCode,
                    ProductName = p.ProductName,
                    ProductCategory = p.ProductCategory,
                    BasePrice = p.BasePrice,
                    ImageUrl = p.ImageUrl,
                    LocalImagePath = p.LocalImagePath,
                    IsAvailable = p.IsAvailable,
                    Sizes = p.ProductSizes
                        .Where(s => s.IsActive)
                        .OrderBy(s => s.Price)
                        .Select(s => new ProductSizeResponseDto
                        {
                            ProductSizeId = s.ProductSizeId,
                            SizeName = s.SizeName,
                            Price = s.Price
                        })
                        .ToList()
                })
                .ToListAsync();

            return Ok(products);
        }

        // GET api/tenant/{companyId}/products/{id}
        [HttpGet("{id:int}")]
        public async Task<ActionResult<ProductResponseDto>> GetProduct(int companyId, int id)
        {
            await using var tenant = await _tenantFactory.CreateAsync(companyId);

            var product = await tenant.Products
                .AsNoTracking()
                .Where(p => p.ProductId == id)
                .Select(p => new ProductResponseDto
                {
                    ProductId = p.ProductId,
                    ProductCode = p.ProductCode,
                    ProductName = p.ProductName,
                    ProductCategory = p.ProductCategory,
                    BasePrice = p.BasePrice,
                    ImageUrl = p.ImageUrl,
                    LocalImagePath = p.LocalImagePath,
                    IsAvailable = p.IsAvailable,
                    Sizes = p.ProductSizes
                        .Where(s => s.IsActive)
                        .OrderBy(s => s.Price)
                        .Select(s => new ProductSizeResponseDto
                        {
                            ProductSizeId = s.ProductSizeId,
                            SizeName = s.SizeName,
                            Price = s.Price
                        })
                        .ToList()
                })
                .FirstOrDefaultAsync();

            if (product is null)
                return NotFound();

            return Ok(product);
        }

        // GET api/tenant/{companyId}/products/categories
        // Returns distinct categories as a plain list of strings.
        [HttpGet("categories")]
        public async Task<ActionResult<List<string>>> GetCategories(int companyId)
        {
            await using var tenant = await _tenantFactory.CreateAsync(companyId);

            var categories = await tenant.Products
                .AsNoTracking()
                .Where(p => p.IsActive && p.IsAvailable)
                .Select(p => p.ProductCategory)
                .Distinct()
                .OrderBy(c => c)
                .ToListAsync();

            return Ok(categories);
        }

        // GET api/tenant/{companyId}/products/modifiers
        // Returns all active product modifiers (the add-ons checklist).
        [HttpGet("modifiers")]
        public async Task<ActionResult<List<ProductModifierResponseDto>>> GetModifiers(int companyId)
        {
            await using var tenant = await _tenantFactory.CreateAsync(companyId);

            var modifiers = await tenant.ProductModifiers
                .AsNoTracking()
                .Where(m => m.IsActive)
                .OrderBy(m => m.ProductModifierId)
                .Select(m => new ProductModifierResponseDto
                {
                    ProductModifierId = m.ProductModifierId,
                    Name = m.Name,
                    Category = m.Category,
                    Price = m.Price
                })
                .ToListAsync();

            return Ok(modifiers);
        }
    }
}
```

**Notes:**

- Four endpoints: `GetProducts` (with nested sizes), `GetProduct` (single), `GetCategories`, `GetModifiers`.
- **Route ordering matters:** `[HttpGet("categories")]` and `[HttpGet("modifiers")]` are declared *after* `[HttpGet("{id:int}")]`, but because the `{id:int}` route is constrained to ints, "categories" and "modifiers" won't be mistaken for IDs. If you got a routing conflict (you shouldn't), reordering would fix it — but the `:int` constraint handles it.
- Sizes are ordered by price ascending, so Regular comes before Large before XL. Good for the card.

# File 5 — `CRM_Morcaffein.winforms/Services/Api/ProductApi.cs`

```csharp
using System.Net.Http.Json;
using CRM_Morcaffein.api.DTOs;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.winforms.Services.Api
{
    public class ProductApi
    {
        private readonly HttpClient _http;

        public ProductApi()
        {
            _http = new HttpClient { BaseAddress = new Uri(ApiConfig.BaseUrl) };
        }

        // GET api/tenant/{companyId}/products
        public async Task<List<ProductResponseDto>> GetProductsAsync()
        {
            var response = await _http.GetAsync($"api/tenant/{ApiConfig.CompanyId}/products");
            await EnsureSuccess(response);
            var result = await response.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync<List<ProductResponseDto>>();
            return result ?? new List<ProductResponseDto>();
        }

        // GET api/tenant/{companyId}/products/{id}
        public async Task<ProductResponseDto?> GetProductAsync(int productId)
        {
            var response = await _http.GetAsync($"api/tenant/{ApiConfig.CompanyId}/products/{productId}");
            if (response.StatusCode == System.Net.HttpStatusCode.NotFound)
                return null;
            await EnsureSuccess(response);
            return await response.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync<ProductResponseDto>();
        }

        // GET api/tenant/{companyId}/products/categories
        public async Task<List<string>> GetCategoriesAsync()
        {
            var response = await _http.GetAsync($"api/tenant/{ApiConfig.CompanyId}/products/categories");
            await EnsureSuccess(response);
            var result = await response.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync<List<string>>();
            return result ?? new List<string>();
        }

        // GET api/tenant/{companyId}/products/modifiers
        public async Task<List<ProductModifierResponseDto>> GetModifiersAsync()
        {
            var response = await _http.GetAsync($"api/tenant/{ApiConfig.CompanyId}/products/modifiers");
            await EnsureSuccess(response);
            var result = await response.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync<List<ProductModifierResponseDto>>();
            return result ?? new List<ProductModifierResponseDto>();
        }

        private static async Task EnsureSuccess(HttpResponseMessage response)
        {
            if (response.IsSuccessStatusCode) return;
            var body = await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync();
            throw new InvalidOperationException(
                string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(body)
                    ? $"API returned {(int)response.StatusCode}."
                    : body);
        }
    }
}
```

## The bigger shape of what's coming

Before the next files, let me lay out how the **fetch-once, cache** approach actually changes `TransactionController` and `TransactionView`, because it's a bit different from the previous migrations.

**Current state:**

- `TransactionController` takes `IProductCatalogService` (mock) and calls `_catalogService.GetProducts()`, `GetByCategory()`, `GetCategories()`, `GetModifiers()` synchronously.

**Target state:**

- `TransactionController` takes **pre-fetched lists** — `IReadOnlyList<Product> allProducts`, `IReadOnlyList<string> categories`, `IReadOnlyList<ProductModifier> modifiers` — as constructor params.
- `TransactionView` fetches these from `ProductApi` **once** (on first customer selection, or on control load), converts the DTOs into the domain entities the controller wants, and caches them.
- `TransactionController.GetProducts(category, search)` filters the cached list — no network call. Same as the current mock behavior.
- `TransactionController.GetModifiers()` returns the cached modifier list.

**Why this works:** the POS is a "single counter" — the catalog doesn't change mid-shift. Fetching once at sale-start and caching is the right trade-off. If the catalog ever changes mid-shift, the app would need a restart or a manual refresh — acceptable for this project.

**What I need to decide before writing File 6:**

`TransactionController` currently works with **domain entities** (`Product`, `ProductSize`, `ProductModifier`) — the cart stores them, `FrmItemCustomizer` receives `IReadOnlyList<ProductModifier>`, etc. If we change the controller to take DTOs instead, we'd have to change the whole cart pipeline to work with DTOs, which is a bigger refactor.

**The simpler path:** `TransactionView` fetches DTOs from the API, converts them to domain entities once, and passes the entity lists to `TransactionController`. **The controller doesn't change shape at all** — it still takes `IProductCatalogService` OR it takes pre-fetched entity lists. Everything downstream (cart, customizer, cart line) keeps working with entities.

**So File 6 will be:**

1. **`ProductApi`** (done — File 5 above)
2. **`TransactionView`** — fetch products/categories/modifiers/modifiers from `ProductApi` once, convert DTOs → entities, cache them
3. **`TransactionController`** — replace `IProductCatalogService` with three pre-fetched lists (`allProducts`, `categories`, `modifiers`)
4. **`ProductCardControl`** — load images from `LocalImagePath` (relative to the app's working directory)
5. **Delete** `IProductCatalogService`, `MockProductCatalogService`

**One question before File 6:** the cache lives in `TransactionView`, and it re-fetches every time the customer search finds a new customer (or every time the view loads). **Which do you want?**

- **(A) Fetch once per app session** — the view loads the catalog on first construction, keeps it for the whole app life. Fast, but if you edit a product in the DB you'd need to restart the app.
- **(B) Fetch once per transaction** — the view re-fetches the catalog every time a new customer is selected. Slower (one HTTP call per sale-start), but always fresh.

**My recommendation: (A) fetch once per app session.** The catalog is static; refetching on every customer selection adds latency for zero benefit. Cache it as a static field or a lazy-loaded property on the view, so it survives view re-creations (the view is rebuilt every time you click the Transactions nav).

**Which do you want?** Say (A) or (B) and I'll write File 6 accordingly.

Good — A, and it fetches from the DB via the API (not the mock). The mock catalog is what we're deleting.

To make "fetch once for the app session" work when the view is re-created every time you click the Transactions nav, the cache needs to live **outside the view** — otherwise every navigation re-fetches. I'll put it in a small static class.

# File 6 — `CRM_Morcaffein.winforms/Services/Api/ProductCatalogCache.cs`

```csharp
using CRM_Morcaffein.api.DTOs;
using CRM_Morcaffein.winforms.Services.Api;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.winforms.Services
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Session-scoped cache of the product catalog. Fetched once from the API on first
    /// use, then held in memory for the rest of the app session — the Transactions view
    /// is re-created every time the user clicks the nav button, so a per-view cache
    /// would re-fetch on every navigation.
    ///
    /// To force a refresh (e.g., after editing the menu in the DB), restart the app or
    /// call Reset(). There's no automatic invalidation.
    /// </summary>
    public static class ProductCatalogCache
    {
        private static readonly SemaphoreSlim _lock = new(1, 1);

        private static List<ProductResponseDto>? _products;
        private static List<ProductModifierResponseDto>? _modifiers;
        private static List<string>? _categories;

        public static async Task<List<ProductResponseDto>> GetProductsAsync()
        {
            if (_products is not null) return _products;

            await _lock.WaitAsync();
            try
            {
                if (_products is null)
                {
                    var api = new ProductApi();
                    _products = await api.GetProductsAsync();
                }
                return _products;
            }
            finally { _lock.Release(); }
        }

        public static async Task<List<ProductModifierResponseDto>> GetModifiersAsync()
        {
            if (_modifiers is not null) return _modifiers;

            await _lock.WaitAsync();
            try
            {
                if (_modifiers is null)
                {
                    var api = new ProductApi();
                    _modifiers = await api.GetModifiersAsync();
                }
                return _modifiers;
            }
            finally { _lock.Release(); }
        }

        public static async Task<List<string>> GetCategoriesAsync()
        {
            if (_categories is not null) return _categories;

            await _lock.WaitAsync();
            try
            {
                if (_categories is null)
                {
                    var api = new ProductApi();
                    _categories = await api.GetCategoriesAsync();
                }
                return _categories;
            }
            finally { _lock.Release(); }
        }

        /// <summary>Drops the cache. Call if the product catalog changes at runtime.</summary>
        public static void Reset()
        {
            _products = null;
            _modifiers = null;
            _categories = null;
        }
    }
}
```

**Why the lock:** if two UI threads hit `GetProductsAsync` simultaneously before the cache is populated, both would fire HTTP requests. The semaphore ensures only one actually fetches; the other waits and returns the cached result.

**Why not `Lazy<T>`:** `Lazy<T>` doesn't play well with async without extra machinery, and the semaphore is clearer. Same idea.
