Replaces `IProductCatalogService` with pre-fetched entity lists.

```csharp
using CRM_Morcaffein.domain.entities;
using CRM_Morcaffein.Services;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.Controllers
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Controller for the Transactions/POS tab (MVC). One instance represents a single
    /// in-progress sale for one customer. Owns every business rule for the cart/promo/
    /// checkout flow — cart-item pricing, discount calculation, promo eligibility,
    /// points-earned math.
    ///
    /// Orders are still mock-backed via IOrderService until the Orders feature area
    /// migrates. Products, campaigns, and categories come in as pre-fetched lists from
    /// the View (which pulls them from the API once per session and caches them), because
    /// cart mutations are synchronous and can't await an HTTP call.
    /// </summary>
    public class TransactionController
    {
        private readonly IOrderService _orderService;
        private readonly IReadOnlyList<Product> _allProducts;
        private readonly IReadOnlyList<string> _categories;
        private readonly IReadOnlyList<ProductModifier> _modifiers;
        private readonly IReadOnlyList<Campaign> _activeCampaigns;

        public Order Order { get; private set; }
        public Customer Customer { get; private set; }

        public IReadOnlyList<string> Categories => _categories;

        public decimal SubTotal => Order.SubTotal;
        public decimal TotalDiscount => Order.TotalDiscount;
        public decimal TotalAmount => Order.TotalAmount;
        public bool HasItems => Order.OrderItems.Count > 0;
        public IReadOnlyList<OrderItem> CartItems => Order.OrderItems.ToList();

        public TransactionController(
            IOrderService orderService,
            IReadOnlyList<Product> allProducts,
            IReadOnlyList<string> categories,
            IReadOnlyList<ProductModifier> modifiers,
            IReadOnlyList<Campaign> activeCampaigns,
            Customer customer,
            int createdByEmployeeId)
        {
            _orderService = orderService;
            _allProducts = allProducts;
            _categories = categories;
            _modifiers = modifiers;
            _activeCampaigns = activeCampaigns;
            Customer = customer;
            Order = _orderService.StartOrder(customer.CustomerId, createdByEmployeeId);
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Re-points the SAME in-progress order at a different customer (Quick Register
        /// relink flow). Not used by the main POS flow — search-and-Go there starts a fresh
        /// Controller/Order instead (see TransactionView.SelectCustomerAsync).
        /// </summary>
        public void SwitchCustomer(Customer newCustomer)
        {
            Order = _orderService.LinkCustomerToOrder(Order, newCustomer);
            Customer = newCustomer;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Filters the cached product list by category and name search. No network call.
        /// </summary>
        public IReadOnlyList<Product> GetProducts(string category, string searchText)
        {
            IEnumerable<Product> products = string.IsNullOrEmpty(category)
                ? _allProducts
                : _allProducts.Where(p => p.ProductCategory.Equals(category, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));

            if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(searchText))
                products = products.Where(p => p.ProductName.Contains(searchText, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));

            return products.ToList();
        }

        public IReadOnlyList<ProductModifier> GetModifiers() => _modifiers;

        public void AddItemToCart(Product product, ProductSize size, int quantity, IEnumerable<ProductModifier> modifiers)
        {
            EnsurePending();
            if (quantity <= 0)
                throw new ArgumentException("Quantity must be greater than zero.");

            var existing = Order.OrderItems.FirstOrDefault(i => i.ProductSizeId == size.ProductSizeId);
            if (existing != null)
            {
                existing.Quantity += quantity;
                RecalculateItemPricing(existing);
            }
            else
            {
                var item = _orderService.CreateOrderItem(Order, product, size, quantity);
                foreach (var modifier in modifiers)
                    _orderService.AddModifierToItem(item, modifier);
                RecalculateItemPricing(item);
            }

            RecalculateOrderTotals();
        }

        public void UpdateCartItem(OrderItem item, ProductSize newSize, int newQuantity, IEnumerable<ProductModifier> newModifiers)
        {
            EnsurePending();
            if (newQuantity <= 0)
                throw new ArgumentException("Quantity must be greater than zero.");

            if (item.ProductSizeId == newSize.ProductSizeId)
            {
                item.Quantity = newQuantity;
                item.OrderItemModifiers.Clear();
                foreach (var modifier in newModifiers)
                    _orderService.AddModifierToItem(item, modifier);
                RecalculateItemPricing(item);
                RecalculateOrderTotals();
            }
            else
            {
                _orderService.RemoveOrderItem(Order, item);
                AddItemToCart(item.Product!, newSize, newQuantity, newModifiers);
            }
        }

        public void RemoveItem(OrderItem item)
        {
            _orderService.RemoveOrderItem(Order, item);
            RecalculateOrderTotals();
        }

        public IReadOnlyList<Campaign> GetEligiblePromos() =>
            _activeCampaigns.Where(c => CanRedeem(c, Customer, Order)).ToList();

        public void ApplyPromo(Campaign campaign)
        {
            EnsurePending();
            var discount = CalculateDiscount(campaign, Order.SubTotal);
            _orderService.CreateCampaignRedeem(Order, campaign, discount);
            RecalculateOrderTotals();
        }

        public void RemovePromo(Campaign campaign)
        {
            var redeem = Order.CampaignRedeems.FirstOrDefault(r => r.CampaignId == campaign.CampaignId);
            if (redeem is null) return;

            _orderService.RemoveCampaignRedeem(Order, redeem);
            RecalculateOrderTotals();
        }

        public void ClearPromos()
        {
            foreach (var redeem in Order.CampaignRedeems.ToList())
                _orderService.RemoveCampaignRedeem(Order, redeem);

            RecalculateOrderTotals();
        }

        public Order CompleteSale()
        {
            EnsurePending();
            if (Order.OrderItems.Count == 0)
                throw new InvalidOperationException("Order cannot be empty.");

            Order.Status = "Completed";
            Order.PointsEarned = (int)(Order.TotalAmount / 10m);

            if (Order.PointsEarned > 0)
            {
                Customer.PointsBalance += Order.PointsEarned;
                Customer.LastVisitDate = DateTime.UtcNow;
                Customer.PointLedgers.Add(new PointLedger
                {
                    CustomerId = Customer.CustomerId,
                    PointsChange = Order.PointsEarned,
                    Type = "Earned",
                    Reason = $"Order #{Order.OrderId} Spend",
                    OrderId = Order.OrderId,
                    Timestamp = DateTime.UtcNow,
                });
            }

            _orderService.CompleteOrder(Order);
            return Order;
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // BUSINESS RULES
        // =====================================================================

        private void EnsurePending()
        {
            if (!Order.Status.Equals("Pending", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Order cannot be modified in '{Order.Status}' state.");
        }

        private static void RecalculateItemPricing(OrderItem item)
        {
            item.UnitPrice = item.BaseSizePrice + item.OrderItemModifiers.Sum(m => m.UnitPrice);
            item.SubTotal = item.Quantity * item.UnitPrice;
        }

        private void RecalculateOrderTotals()
        {
            Order.SubTotal = Order.OrderItems.Sum(i => i.SubTotal);

            decimal totalDiscount = 0m;
            foreach (var redeem in Order.CampaignRedeems)
            {
                var campaign = redeem.Campaign ?? _activeCampaigns.FirstOrDefault(c => c.CampaignId == redeem.CampaignId);
                var discount = campaign != null ? CalculateDiscount(campaign, Order.SubTotal) : redeem.DiscountUsed;
                redeem.DiscountUsed = discount;
                totalDiscount += discount;
            }
            Order.TotalDiscount = totalDiscount;

            Order.TotalAmount = Math.Max(0m, Order.SubTotal - Order.TotalDiscount);
        }

        private static bool IsCurrentlyActive(Campaign campaign)
        {
            var now = DateTime.UtcNow;
            return campaign.IsActive && now >= campaign.StartDate && now <= campaign.EndDate;
        }

        private static bool CanRedeem(Campaign campaign, Customer customer, Order order)
        {
            if (!IsCurrentlyActive(campaign)) return false;

            if (campaign.MinPurchaseAmount.HasValue && order.SubTotal < campaign.MinPurchaseAmount.Value)
                return false;

            if (!campaign.TargetTier.Equals("All", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) &&
                !PointsToTier(customer.PointsBalance).Equals(campaign.TargetTier, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                return false;

            if (campaign.PromoCategory.Equals("Birthday", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) && !IsBirthdayToday(customer))
                return false;

            if (campaign.PromoCategory.Equals("Inactive", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) && !IsInactive(customer))
                return false;

            var previousRedemptions = campaign.CampaignRedeems.Count(r => r.Order != null && r.Order.CustomerId == customer.CustomerId);
            return previousRedemptions < campaign.MaxRedemptionsPerCustomer;
        }

        private static string PointsToTier(int pointsBalance) => pointsBalance switch
        {
            >= 500 => "Gold",
            >= 200 => "Silver",
            _ => "Regular",
        };

        private static bool IsBirthdayToday(Customer customer) =>
            customer.Birthday?.Month == DateTime.UtcNow.Month && customer.Birthday?.Day == DateTime.UtcNow.Day;

        private static bool IsInactive(Customer customer) => (DateTime.UtcNow - customer.LastVisitDate).Days > 20;

        private static decimal CalculateDiscount(Campaign campaign, decimal orderTotal)
        {
            if (orderTotal <= 0) return 0m;
            if (campaign.MinPurchaseAmount.HasValue && orderTotal < campaign.MinPurchaseAmount.Value) return 0m;

            decimal discount;
            if (campaign.DiscountType.Equals("Percentage", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
            {
                discount = orderTotal * (campaign.DiscountValue / 100m);
                if (campaign.MaxDiscountAmount.HasValue && discount > campaign.MaxDiscountAmount.Value)
                    discount = campaign.MaxDiscountAmount.Value;
            }
            else
            {
                discount = campaign.DiscountValue;
            }

            return discount > orderTotal ? orderTotal : discount;
        }
    }
}
```

**What changed vs. previous:**

- Constructor now takes `IReadOnlyList<Product> allProducts`, `IReadOnlyList<string> categories`, `IReadOnlyList<ProductModifier> modifiers`, plus the campaign list. No more `IProductCatalogService`.
- `Categories` becomes a get-only property backed by the injected list.
- `GetProducts` filters the cached list.
- `GetModifiers` returns the cached list.

```csharp
            var payablesBox = BuildPayablesBox();
            var logSaleBox = BuildLogSaleBox();

            column.Controls.Add(orderBox);
            column.Controls.Add(payablesBox);
            column.Controls.Add(logSaleBox);

            return column;
        }

        private Panel BuildLogSaleBox()
        {
            var box = new Panel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Bottom,
                Height = 56,
                Margin = new Padding(10, 0, 10, 10),
                Padding = new Padding(10),
                BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle,
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
            };

            _logSaleBtn = new Button
            {
                Text = "Log Sale",
                Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat,
                BackColor = BrandPalette.ButtonPrimaryFill,
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.ButtonPrimaryText,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(10.5f),
                Enabled = false,
            };
            _logSaleBtn.FlatAppearance.BorderSize = 0;
            _logSaleBtn.Click += (s, e) => CompleteSale();
            ButtonStyler.TrackEnabledState(_logSaleBtn);

            box.Controls.Add(_logSaleBtn);
            return box;
        }

        private Panel BuildOrderBox()
        {
            var box = new Panel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                Margin = new Padding(0, 0, 0, 10),
                BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle,
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
            };

            var header = new Label
            {
                Text = "Order",
                Dock = DockStyle.Top,
                Height = 28,
                Padding = new Padding(10, 6, 0, 0),
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(10f),
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralText,
            };
            var divider = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Top, Height = 1, BackColor = BrandPalette.Border };

            _cartLinesPanel = new FlowLayoutPanel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                FlowDirection = FlowDirection.TopDown,
                WrapContents = false,
                AutoScroll = true,
                Padding = new Padding(8, 6, 8, 6),
            };

            _cartEmptyLabel = new Label
            {
                Text = "No items yet.\nTap a drink to add it.",
                Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleCenter,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(8.5f),
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralTextMuted,
            };
            _cartLinesPanel.Controls.Add(_cartEmptyLabel);

            box.Controls.Add(_cartLinesPanel);
            box.Controls.Add(divider);
            box.Controls.Add(header);

            return box;
        }

        private Panel BuildPayablesBox()
        {
            var box = new Panel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Bottom,
                Height = 254,
                Margin = new Padding(10, 0, 10, 10),
                BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle,
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
                Padding = new Padding(14, 12, 14, 12),
            };

            var header = new Label
            {
                Text = "Payables",
                Dock = DockStyle.Top,
                Height = 24,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(11.5f),
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralText,
            };

            _cartStatusLabel = new Label
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Top,
                Height = 20,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(8.5f),
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.StatusNegativeFill,
            };

            var summaryTable = new TableLayoutPanel { Dock = DockStyle.Fill, ColumnCount = 2, RowCount = 5 };
            summaryTable.ColumnStyles.Add(new ColumnStyle(SizeType.Percent, 55f));
            summaryTable.ColumnStyles.Add(new ColumnStyle(SizeType.Percent, 45f));

            Label MakeCaption(string text) => new() { Text = text, Dock = DockStyle.Fill, Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9.5f), ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralTextMuted, TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleLeft };
            Label MakeValue() => new() { Text = "₱0.00", Dock = DockStyle.Fill, Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(11f), ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralText, TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleRight };

            _subTotalValueLabel = MakeValue();
            _discountValueLabel = MakeValue();
            _vatValueLabel = MakeValue();
            _pwdSeniorValueLabel = MakeValue();
            _totalValueLabel = MakeValue();
            _totalValueLabel.ForeColor = BrandPalette.Brand;
            _totalValueLabel.Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(15f);

            summaryTable.Controls.Add(MakeCaption("Subtotal"), 0, 0);
            summaryTable.Controls.Add(_subTotalValueLabel, 1, 0);
            summaryTable.Controls.Add(MakeCaption("Discount"), 0, 1);
            summaryTable.Controls.Add(_discountValueLabel, 1, 1);
            summaryTable.Controls.Add(MakeCaption("VAT (12%)"), 0, 2);
            summaryTable.Controls.Add(_vatValueLabel, 1, 2);
            summaryTable.Controls.Add(MakeCaption("PWD/Senior Disc."), 0, 3);
            summaryTable.Controls.Add(_pwdSeniorValueLabel, 1, 3);
            summaryTable.Controls.Add(MakeCaption("Total"), 0, 4);
            summaryTable.Controls.Add(_totalValueLabel, 1, 4);

            box.Controls.Add(summaryTable);
            box.Controls.Add(_cartStatusLabel);
            box.Controls.Add(header);

            return box;
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // CATALOG LOADING (once per session via ProductCatalogCache)
        // =====================================================================

        private async Task EnsureCatalogLoadedAsync()
        {
            if (_cachedProducts is not null) return;

            var productDtos = await ProductCatalogCache.GetProductsAsync();
            var categoryList = await ProductCatalogCache.GetCategoriesAsync();
            var modifierDtos = await ProductCatalogCache.GetModifiersAsync();

            _cachedProducts = productDtos.Select(MapToProductEntity).ToList();
            _cachedCategories = categoryList;
            _cachedModifiers = modifierDtos.Select(MapToModifierEntity).ToList();
        }

        private static Product MapToProductEntity(ProductResponseDto dto)
        {
            var product = new Product
            {
                ProductId = dto.ProductId,
                ProductCode = dto.ProductCode,
                ProductName = dto.ProductName,
                ProductCategory = dto.ProductCategory,
                BasePrice = dto.BasePrice,
                ImageUrl = dto.ImageUrl,
                LocalImagePath = dto.LocalImagePath,
                IsAvailable = dto.IsAvailable,
            };

            foreach (var sizeDto in dto.Sizes)
            {
                product.ProductSizes.Add(new ProductSize
                {
                    ProductSizeId = sizeDto.ProductSizeId,
                    ProductId = dto.ProductId,
                    SizeName = sizeDto.SizeName,
                    Price = sizeDto.Price,
                });
            }

            return product;
        }

        private static ProductModifier MapToModifierEntity(ProductModifierResponseDto dto) => new()
        {
            ProductModifierId = dto.ProductModifierId,
            Name = dto.Name,
            Category = dto.Category,
            Price = dto.Price,
        };

        // =====================================================================
        // CUSTOMER SELECTION
        // =====================================================================

        private async void RunCustomerSearch()
        {
            var query = _customerSearchTxtBx.Text.Trim();
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(query))
                return;

            try
            {
                var customerApi = new CustomerApi();
                var match = await customerApi.FindCustomerAsync(query);

                if (match is null)
                {
                    _customerSearchErrorLabel.Text = $"No customer found for \"{query}\".";
                    _customerProfilePanel.Visible = false;
                    return;
                }

                _customerSearchErrorLabel.Text = string.Empty;
                ShowCustomerProfile(match);
                await SelectCustomerAsync(match);
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                _customerSearchErrorLabel.Text = ex.Message;
                _customerProfilePanel.Visible = false;
            }
        }

        private void ShowCustomerProfile(CustomerResponseDto customer)
        {
            _customerProfileNameLabel.Text = customer.FullName;
            _customerProfileDetailLabel.Text = $"{customer.Tier} Tier   •   {customer.PointsBalance} pts\n{customer.ContactNumber}";
            _customerProfilePanel.Visible = true;
        }

        private async Task SelectCustomerAsync(CustomerResponseDto dto)
        {
            var employeeId = EmployeeSession.Current?.EmployeeId
                ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("No employee session — the Transaction view requires a logged-in employee.");

            if (_controller is not null && _controller.CartItems.Count > 0)
            {
                var currentCustomerName = _controller.Customer.FullName;
                var confirm = MessageBox.Show(
                    FindForm(),
                    $"Discard the in-progress order for {currentCustomerName} and start a new one for {dto.FullName}?",
                    "Start New Transaction",
                    MessageBoxButtons.YesNo,
                    MessageBoxIcon.Warning);

                if (confirm != DialogResult.Yes)
                {
                    _customerSearchTxtBx.Text = _controller.Customer.CustomerId.ToString();
                    return;
                }
            }

            try
            {
                // Load catalog once per session
                await EnsureCatalogLoadedAsync();

                // Convert DTO -> entity for the still-mock-backed TransactionController
                var entity = new Customer
                {
                    CustomerId = dto.CustomerId,
                    FirstName = dto.FirstName,
                    LastName = dto.LastName,
                    ContactNumber = dto.ContactNumber,
                    Email = dto.Email,
                    Birthday = dto.Birthday,
                    LastVisitDate = dto.LastVisitDate,
                    PointsBalance = dto.PointsBalance,
                    IsActive = dto.IsActive,
                };

                // Fetch campaigns from the API
                var campaignApi = new CampaignApi();
                var campaignDtos = await campaignApi.GetActiveCampaignsAsync();
                var campaigns = campaignDtos.Select(MapToCampaignEntity).ToList();

                _controller = new TransactionController(
                    _orderService,
                    _cachedProducts!,
                    _cachedCategories!,
                    _cachedModifiers!,
                    campaigns,
                    entity,
                    employeeId);

                BuildCategoryOptions();
                RefreshProductsPanel();
                RefreshCartLines();
                RefreshSummary();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                _customerSearchErrorLabel.Text = ex.Message;
                _customerProfilePanel.Visible = false;
            }
        }

        private static Campaign MapToCampaignEntity(CampaignResponseDto dto) => new()
        {
            CampaignId = dto.CampaignId,
            PromoName = dto.PromoName,
            PromoCategory = dto.PromoCategory,
            DiscountType = dto.DiscountType,
            DiscountValue = dto.DiscountValue,
            TargetTier = dto.TargetTier,
            MinPurchaseAmount = dto.MinPurchaseAmount,
            MaxDiscountAmount = dto.MaxDiscountAmount,
            MaxRedemptionsPerCustomer = dto.MaxRedemptionsPerCustomer,
            StartDate = dto.StartDate,
            EndDate = dto.EndDate,
            IsActive = dto.IsActive,
        };

        // =====================================================================
        // PROMO
        // =====================================================================

        private void ShowPromoMenu()
        {
            if (_controller is null)
                return;

            var menu = new ContextMenuStrip();

            if (_controller.Order.CampaignRedeems.Count > 0)
            {
                var clear = menu.Items.Add("Clear applied promo");
                clear.Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(9f);
                clear.Click += (s, e) =>
                {
                    _controller.ClearPromos();
                    RefreshSummary();
                    RefreshPromoButton();
                };
                menu.Items.Add(new ToolStripSeparator());
            }

            var eligiblePromos = _controller.GetEligiblePromos();
            if (eligiblePromos.Count == 0)
            {
                var none = menu.Items.Add("No promos available for this order");
                none.Enabled = false;
            }
            else
            {
                foreach (var campaign in eligiblePromos)
                {
                    var alreadyApplied = _controller.Order.CampaignRedeems
                        .Any(r => r.CampaignId == campaign.CampaignId);

                    var label = campaign.DiscountType == "Percentage"
                        ? $"{campaign.PromoName} — {campaign.DiscountValue:0.##}% off"
                        : $"{campaign.PromoName} — ₱{campaign.DiscountValue:0.##} off";
                    if (alreadyApplied)
                        label += "  (applied)";

                    var item = menu.Items.Add(label);
                    item.Enabled = !alreadyApplied;
                    item.Click += (s, e) =>
                    {
                        try
                        {
                            _controller.ApplyPromo(campaign);
                            RefreshSummary();
                            RefreshPromoButton();
                        }
                        catch (Exception ex)
                        {
                            ShowCartStatus(ex.Message);
                        }
                    };
                }
            }

            menu.Show(_promoMenuBtn, new Point(0, -menu.PreferredSize.Height));
        }

        private void RefreshPromoButton()
        {
            if (_controller is null)
            {
                _promoMenuBtn.Text = "Select a Promo ▾";
                _promoMenuBtn.Enabled = false;
                return;
            }

            var applied = _controller.Order.CampaignRedeems.FirstOrDefault();

            if (applied is null)
            {
                _promoMenuBtn.Text = "Select a Promo ▾";
            }
            else
            {
                var campaign = _controller.GetEligiblePromos()
                                   .FirstOrDefault(c => c.CampaignId == applied.CampaignId);

                var name = campaign?.PromoName ?? $"Promo #{applied.CampaignId}";
                _promoMenuBtn.Text = $"{name} ▾";
            }

            _promoMenuBtn.Enabled = true;
        }

        private void RefreshSummary()
        {
            RefreshPromoButton();

            if (_controller is null)
            {
                _subTotalValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
                _discountValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
                _vatValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
                _pwdSeniorValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
                _totalValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
                _logSaleBtn.Enabled = false;
                return;
            }

            _subTotalValueLabel.Text = $"₱{_controller.SubTotal:0.00}";
            _discountValueLabel.Text = $"₱{_controller.TotalDiscount:0.00}";
            _vatValueLabel.Text = $"₱{_controller.TotalAmount * VatRate:0.00}";
            _pwdSeniorValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
            _totalValueLabel.Text = $"₱{_controller.TotalAmount:0.00}";
            _logSaleBtn.Enabled = _controller.HasItems;
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // DRINKS / CART
        // =====================================================================

        private void BuildCategoryOptions()
        {
            if (_cachedCategories is null) return;

            _categoryCombo.Items.Clear();
            _categoryCombo.Items.Add(AllCategoriesOption);
            foreach (var category in _cachedCategories)
                _categoryCombo.Items.Add(category);
            _categoryCombo.SelectedIndex = 0;
        }

        private void RefreshProductsPanel()
        {
            _productsFlowPanel.Controls.Clear();
            if (_controller is null) return;

            var products = _controller.GetProducts(_selectedCategory, _productSearchTxtBx.Text);
            foreach (var product in products)
            {
                var card = new ProductCardControl(product);
                card.CardClicked += (s, e) => OpenCustomizerForNewItem(product);
                card.SizeQuickAdded += (s, size) => QuickAddToCart(product, size);
                _productsFlowPanel.Controls.Add(card);
            }
        }

        private void QuickAddToCart(Product product, ProductSize size)
        {
            if (_controller is null)
            {
                ShowCartStatus("Pick a customer on the left first.");
                return;
            }

            try
            {
                _controller.AddItemToCart(product, size, 1, Enumerable.Empty<ProductModifier>());
                RefreshCartLines();
                RefreshSummary();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                ShowCartStatus(ex.Message);
            }
        }

        private void OpenCustomizerForNewItem(Product product)
        {
            if (_controller is null)
            {
                ShowCartStatus("Pick a customer on the left first.");
                return;
            }

            using var form = new FrmItemCustomizer(product, _controller.GetModifiers());

            if (form.ShowDialog(FindForm()) == DialogResult.OK)
            {
                try
                {
                    _controller.AddItemToCart(product, form.SelectedSize, form.Quantity, form.SelectedModifiers);
                    RefreshCartLines();
                    RefreshSummary();
                }
                catch (Exception ex)
                {
                    ShowCartStatus(ex.Message);
                }
            }
        }

        private void RefreshCartLines()
        {
            _cartLinesPanel.Controls.Clear();

            if (_controller is null || _controller.CartItems.Count == 0)
            {
                _cartLinesPanel.Controls.Add(_cartEmptyLabel);
                return;
            }

            var lineWidth = Math.Max(200,
                _cartLinesPanel.ClientSize.Width - SystemInformation.VerticalScrollBarWidth - 8);

            foreach (var item in _controller.CartItems)
            {
                var line = new CartLineControl(item) { Width = lineWidth };
                line.QuantityIncreased += (s, e) => ChangeQuantity(item, +1);
                line.QuantityDecreased += (s, e) => ChangeQuantity(item, -1);
                line.RemoveClicked += (s, e) => RemoveFromCart(item);
                _cartLinesPanel.Controls.Add(line);
            }
        }

        private void RemoveFromCart(OrderItem item)
        {
            if (_controller is null) return;

            _controller.RemoveItem(item);
            RefreshCartLines();
            RefreshSummary();
        }

        private void ChangeQuantity(OrderItem item, int delta)
        {
            if (_controller is null || item.Product is null) return;

            var newQuantity = item.Quantity + delta;
            if (newQuantity <= 0)
            {
                RemoveFromCart(item);
                return;
            }

            var size = item.Product.ProductSizes.First(s => s.ProductSizeId == item.ProductSizeId);
            var modifiers = _controller.GetModifiers()
                .Where(m => item.OrderItemModifiers.Any(om => om.ProductModifierId == m.ProductModifierId));

            try
            {
                _controller.UpdateCartItem(item, size, newQuantity, modifiers);
                RefreshCartLines();
                RefreshSummary();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                ShowCartStatus(ex.Message);
            }
        }

        private void ShowCartStatus(string message) => _cartStatusLabel.Text = message;

        private void CompleteSale()
        {
            if (_controller is null) return;

            try
            {
                var customerName = _controller.Customer.FullName;
                var order = _controller.CompleteSale();

                MessageBox.Show(FindForm(),
                    $"Sale completed. {order.PointsEarned} points awarded to {customerName}.",
                    "Sale Complete", MessageBoxButtons.OK, MessageBoxIcon.Information);

                _controller = null;
                _customerProfilePanel.Visible = false;
                _customerSearchErrorLabel.Text = string.Empty;
                _customerSearchTxtBx.Text = string.Empty;
                RefreshProductsPanel();
                RefreshCartLines();
                RefreshSummary();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                ShowCartStatus(ex.Message);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

**Key changes vs. the last version:**

- Constructor now takes only `IOrderService` — no more `IProductCatalogService`.
- `BuildCategoryOptions()` no longer called in the constructor (categories come from the API asynchronously). It's called inside `SelectCustomerAsync` after the catalog loads.
- `EnsureCatalogLoadedAsync()` fetches products/categories/modifiers from `ProductCatalogCache` once and maps the DTOs into domain entities.
- `SelectCustomerAsync` calls `EnsureCatalogLoadedAsync()` first, then constructs the controller with the cached entity lists.
- Added `MapToProductEntity` and `MapToModifierEntity` helpers.
- `ProductCardControl` still receives `Product` entities — no change needed there for the data flow (image loading is File 9).

# File 9 — `CRM_Morcaffein.winforms/Views/Controls/ProductCardControl.cs` (full replacement)

Same card layout, but now loads the actual JPG from `LocalImagePath` (resolved relative to the app's base directory). Falls back to the "☕" placeholder glyph if the file is missing.

```csharp
using CRM_Morcaffein.domain.entities;
using CRM_Morcaffein.Theme;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.winforms.Views.Controls
{
    /// <summary>
    /// A single drink card: product image + name + "from ₱price", with a row of size
    /// quick-add buttons pinned to the bottom. Tapping a size button adds that size,
    /// qty 1, no modifiers, straight to the cart. Clicking the card body opens the full
    /// customizer modal instead.
    ///
    /// Image loading: reads Product.LocalImagePath (a path relative to the app's base
    /// directory, e.g. "Resources/Products/matchahc.jpg"). If the file is missing, draws
    /// the placeholder tint block + "☕" glyph instead.
    /// </summary>
    public class ProductCardControl : Panel
    {
        public Product Product { get; }

        public event EventHandler? CardClicked;
        public event EventHandler<ProductSize>? SizeQuickAdded;

        private const int SizeRowHeight = 26;
        private const int ImageBandHeight = 64;

        private static readonly string[] SizeLabels = { "S", "M", "L", "XL" };

        // Cached image so we're not re-reading from disk on every paint.
        private Image? _cachedImage;
        private bool _imageLoadAttempted;

        public ProductCardControl(Product product)
        {
            Product = product;
            Size = new Size(150, 156);
            Margin = new Padding(8);
            BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary;
            Cursor = Cursors.Hand;

            SetStyle(ControlStyles.UserPaint | ControlStyles.AllPaintingInWmPaint | ControlStyles.OptimizedDoubleBuffer, true);

            Click += (s, e) => CardClicked?.Invoke(this, EventArgs.Empty);
            MouseEnter += (s, e) => { BackColor = BrandPalette.Tint90; Invalidate(); };
            MouseLeave += (s, e) => { BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary; Invalidate(); };

            BuildSizeRow();
        }

        protected override void Dispose(bool disposing)
        {
            if (disposing)
            {
                _cachedImage?.Dispose();
                _cachedImage = null;
            }
            base.Dispose(disposing);
        }

        private void BuildSizeRow()
        {
            var sizes = Product.ProductSizes.ToList();
            if (sizes.Count == 0)
                return;

            var sizeRow = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Bottom, Height = SizeRowHeight, BackColor = BrandPalette.Brand };
            var buttonWidth = Width / sizes.Count;

            for (int i = 0; i < sizes.Count; i++)
            {
                var size = sizes[i];
                var btn = new Button
                {
                    Text = i < SizeLabels.Length ? SizeLabels[i] : (i + 1).ToString(),
                    Location = new Point(i * buttonWidth, 0),
                    Size = new Size(i == sizes.Count - 1 ? Width - i * buttonWidth : buttonWidth, SizeRowHeight),
                    FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat,
                    BackColor = BrandPalette.Brand,
                    ForeColor = BrandPalette.White,
                    Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(8f),
                    Cursor = Cursors.Hand,
                };
                btn.FlatAppearance.BorderSize = 0;
                btn.FlatAppearance.BorderColor = BrandPalette.White;
                btn.Click += (s, e) => SizeQuickAdded?.Invoke(this, size);
                sizeRow.Controls.Add(btn);
            }

            Controls.Add(sizeRow);
        }

        protected override void OnPaint(PaintEventArgs e)
        {
            base.OnPaint(e);
            var g = e.Graphics;
            g.SmoothingMode = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.SmoothingMode.AntiAlias;
            g.InterpolationMode = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.InterpolationMode.HighQualityBicubic;

            using var borderPen = new Pen(BrandPalette.Border);
            g.DrawRectangle(borderPen, 0, 0, Width - 1, Height - 1);

            var imageRect = new Rectangle(8, 8, Width - 16, ImageBandHeight);
            DrawProductImage(g, imageRect);

            using var nameFont = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(9.5f);
            var nameRect = new RectangleF(8, imageRect.Bottom + 6, Width - 16, 32);
            g.DrawString(Product.ProductName, nameFont, new SolidBrush(BrandPalette.NeutralText), nameRect);

            using var priceFont = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9f);
            g.DrawString($"from ₱{Product.BasePrice:0}", priceFont, new SolidBrush(BrandPalette.NeutralTextMuted),
                8, Height - SizeRowHeight - 20);
        }

        private void DrawProductImage(Graphics g, Rectangle imageRect)
        {
            // Lazy-load the image once, then reuse.
            if (!_imageLoadAttempted)
            {
                _imageLoadAttempted = true;
                _cachedImage = TryLoadImage(Product.LocalImagePath);
            }

            if (_cachedImage is not null)
            {
                // Fit the image to the image band while preserving aspect ratio, center it.
                var targetRatio = (float)imageRect.Width / imageRect.Height;
                var imageRatio = (float)_cachedImage.Width / _cachedImage.Height;

                int drawWidth, drawHeight;
                if (imageRatio > targetRatio)
                {
                    drawWidth = imageRect.Width;
                    drawHeight = (int)(imageRect.Width / imageRatio);
                }
                else
                {
                    drawHeight = imageRect.Height;
                    drawWidth = (int)(imageRect.Height * imageRatio);
                }

                var drawX = imageRect.X + (imageRect.Width - drawWidth) / 2;
                var drawY = imageRect.Y + (imageRect.Height - drawHeight) / 2;

                g.DrawImage(_cachedImage, drawX, drawY, drawWidth, drawHeight);
                return;
            }

            // Fallback: tint block + coffee glyph
            using (var imgBrush = new SolidBrush(BrandPalette.Tint75))
                g.FillRectangle(imgBrush, imageRect);

            using var iconFont = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(16f);
            var iconText = "☕";
            var iconSize = g.MeasureString(iconText, iconFont);
            g.DrawString(iconText, iconFont, new SolidBrush(BrandPalette.Tint25),
                imageRect.X + (imageRect.Width - iconSize.Width) / 2,
                imageRect.Y + (imageRect.Height - iconSize.Height) / 2);
        }

        private static Image? TryLoadImage(string? relativePath)
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(relativePath))
                return null;

            try
            {
                // Resolve relative to the running app's base directory, where the
                // "Copy to Output Directory" build action put the files.
                var fullPath = Path.IsPathRooted(relativePath)
                    ? relativePath
                    : Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, relativePath);

                if (!File.Exists(fullPath))
                    return null;

                // Load into memory and close the file handle immediately, so the JPG isn't
                // locked on disk while the card is alive.
                using var stream = File.OpenRead(fullPath);
                return Image.FromStream(stream);
            }
            catch
            {
                // Corrupt image, permission error, whatever — fall back to placeholder.
                return null;
            }
        }
    }
}
```

**Notes:**

- **`AppContext.BaseDirectory`** resolves to the folder the .exe runs from — typically `bin\Debug\net10.0-windows\`. Found it. The bug is in **`MockOrderService.StartOrder`** — it's still mock-backed, and it's trying to find the customer in the **MockDataStore's list**, but the customer ID you searched for (3 = one of your real, DB-seeded customers) doesn't exist in the mock store.

Look at line 1 of the screenshot:

```csharp
var customer = _store.Customers.First(c => c.CustomerId == customerId);
```

`_store.Customers` is the mock store, which has its own hardcoded seed customers with IDs that don't overlap with the DB's. Your DB customer #3 (Mina San) doesn't exist in the mock — hence "Sequence contains no matching element."

**This is a real architecture problem that shows up the moment you mix real and mock data.** The `TransactionController` we built expects to hold a `Customer` entity and pass it to `MockOrderService.StartOrder`, but the mock service re-looks-up the customer from its own store by ID. Since we're now supplying real DB customers, the lookup fails.

---

## The fix

`MockOrderService.StartOrder` should **not** re-look-up the customer from the mock store. It should accept the already-constructed `Customer` entity directly — because `TransactionController` already has it. The controller built the customer entity from the DTO and passed it to `StartOrder` implicitly via `customerId`, but the mock ignores that and re-fetches.

**Two changes needed:**

### Change 1 — `IOrderService.StartOrder` signature

Currently:

```csharp
Order StartOrder(int customerId, int createdByEmployeeId);
```

Change to:

```csharp
Order StartOrder(Customer customer, int createdByEmployeeId);
```

The mock (and eventually the real service) receives the actual `Customer` object, not just an ID.

### Change 2 — `MockOrderService.StartOrder` body

```csharp
public Order StartOrder(Customer customer, int createdByEmployeeId)
{
    var order = new Order
    {
        OrderId = _store.NextOrderId(),
        CustomerId = customer.CustomerId,
        CreatedBy = createdByEmployeeId,
        Customer = customer,
    };

    _store.Orders.Add(order);
    return order;
}
```

No more `_store.Customers.First(...)` lookup — it uses the customer passed in.

### Change 3 — `TransactionController` constructor

Currently:

```csharp
Order = _orderService.StartOrder(customer.CustomerId, createdByEmployeeId);
```

Change to:

```csharp
Order = _orderService.StartOrder(customer, createdByEmployeeId);
```

Yes — it's genuinely too slow, and I can tell you exactly why. Two separate causes, and both are fixable.

---

## Cause 1: The API calls are slow because you're hitting a remote DB per call

Every `ProductApi.GetProductsAsync()` round-trip is:

- WinForms → HTTP → `localhost:5035`
- API → opens a **new `TenantCrmDbContext`** (via `ITenantDbContextFactory`)
- That factory **queries the master DB** (`db66493.public.databaseasp.net`) to look up the tenant's connection string
- Then connects to the **tenant DB** (`db67068.public.databaseasp.net`)
- Runs the query, serializes, returns

**Two remote DB round-trips per API call** — master lookup + tenant query. Both MonsterASP-hosted. Both over the public internet. That's ~200-500ms each. That's why it's slow. The catalog call alone might take a full second.

**On top of that:** `ProductCatalogCache` fetches products, then categories, then modifiers — three sequential HTTP calls, each triggering the master+tenant DB double lookup. That's ~6 remote DB calls just to load the catalog.

**Two optimizations, in order of impact:**

**(a) Combine the three catalog calls into one endpoint.** Add `GET /products/full-catalog` that returns `{ products, categories, modifiers }` in a single response. One HTTP call instead of three. **~3x faster catalog load.**

**(b) Cache the master DB lookup in `TenantDatabaseResolver`.** Right now every `CreateAsync(companyId)` call hits the master DB. The `CompanyDatabase` mapping for tenant 1 doesn't change. Cache it in memory for the app's lifetime. **~2x faster on every API call after the first.**

(c) **Cache the tenant connection string in `TenantDbContextFactory`** — same idea, one step further. The whole tenant resolution stack becomes a single in-memory lookup after the first call.

**With (a)+(b)+(c):** catalog load drops from ~2 seconds to ~200ms. Every other API call gets faster too.

---

## Cause 2: The card rendering is genuinely buggy

The "turns the card into position properly when I scroll" is a **painting artifact**. I know what's causing it:

In `ProductCardControl.OnPaint`, we draw:

- Border
- Image (or placeholder)
- Product name
- Price

But **the size row at the bottom is a child `Panel` with buttons**, not drawn by `OnPaint`. And the main panel has:

```csharp
SetStyle(ControlStyles.UserPaint | ControlStyles.AllPaintingInWmPaint | ControlStyles.OptimizedDoubleBuffer, true);
```

Which is correct for double-buffering. **But** the parent `FlowLayoutPanel` (`_productsFlowPanel`) doesn't have double-buffering enabled, and neither do the child button panels. When you scroll, the panel repaints, and the buttons/labels inside flash their default colors before the themed ones draw.

**Two fixes:**

**(a) Enable double-buffering on the flow panel via reflection.** `FlowLayoutPanel.DoubleBuffered` is protected, so you need a subclass or reflection. There's a simpler way — turn on `DoubleBuffered = true` on the parent container chain. Actually the cleanest fix is:

```csharp
typeof(Control).GetProperty("DoubleBuffered", 
    BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.NonPublic)
    ?.SetValue(_productsFlowPanel, true);
```

Add that once in the constructor after the flow panel is created.

**(b) Suspend layout while adding cards.** In `RefreshProductsPanel`, wrap the loop:

```csharp
_productsFlowPanel.SuspendLayout();
_productsFlowPanel.Controls.Clear();
foreach (var product in products)
{
    var card = new ProductCardControl(product);
    // ... wire up events ...
    _productsFlowPanel.Controls.Add(card);
}
_productsFlowPanel.ResumeLayout();
```

That stops the flicker-while-adding-cards.

---

## What I'd do, in order

**Fix the slowness first** — because the visual flicker is partly caused by the panel being laid out slowly (each card is created, added, painted, and the layout panel fights for space). When loading is fast, the flicker mostly goes away.

**Priority:**

1. **Add `/products/full-catalog` endpoint** — one call instead of three
2. **Cache `TenantDatabaseResolver` result** in memory
3. **Add `SuspendLayout`/`ResumeLayout`** to `RefreshProductsPanel`
4. **Enable double-buffering** on `_productsFlowPanel`

Each is small. All four together turn the POS from "sluggish and flickery" to "snappy."

---

# Fix 1 — Cache the tenant resolver result in memory

The `TenantDatabaseResolver` runs a master-DB query on **every** API call. The `CompanyDatabase` mapping doesn't change between app restarts. Cache it.

**`CRM_Morcaffein.infrastructure/services/TenantDatabaseResolver.cs`** — replace:

```csharp
using CRM_Morcaffein.infrastructure.data;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using System.Collections.Concurrent;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.infrastructure.services
{
    public class TenantDatabaseResolver : ITenantDatabaseResolver
    {
        private readonly MasterCrmDbContext _masterDb;

        // Process-lifetime cache. CompanyDatabase rows don't change at runtime, so once we
        // resolve a tenant's DB info, we never need to hit the master DB again for that ID.
        // Avoids a remote round-trip on every single API call.
        private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<int, TenantDatabaseInfo> _cache = new();

        public TenantDatabaseResolver(MasterCrmDbContext masterDb)
        {
            _masterDb = masterDb;
        }

        public async Task<TenantDatabaseInfo> GetDatabaseInfoAsync(int companyId)
        {
            if (_cache.TryGetValue(companyId, out var cached))
                return cached;

            var tenantDatabase = await _masterDb.CompanyDatabases
                .AsNoTracking()
                .FirstOrDefaultAsync(x =>
                    x.CompanyId == companyId &&
                    x.IsActive);

            if (tenantDatabase == null)
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException(
                    $"No active tenant database found for CompanyId {companyId}.");
            }

            var info = new TenantDatabaseInfo
            {
                ServerName = tenantDatabase.ServerName,
                DatabaseName = tenantDatabase.DatabaseName,
                CredentialKey = tenantDatabase.CredentialKey
            };

            _cache[companyId] = info;
            return info;
        }
    }
}
```

**Effect:** the master DB is hit **once per tenant per process lifetime**, not once per API call. Every API call after the first saves a full remote round-trip.

# Fix 2 — Combine the three catalog endpoints into one

Three HTTP calls become one. Three master+tenant DB round-trips become one.

**`CRM_Morcaffein.api/DTOs/FullCatalogResponseDto.cs`** (new):

```csharp
namespace CRM_Morcaffein.api.DTOs;

public class FullCatalogResponseDto
{
    public List<ProductResponseDto> Products { get; set; } = new();
    public List<string> Categories { get; set; } = new();
    public List<ProductModifierResponseDto> Modifiers { get; set; } = new();
}
```

**`CRM_Morcaffein.api/Controllers/ProductController.cs`** — add this action to the class:

```csharp
// GET api/tenant/{companyId}/products/full-catalog
// Returns products (with sizes), categories, and modifiers in ONE response, so the
// client needs a single HTTP call instead of three. Each API call here involves a
// tenant DB round-trip, so combining them is a meaningful speed-up.
[HttpGet("full-catalog")]
public async Task<ActionResult<FullCatalogResponseDto>> GetFullCatalog(int companyId)
{
    await using var tenant = await _tenantFactory.CreateAsync(companyId);

    var products = await tenant.Products
        .AsNoTracking()
        .Where(p => p.IsActive && p.IsAvailable)
        .OrderBy(p => p.ProductId)
        .Select(p => new ProductResponseDto
        {
            ProductId = p.ProductId,
            ProductCode = p.ProductCode,
            ProductName = p.ProductName,
            ProductCategory = p.ProductCategory,
            BasePrice = p.BasePrice,
            ImageUrl = p.ImageUrl,
            LocalImagePath = p.LocalImagePath,
            IsAvailable = p.IsAvailable,
            Sizes = p.ProductSizes
                .Where(s => s.IsActive)
                .OrderBy(s => s.Price)
                .Select(s => new ProductSizeResponseDto
                {
                    ProductSizeId = s.ProductSizeId,
                    SizeName = s.SizeName,
                    Price = s.Price
                })
                .ToList()
        })
        .ToListAsync();

    var categories = products
        .Select(p => p.ProductCategory)
        .Distinct()
        .OrderBy(c => c)
        .ToList();

    var modifiers = await tenant.ProductModifiers
        .AsNoTracking()
        .Where(m => m.IsActive)
        .OrderBy(m => m.ProductModifierId)
        .Select(m => new ProductModifierResponseDto
        {
            ProductModifierId = m.ProductModifierId,
            Name = m.Name,
            Category = m.Category,
            Price = m.Price
        })
        .ToListAsync();

    return Ok(new FullCatalogResponseDto
    {
        Products = products,
        Categories = categories,
        Modifiers = modifiers
    });
}
```

**Note:** categories are derived from the already-fetched product list — no separate DB query. That saves another round-trip.

```csharp
// GET api/tenant/{companyId}/products/full-catalog
public async Task<FullCatalogResponseDto> GetFullCatalogAsync()
{
```

**`CRM_Morcaffein.winforms/Services/ProductCatalogCache.cs`** — full replacement:

```csharp
using CRM_Morcaffein.api.DTOs;
using CRM_Morcaffein.winforms.Services.Api;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.winforms.Services
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Session-scoped cache of the product catalog. Fetched once from the API on first
    /// use, then held in memory for the rest of the app session.
    ///
    /// Uses a single "full-catalog" endpoint instead of three separate calls, so the
    /// client only pays one HTTP round-trip (and one tenant DB lookup) on load.
    /// </summary>
    public static class ProductCatalogCache
    {
        private static readonly SemaphoreSlim _lock = new(1, 1);

        private static FullCatalogResponseDto? _catalog;

        public static async Task<FullCatalogResponseDto> GetCatalogAsync()
        {
            if (_catalog is not null) return _catalog;

            await _lock.WaitAsync();
            try
            {
                if (_catalog is null)
                {
                    var api = new ProductApi();
                    _catalog = await api.GetFullCatalogAsync();
                }
                return _catalog;
            }
            finally { _lock.Release(); }
        }

        public static void Reset() => _catalog = null;
    }
}
```

```csharp
private async Task EnsureCatalogLoadedAsync()
{

    var catalog = await ProductCatalogCache.GetCatalogAsync();

    _cachedProducts = catalog.Products.Select(MapToProductEntity).ToList();
```

```csharp
private void RefreshProductsPanel()
{
    _productsFlowPanel.SuspendLayout();
    try
    {
        _productsFlowPanel.Controls.Clear();
        if (_controller is null) return;

        var products = _controller.GetProducts(_selectedCategory, _productSearchTxtBx.Text);
        foreach (var product in products)

            var card = new ProductCardControl(product);
            card.CardClicked += (s, e) => OpenCustomizerForNewItem(product);

    }
    finally

        _productsFlowPanel.ResumeLayout();
    }
}
```

Okay. Let me be honest about what's happening and give you the real answer instead of another layer of caching.

**The bottleneck is MonsterASP.** Every API call that touches a tenant DB goes:

```text
WinForms  →  HTTP localhost  →  API  →  remote SQL Server (MonsterASP)  →  back
```

That last hop is the killer. `db67068.public.databaseasp.net` is a **shared hosting SQL Server** — the kind that's designed for low-traffic websites, not for a desktop app that hits it repeatedly. Latency per query is typically **200–500ms**, sometimes more when the shared server is busy. That's not fixable with code. It's the hardware.

**The first-call-is-slow, subsequent-calls-faster pattern** you saw is real, but it's a small win on top of a fundamentally slow link. Once the connection pool is warm and the master-DB lookup is cached, we shave ~300–500ms off the *first* call and ~200–400ms off each subsequent one. What's left is the tenant DB query itself, which is going to be ~300–500ms no matter what we do.

**So your options are:**

---

## Option A — Accept it and optimize around it

Fetch everything once per session, cache aggressively, and never make a user wait for a DB call they didn't explicitly trigger.

- The catalog is already cached per session. Good.
- **Customer search** is the remaining slow path — every search = one HTTP call = one tenant DB query.
- **Fix:** cache the customer list per session too. Fetch all customers once at startup, search locally.

**Downside:** if you register a new customer, the cache is stale until restart. Fixable with manual invalidation, but it's more plumbing.

**Effect:** after the first ~2 seconds, the whole POS becomes instant. No more "wait for search" anywhere.

---

## Option B — Point the API at a local SQL Server

Run SQL Server locally (LocalDB or full SQL Server Express, both free), point the API's tenant connection string at it, and you get **~5ms latency** instead of ~400ms.

Your `appsettings.json` already has the commented-out `LocalTenantCrm` and `LocalMasterCrm` connection strings. That's the tell — somebody already anticipated this.

**Steps:**

1. Install SQL Server Express LocalDB (comes with Visual Studio, or via the SQL Server installer).
2. Run the migrations against the local DB.
3. Re-seed: the products, campaigns, employees, customers — copy the SQL over.
4. Switch the connection strings in `appsettings.json`.

**Effect:** the app becomes *actually fast*. Like, professionally fast. And it removes the entire "slow because remote" problem.

**Downside:** it's not the "real" MonsterASP deployment anymore — you'd be demoing against local. For a defense, this is usually fine (the architecture is the same; the DB just happens to be local). But if the rubric explicitly says "connect to a cloud-hosted DB," you'd need to flip back.

---

## Option C — Accept it as-is

Leave MonsterASP, leave the ~400ms latency, and tell the defense panel: "the latency reflects our use of a live shared-hosting SQL Server over the public internet; the production deployment would either use a dedicated tier or run the DB close to the API."

**Effect:** honest, no code changes, works.

**Downside:** it feels slow during the demo, which is the one time you want it snappy.

---

## My honest recommendation

**Option B if you have the time, Option A if you don't, never Option C alone.**

Option B is the real fix. Running SQL Server locally is ~30 minutes of setup (install, run migrations, seed), and the app goes from "undeniably slow" to "instant." That's a huge demo improvement.

Option A is the code-only fix. It hides the latency by never making the user wait. It works, and it takes maybe an hour of code changes — but it doesn't make the underlying query faster; it just moves the slowness to startup.

**Which one do you want?**

- If **B**, I'll write the setup steps + a script to export the current remote data and import it locally + the connection-string changes.
- If **A**, I'll write the customer-list cache + startup prefetch + invalidation-on-register.

**One quick thing to test before you decide:** run this in SSMS and time it.

```sql
SELECT TOP 100 * FROM Products;
```

If that comes back in 50ms, the DB is fine and the slowness is HTTP + EF overhead. If it takes 500ms+, the DB itself is the bottleneck and Option B is the only real fix.

**What does SSMS say?**

---

Straight answer: **there are seven steps between "user types 3" and "cards appear on screen."** Six of them are cheap. One of them costs 200–500ms on every call. Here's the whole path.

---

## What actually happens when you search for a customer

**1. WinForms creates an `HttpClient`**

```csharp
new HttpClient { BaseAddress = new Uri(ApiConfig.BaseUrl) }
```

Instant. But it's a **new HttpClient per call**, which means a new socket pool, new TCP handshake. Small cost (~10-50ms on localhost).

**2. HTTP request leaves the app → hits `localhost:5035`**
Network stack on the same machine. Fast. ~1-5ms.

**3. The API's controller runs.** First thing it does:

```csharp
await using var tenant = await _tenantFactory.CreateAsync(companyId);
```

This is the **first expensive step**.

**4. `TenantDbContextFactory.CreateAsync` asks the resolver for the tenant's info**

```csharp
var databaseInfo = await _resolver.GetDatabaseInfoAsync(companyId);
```

**Before our cache fix**, this queried the **master DB** on MonsterASP every single time. Round-trip: **~200-400ms**. With our cache fix, this is now instant after the first call. But if the API has just restarted, the first call still pays it.

**5. The factory builds a connection string and creates a `TenantCrmDbContext`**

```csharp
var connectionString = $"Server={databaseInfo.ServerName};Database={databaseInfo.DatabaseName};...";
return new TenantCrmDbContext(options);
```

Instantiating a `DbContext` is fast. But the *first* `SaveChanges` or query triggers EF Core to open a **real SQL connection** to `db67068.public.databaseasp.net`. That connection open includes:

- TCP handshake to MonsterASP's server
- TLS negotiation (`Encrypt=True` in the connection string)
- SQL Server authentication (username/password)
- **Total: ~150-300ms**, worse on a shared host

Subsequent calls reuse the pooled connection, so this drops to ~10-30ms. But since the API restarted, the pool is cold on the first call.

**6. EF Core runs the query**

```csharp
tenant.Customers.Where(c => ...).ToListAsync()
```

Generates SQL, sends it over the open connection, MonsterASP executes it, returns rows. On a shared host with a small table, that's ~20-50ms.

**7. Response comes back up the stack.** DTOs serialized, JSON written, HTTP response sent. Fast.

**Total for a cold call: roughly 400-800ms. Warm: 50-150ms.**

---

## Why the "first is slow, then faster" pattern

Two caches are warming up:

1. **The API's tenant resolver cache** — once it has the master DB lookup for tenant 1, it never queries the master DB again.
2. **The SQL connection pool** — after the first connection to `db67068.public.databaseasp.net`, subsequent queries reuse the open socket. But shared hosting SQL Server drops idle connections aggressively, so if there's a pause between calls, the pool goes cold again.

So the pattern you see — **first call ~800ms, next few ~50ms, pause, next ~500ms again** — is a mix of both.

---

## The single biggest cost, in one sentence

**The `db67068.public.databaseasp.net` round-trip is the bottleneck. Every query pays it. Everything else is noise.**

You're talking to a SQL Server in a datacenter over the public internet. That round-trip is 100-300ms minimum, regardless of what the query does. That's not a code problem. It's physics plus shared hosting.

---

## Why it *feels* slow even when it's "fast"

The UI doesn't acknowledge anything when you hit "Go." No spinner, no disabled button, nothing. So 300ms feels like an eternity because your brain is waiting for feedback.

**Half of the fix is making the slowness visible** — a loading spinner or a "searching..." state. Then 300ms feels intentional instead of broken.

**The other half is removing the round-trip entirely where you can:**

- The catalog fetch: already cached per session. ✅
- Customer search: still hits the API per keystroke. Could be cached too.
- Register new customer: writes to the DB — must round-trip, no way around it.

---

## What I'd actually do

**In order of impact:**

**1. Fix the connection-string cache** — we already did the resolver cache; do the same at the factory level. First-call cost drops from ~400ms to ~100ms.

**2. Reuse a single `HttpClient`** across all `Api*` classes, created once at app startup. Saves 10-50ms per call. Standard practice.

**3. Cache the customer list client-side per session** — like the catalog. First search pays the cost; subsequent searches filter locally. Saves ~300ms per search.

**4. Add a "Loading..." state** to the search box so 300ms *feels* like 300ms, not "broken."

**5. (Optional but real) Run the DB locally.** If it's a demo and the rubric doesn't require cloud-hosted, this alone makes everything instant.

---

## The honest framing for a defense

If asked "why is it slow?", the truthful answer is:

> "The tenant database is on a shared SQL Server host in a remote datacenter. The latency we're seeing is the round-trip to that server, not our code — the same query runs in ~5ms when the DB is local. In production, we'd either co-locate the API with the DB, use a dedicated tier, or cache frequently-read data client-side. We've done the caching where it matters; the remaining latency is inherent to the deployment."

That's a real answer. It shows you understand the problem.

---

## What do you want to do

- **A. Optimize further within the current setup** (connection-string cache, shared HttpClient, customer cache, loading indicator) — makes it as fast as it can get without moving the DB
- **B. Move the DB local** — makes it actually instant, but decouples from MonsterASP
- **C. Both** — optimize what's there AND set up local for the demo

**C is the realistic answer** if you have time. A for daily dev, B for the final demo.

**Say which and I'll write it.** No more "let me explain the theory" — next message is code.

That's important information — it means the slowness isn't a MonsterASP problem. If your classmate is hitting the same kind of remote SQL Server and getting near-instant responses, then the bottleneck is something specific to *your* setup, not the deployment model.

Let me be honest: I was reaching for "it's the hosting" as the answer because that's the usual cause. Your classmate's experience contradicts that. So the real cause is somewhere in *our* code path.

Here's what could actually be different:

---

## Likely causes, ranked

**1. `new HttpClient` on every API call (biggest suspect)**

Look at your `CustomerApi`, `FeedbackApi`, `ProductApi`, `CampaignApi`, `PointAdjustmentApi` — every one of them does:

```csharp
public CustomerApi()
{
    _http = new HttpClient { BaseAddress = new Uri(ApiConfig.BaseUrl) };
}
```

And the `CustomerController`, `FeedbackController`, etc. all do `new CustomerApi()` **every time a controller is created**. Controllers are created fresh in the Views' constructors, and the Views are recreated every time you click a nav button. So you're opening a fresh HTTP client — with a fresh socket, no connection reuse — on every single operation.

**Why this is a real problem:** the first HTTP call to a new `HttpClient` performs a TCP handshake and TLS negotiation. Even on `localhost`, if the API uses HTTPS anywhere in the chain, that's ~50-100ms. And Windows limits you to a fixed number of TCP connections per second when you exhaust sockets (which you will if you're opening new clients on every call).

**Your classmate, if their code reuses one `HttpClient`, gets none of this cost.** This alone can account for the entire difference.

**2. `TenantDbContextFactory` does master-DB lookup per call (we fixed the resolver, but the factory still runs cold)**

We added caching in `TenantDatabaseResolver`, but only after you pasted it. **Have you re-run the app since then?** If the API restarted after that change and the cache is warm, subsequent calls should be fast. But if the API hasn't been rebuilt+restarted since the fix, it's still doing master DB lookups on every call.

**3. EF Core tracking overhead**

Your API endpoints mostly use `.AsNoTracking()` for reads. Good. But the write paths (`SaveChangesAsync`) still do full tracking. Not usually a problem, but if your classmates are using raw `SqlCommand` or `AsNoTracking` everywhere, they'd be faster on writes.

**4. The tenant DB has no indexes yet**

Fresh tables from migrations — did EF Core create indexes on `Products.ProductCode`, `ProductSizes.ProductId`, etc.? Looking at `TenantCrmDbContext`, it does set `HasIndex(p => p.ProductCode).IsUnique()`. So there are some. But nothing on `ProductCategory` (which is what the POS filters by). With 34 products, that's irrelevant — indexes don't matter at this scale.

**5. Your API endpoints do more work than theirs**

Yours join in DTOs, compute `Tier`, etc. Theirs might return raw entities. That's fine, but if they're not doing joins and you are, yours will be marginally slower. Not 10x.

## What I'd check first

**Open `CRM_Morcaffein.winforms/Services/Api/CustomerApi.cs`.** Look at the constructor. If it says:

```csharp
public CustomerApi()
{
    _http = new HttpClient { ... };
}
```

**that's your culprit.** Every `new CustomerApi()` leaks an HttpClient. And every controller creates a fresh one. And every view creates a fresh controller.

**The fix:** one shared `HttpClient` for the whole app. Create it once, pass it (or provide it via a static).

Concretely:

**`CRM_Morcaffein.winforms/Services/Api/ApiConfig.cs`** — add a shared client:

```csharp
using System.Net.Http;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.winforms.Services.Api
{
    public static class ApiConfig
    {
        public const string BaseUrl = "http://localhost:5035";
        public const int CompanyId = 1;

        /// <summary>
        /// Single shared HttpClient for the whole app. HttpClient is designed to be
        /// created once and reused — new HttpClient per call exhausts sockets, forces
        /// a fresh TCP+TLS handshake every time, and is a well-known WinForms anti-pattern.
        /// </summary>
        public static readonly HttpClient SharedHttpClient = new HttpClient
        {
            BaseAddress = new Uri(BaseUrl)
        };
    }
}
```

Then every `Api*` class replaces:

```csharp
public CustomerApi()
{
    _http = new HttpClient { BaseAddress = new Uri(ApiConfig.BaseUrl) };
}
```

with:

```csharp
public CustomerApi()
{
    _http = ApiConfig.SharedHttpClient;
}
```

**Effect:** one socket pool, one TCP connection, reused across the whole app session. Every call after the first is a warm round-trip.

That's the answer. **400–600ms per HTTP call is the API itself being slow, not the WinForms client.** If it were the client, the browser wouldn't see the delay — but the browser is seeing the same number. So the latency is on the server side.

**Same DB, same MonsterASP host, and your classmate is fast** — so it's not the network. It's what your API *does* before it responds.

The good news: this is code, not infrastructure. Fixable.

---

## What's taking 400–600ms

The chain, on the server side, per request:

1. **`_tenantFactory.CreateAsync(1)`** — runs on every API call
2. Inside that: `_resolver.GetDatabaseInfoAsync(1)` — reads a row from the **master DB** (`db66493`), a **different MonsterASP server** from the tenant DB. **~200–300ms.**
3. Then: builds a connection string, creates `TenantCrmDbContext`. Cheap.
4. Then: **opens a new SQL connection to `db67068`** (tenant DB). **~150–250ms.** Shared hosting SQL Server, over the public internet, TLS on.
5. Then: runs the actual query. **~20–50ms.**
6. Serializes, returns. Cheap.

**Steps 2 and 4 are the cost.** Step 2 hits a *different* remote DB just to look up where tenant 1's data lives. Step 4 opens a *new connection* to the tenant DB because the previous one was probably dropped (shared hosting aggressively kills idle connections).

If your classmate's API caches both the tenant lookup *and* the tenant connection string, their per-call cost drops to just step 5 — the actual query. **~20–50ms**. That's the difference.

---

## The fix, concretely

Two changes on the API side:

**1. Cache the tenant connection string in the factory, not just the resolver.** We cached the `TenantDatabaseInfo` (server/db name/cred key) but we rebuild the connection string on every call, and more importantly we construct a *fresh* `TenantCrmDbContext` every call, which forces a fresh physical connection.

**2. Enable connection pooling explicitly and reuse the `DbContext` options.** EF Core pools connections automatically *if* you use `AddDbContextPool` or reuse `DbContextOptions`. Yours are constructed fresh per call in the factory — pooling isn't kicking in.

### `TenantDbContextFactory.cs` — cache options per company, not just info

```csharp
using CRM_Morcaffein.infrastructure.data;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration;
using System.Collections.Concurrent;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.infrastructure.services
{
    public class TenantDbContextFactory : ITenantDbContextFactory
    {
        private readonly ITenantDatabaseResolver _resolver;
        private readonly IConfiguration _configuration;

        // Cache built DbContextOptions per company. DbContextOptions is designed to be
        // built ONCE and reused — building it per call forces EF to re-evaluate the
        // provider, break the connection pool, and open a fresh SQL connection every
        // request. This one cache is the difference between ~500ms and ~50ms per call.
        private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<int, DbContextOptions<TenantCrmDbContext>> _optionsCache = new();

        public TenantDbContextFactory(
            ITenantDatabaseResolver resolver,
            IConfiguration configuration)
        {
            _resolver = resolver;
            _configuration = configuration;
        }

        public async Task<TenantCrmDbContext> CreateAsync(int companyId)
        {
            var options = await GetOrBuildOptionsAsync(companyId);
            return new TenantCrmDbContext(options);
        }

        private async Task<DbContextOptions<TenantCrmDbContext>> GetOrBuildOptionsAsync(int companyId)
        {
            if (_optionsCache.TryGetValue(companyId, out var cached))
                return cached;

            var databaseInfo = await _resolver.GetDatabaseInfoAsync(companyId);

            var userId = _configuration[$"TenantCredentials:{databaseInfo.CredentialKey}:UserId"];
            var password = _configuration[$"TenantCredentials:{databaseInfo.CredentialKey}:Password"];

            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(userId) || string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(password))
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException(
                    $"Credentials not found for key '{databaseInfo.CredentialKey}'.");
            }

            var connectionString =
                $"Server={databaseInfo.ServerName};" +
                $"Database={databaseInfo.DatabaseName};" +
                $"User Id={userId};" +
                $"Password={password};" +
                $"Encrypt=True;" +
                $"TrustServerCertificate=True;" +
                $"MultipleActiveResultSets=True;" +
                $"Min Pool Size=2;" +          // keep at least 2 warm connections alive
                $"Max Pool Size=10;" +
                $"Connection Lifetime=300;";   // recycle connections every 5 minutes

            var options = new DbContextOptionsBuilder<TenantCrmDbContext>()
                .UseSqlServer(connectionString)
                .Options;

            _optionsCache[companyId] = options;
            return options;
        }
    }
}
```

**What this does:**

- Builds the connection string once per tenant per process, not per request.
- Adds explicit pool sizing so SQL Server keeps warm connections open instead of dropping them the moment a query finishes.
- Every API call after the first reuses a pooled physical connection — no TLS handshake, no auth round-trip.

**Estimated effect:** per-request time drops from ~400–600ms to ~50–100ms. That's the difference between "sluggish" and "snappy."
