# Step 3 — Design-time factories

Two factories, both pointing at LocalDB now. Migrations will run against the local DB after this.

## 3a — `CRM_Morcaffein.infrastructure/data/TenantCrmDbContextFactory.cs`

**Replace the entire file with:**

```csharp
using CRM_Morcaffein.infrastructure.data;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.infrastructure.data
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Design-time only: used by `dotnet ef migrations add/update`. The connection string
    /// is inlined because this file never runs at runtime — it only exists so EF's
    /// migration tooling can build a TenantCrmDbContext without the full DI stack.
    ///
    /// Currently pointed at LocalDB for local development. Switch to the MonsterASP
    /// connection string when you want migrations to target the cloud tenant DB.
    /// </summary>
    public class TenantCrmDbContextFactory : IDesignTimeDbContextFactory<TenantCrmDbContext>
    {
        public TenantCrmDbContext CreateDbContext(string[] args)
        {
            const string connectionString =
                "Server=(localdb)\\MSSQLLocalDB;" +
                "Database=CRM_Morcaffein_TenantCrm;" +
                "Trusted_Connection=True;" +
                "TrustServerCertificate=True;" +
                "MultipleActiveResultSets=True;";

            var options = new DbContextOptionsBuilder<TenantCrmDbContext>()
                .UseSqlServer(connectionString)
                .Options;

            return new TenantCrmDbContext(options);
        }
    }
}
```

## 3b — `CRM_Morcaffein.infrastructure/data/MasterCrmDbContextFactory.cs` (new file)

Doesn't exist yet — create it.

```csharp
using CRM_Morcaffein.infrastructure.data;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.infrastructure.data
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Design-time only: used by `dotnet ef migrations add/update` for MasterCrmDbContext.
    /// Points at the local master DB. Never runs at runtime — only during migrations.
    /// </summary>
    public class MasterCrmDbContextFactory : IDesignTimeDbContextFactory<MasterCrmDbContext>
    {
        public MasterCrmDbContext CreateDbContext(string[] args)
        {
            const string connectionString =
                "Server=(localdb)\\MSSQLLocalDB;" +
                "Database=CRM_Morcaffein_MasterCrm;" +
                "Trusted_Connection=True;" +
                "TrustServerCertificate=True;" +
                "MultipleActiveResultSets=True;";

            var options = new DbContextOptionsBuilder<MasterCrmDbContext>()
                .UseSqlServer(connectionString)
                .Options;

            return new MasterCrmDbContext(options);
        }
    }
}
```


Then rerun `Update-Database -Context MasterCrmDbContext`.

Check that `MasterCrmDbContextFactory.cs` exists, has `public class MasterCrmDbContextFactory : IDesignTimeDbContextFactory<MasterCrmDbContext>`, and is in the `CRM_Morcaffein.infrastructure.data` namespace.

## Clean the old master data

In SSMS, connected to `(localdb)\MSSQLLocalDB`, run this against the **`CRM_Morcaffein_MasterCrm`** database (right-click the DB → New Query):

```sql
-- Inspect what's there first
SELECT * FROM Companies;
SELECT * FROM CompanyDatabases;
SELECT * FROM Devices;

-- If the old lab data is still there, clear it out
DELETE FROM CompanyDatabases;
DELETE FROM Devices;
DELETE FROM Companies;

-- Reset identity seeds so the next inserts start from 1
DBCC CHECKIDENT ('CompanyDatabases', RESEED, 0);
DBCC CHECKIDENT ('Devices', RESEED, 0);
DBCC CHECKIDENT ('Companies', RESEED, 0);

-- Confirm empty
SELECT * FROM Companies;
SELECT * FROM CompanyDatabases;
SELECT * FROM Devices;
```

**Run this in the context of `CRM_Morcaffein_MasterCrm`**, not `master` or any other DB — the `DELETE FROM` will hit whichever DB is selected. Double-check the dropdown at the top of the SSMS query window says `CRM_Morcaffein_MasterCrm`.

**What this does:**

- Clears the old lab rows so nothing interferes with our seed in Step 6.
- Resets identity counters so your first real tenant gets `CompanyId = 1` (the app hardcodes that).

**Note:** if the schema uses `ON DELETE RESTRICT` between Companies and CompanyDatabases (which it should, per the model config), delete order matters: `CompanyDatabases` and `Devices` first, `Companies` last.

---

## Verify

After running, all three `SELECT *` at the end should return **zero rows**.

**Then say "next" for Step 5 — migrating the tenant DB locally.**

---

Those messages are harmless:

- **`(1 row affected)` (×3)** — the three DELETEs removed the old lab data (1 company, 1 company-database, 1 device).
- **`'Devices' does not contain an identity column`** — your `Devices` entity uses a `Guid` for its PK, not an auto-increment `int`. So `DBCC CHECKIDENT` had nothing to reset there. Not a problem.
- **`Companies` identity reseeded to 1** — good, so your next real tenant will be `CompanyId = 1`.
- **Final three `SELECT *` all returned `(0 rows affected)`** — everything is clean.

**Nothing more to do here. Go next.**

The error is `Login failed for user 'db67068'` — that's the **cloud credential** being used against LocalDB.

**The tenant resolver is still returning the cloud connection string**, which means the master DB lookup is hitting the cloud master (`db66493`), not your local master.

Why? Two possibilities:

## Possibility 1 — The API is still reading the cloud master connection string

You may have changed `Program.cs` on disk but not rebuilt/restarted the API. Or you changed the wrong line. **Double-check `Program.cs`:**

```csharp
builder.Services.AddDbContext<MasterCrmDbContext>(options =>
  options.UseSqlServer(
    builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("LocalMasterCrm")));   // ← must say "LocalMasterCrm"

builder.Services.AddDbContext<TenantCrmDbContext>(options =>
  options.UseSqlServer(
    builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("LocalTenantCrm")));   // ← must say "LocalTenantCrm"
```

If either still says `"MasterCrm"` or `"TenantCrm"`, that's the problem. Fix and rebuild.

## Possibility 2 — `appsettings.json` doesn't have the Local strings uncommented

Recheck `appsettings.json`. The two `Local*` strings must be present and uncommented. If they're still wrapped in `//`, `GetConnectionString("LocalMasterCrm")` returns null, and the API fails at startup — but you'd get a different error. So this is probably not the case.

## Possibility 3 — The API process wasn't restarted

Even if `Program.cs` is correct on disk, **Visual Studio's Hot Reload** does not pick up changes to connection strings or DI setup. You need a **full stop → rebuild → restart**.

Do this:

1. **Stop the API** (red square in the toolbar).
2. **Right-click the solution → Rebuild Solution.** Wait for it to say `Build succeeded`.
3. **Start the API** again (F5 or right-click `.api` → Debug → Start New Instance).
4. **Try the endpoint** `http://localhost:5035/api/tenant/1/customers`.

## Possibility 4 — There are cached options from a previous run

`TenantDbContextFactory._optionsCache` is a **static** dictionary. If the process was running during a period when it resolved the cloud connection string, that cache persists. But a **full stop-and-restart** clears it because statics are per-process.

**So Possibility 3 covers this.**

## Why both controllers fail identically

Because both call `_tenantFactory.CreateAsync(companyId)` as their first line. That method:

1. Asks `TenantDatabaseResolver` for the tenant's `ServerName` + `DatabaseName`.
2. The resolver queries the **master DB** (whichever connection string `Program.cs` told it to use).
3. If the master is the **cloud** one, it returns `ServerName = db67068.public.databaseasp.net`.
4. The factory then builds a cloud-style connection string with the `db67068` user + password from `TenantCredentials`.
5. That connection string is handed to `TenantCrmDbContext`, which tries to open it.
6. **But** — if the API's tenant connection string config is pointed at LocalDB, EF tries to open the cloud-auth string against LocalDB → "Login failed for user 'db67068'."

So the answer is entirely decided by **which master DB the resolver is talking to**. Check 1 tells us what the local master says, Check 2 tells us what the API reads. Fix whichever is wrong.

**Paste:**

1. `SELECT * FROM CompanyDatabases;` from LocalDB `CRM_Morcaffein_MasterCrm`.
2. The two `AddDbContext` lines from `Program.cs`.

Then I can tell you the exact fix.

Good — that eliminates both obvious causes. So the resolver is finding the right row (LocalDB), the API is reading the right connection string, and yet `db67068` still appears in the login error. That can only come from one place: **the `TenantDbContextFactory` cache**.

## The real cause

Look at `TenantDbContextFactory.cs`:

```csharp
private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<int, DbContextOptions<TenantCrmDbContext>> _optionsCache = new();
```

That `static` dictionary **persists for the lifetime of the API process**. When you were testing against the cloud (before the cutover), it cached a `DbContextOptions` for `companyId = 1` built from the **cloud** connection string — `db67068`, `db67068` user, password, etc.

When you switched to LocalDB and restarted the API via VS, if the process wasn't fully killed (VS sometimes keeps the app running between "Stop" and "Start" in a way that preserves static state), the cache from before **is still there**. So `CreateAsync(1)` returns the cached cloud options instead of building new LocalDB options.

**That's why the resolver and connection string are all correct, but the error still says `db67068`.**

## The fix

**Full process kill.** Not just Stop in VS — actually kill the process. Two ways:

### Option A — Kill from Task Manager

1. Stop the API in VS.
2. Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc).
3. Look for **`CRM_Morcaffein.api.exe`** or **`dotnet.exe`** processes.
4. If any still running, **End Task** on them.
5. Start the API again from VS.

### Option B — Close Visual Studio

Close VS entirely, reopen, run the API. That's the surest way.

### Option C — Clear the cache code defensively

Belt and suspenders — add a cache-busting line to the factory so this can't happen again:

```csharp
public class TenantDbContextFactory : ITenantDbContextFactory
{
    private readonly ITenantDatabaseResolver _resolver;
    private readonly IConfiguration _configuration;

    private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<int, DbContextOptions<TenantCrmDbContext>> _optionsCache = new();
    private static readonly string _cacheFingerprint = Guid.NewGuid().ToString();

    // ... existing code ...
}
```

That doesn't help by itself. **The real defensive fix** is to clear the cache whenever the process restarts, which is already true — statics don't survive a process restart. So as long as you kill the process properly, you're fine.

**But** — one thing is worth checking: are you *sure* the API process is a new one? Here's how to tell:

- **Compare the GUID/ID in the API's console output.** When [ASP.NET](https://asp.net/) Core starts, it prints lines like `Now listening on: http://localhost:5035` and `Application started. Press Ctrl+C to shut down.` If the log timestamps don't match "just now," it's the old process.

Or **check Task Manager for the process start time.** If the process started before you made the `Program.cs` change, it's the old one.

4. **Reopen VS.**

6. **In a browser, hit** `http://localhost:5035/api/tenant/1/customers`.

If it now returns 5 customers, the cache was the issue. If it still fails with `db67068`, then something is writing that connection string at runtime, and we'll need to add temporary logging.

Found it. The file is exactly as it was — **the `if (isLocalDb)` branch was never added.** It detects LocalDB but then falls through to the cloud-only connection-string construction, which is why you're seeing `User Id=db67068;Password=...` even though the server is `(localdb)\MSSQLLocalDB`.

**Replace the whole file with this:**

```csharp
using CRM_Morcaffein.infrastructure.data;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration;
using System.Collections.Concurrent;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.infrastructure.services
{
    public class TenantDbContextFactory : ITenantDbContextFactory
    {
        private readonly ITenantDatabaseResolver _resolver;
        private readonly IConfiguration _configuration;

        // Cache built DbContextOptions per company. DbContextOptions is designed to be
        // built ONCE and reused — building it per call forces EF to re-evaluate the
        // provider, break the connection pool, and open a fresh SQL connection every
        // request. This one cache is the difference between ~500ms and ~50ms per call.
        private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<int, DbContextOptions<TenantCrmDbContext>> _optionsCache = new();

        public TenantDbContextFactory(
            ITenantDatabaseResolver resolver,
            IConfiguration configuration)
        {
            _resolver = resolver;
            _configuration = configuration;
        }

        public async Task<TenantCrmDbContext> CreateAsync(int companyId)
        {
            var options = await GetOrBuildOptionsAsync(companyId);
            return new TenantCrmDbContext(options);
        }

        private async Task<DbContextOptions<TenantCrmDbContext>> GetOrBuildOptionsAsync(int companyId)
        {
            if (_optionsCache.TryGetValue(companyId, out var cached))
                return cached;

            var databaseInfo = await _resolver.GetDatabaseInfoAsync(companyId);

            // LocalDB uses Windows authentication (Trusted_Connection) — there's no
            // user/password to look up. Cloud SQL Server needs credentials from config.
            var isLocalDb = databaseInfo.ServerName.Contains("(localdb)", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);

            string connectionString;

            if (isLocalDb)
            {
                connectionString =
                    $"Server={databaseInfo.ServerName};" +
                    $"Database={databaseInfo.DatabaseName};" +
                    $"Trusted_Connection=True;" +
                    $"TrustServerCertificate=True;" +
                    $"MultipleActiveResultSets=True;";
            }
            else
            {
                var userId = _configuration[$"TenantCredentials:{databaseInfo.CredentialKey}:UserId"];
                var password = _configuration[$"TenantCredentials:{databaseInfo.CredentialKey}:Password"];

                if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(userId) || string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(password))
                {
                    throw new InvalidOperationException(
                        $"Credentials not found for key '{databaseInfo.CredentialKey}'.");
                }

                connectionString =
                    $"Server={databaseInfo.ServerName};" +
                    $"Database={databaseInfo.DatabaseName};" +
                    $"User Id={userId};" +
                    $"Password={password};" +
                    $"Encrypt=True;" +
                    $"TrustServerCertificate=True;" +
                    $"MultipleActiveResultSets=True;" +
                    $"Min Pool Size=2;" +
                    $"Max Pool Size=10;" +
                    $"Connection Lifetime=300;";
            }

            var options = new DbContextOptionsBuilder<TenantCrmDbContext>()
                .UseSqlServer(connectionString)
                .Options;

            _optionsCache[companyId] = options;
            return options;
        }
    }
}
```

**What's fixed:** the connection-string construction is now split into two branches. If `isLocalDb` is true, it uses `Trusted_Connection=True` and no user/password. Otherwise, it uses the credential lookup as before.

**The debug `Console.WriteLine`s are removed** — you can put them back temporarily if you want to verify, but they shouldn't be in the final file.

## Two things worth clarifying before I sequence

**On #5 (Cancel feedback):**

You already have three status values: `Pending`, `Resolved`, `Dismissed`. Adding a fourth (`Cancelled`) is possible but `Dismissed` is already very close to what "cancel" means — a soft-delete-ish state that doesn't award anything. **Two options:**

- **A. Reuse `Dismissed`.** "Cancel" from the staff app just calls the existing `DismissFeedback` service, which sets `Status = "Dismissed"` and `IsActive` stays true. The ticket disappears from the default grid if you filter by status.
- **B. Add a new status `Cancelled`.** Requires a schema addition (new column value, no migration), a new service method, and a policy decision: do cancelled tickets still show anywhere?

**My recommendation: A** — reuse Dismiss. Fewer moving parts, no schema change, and "dismissed" is honest enough for "staff cancelled this by mistake." The status labels could be renamed in the UI to read "Cancelled" if you prefer the wording.

**On #6 (customer editing as an admin function):**

The current Customers tab is staff-facing — search, view, register. Making **editing** an admin-only action on a separate surface is a design choice. Two paths:

- **A. Add an "Edit" button to the existing Customers drawer, gated by role.** Admin+ sees the button; staff doesn't. Uses the existing `PUT /customers/{id}` endpoint. No new surface, no navigation change.
- **B. Create an "Approvals" admin tab** with sub-sections for promotions, customer edits, etc. This is a bigger structural change and needs its own navigation design.

**My recommendation: A for now.** Ship the simple path — an edit button that admins can see. If the rubric wants a full approvals surface later, we build it then. But I don't want to commit to a new tab structure before we know what the defense expects.

Which do you prefer for #5 and #6 — A or B?

## Customer editing — the design space

You have three concerns stacked on top of each other:

1. **Who can edit** (staff / manager / admin)
2. **What "editing" means** (direct save vs. request-and-approve)
3. **Where it happens** (existing Customers tab vs. a separate surface)

Let me lay out the realistic options and what each implies.

### Option 1 — Admin-only direct edit

Only Admin and SuperAdmin can edit customer details. Staff and Managers see a read-only drawer. Edit button only appears for admins; saves directly via `PUT /customers/{id}`.

- **Pros:** Simplest. Matches the pattern of `Employee` management being Admin+ only. No new state to model.
- **Cons:** Staff can't fix a typo'd phone number without tracking down an admin.
- **Real-world fit:** Most CRMs don't let counter staff edit customer records — too risky.

### Option 2 — Staff can edit, but changes go into a request queue for admin approval

Same shape as point adjustments. Staff or Manager submits a "customer edit request" with the proposed changes. Admin approves or rejects. Only on approval does the customer record actually update.

- **Pros:** Consistent with the existing point-adjustment workflow (staff request → manager/admin approve). Never loses the audit trail.
- **Cons:** Requires a new entity (`CustomerEditRequest`) with its own table, DTOs, endpoints, drawer section, and approval UI. It's the size of the point-adjustment workflow, again. **This is a schema change.**

### Option 3 — Manager+ can edit, staff can't

Counter staff (Barista) can't edit. Manager, Admin, SuperAdmin can. No approval flow — managers save directly.

- **Pros:** Middle ground. Doesn't need a new entity. Fits the hierarchy: "the person responsible for the store can fix records."
- **Cons:** No audit of who changed what unless you add `UpdatedBy` tracking. (You already have `UpdatedAt` from `BaseEntity`.)
- **Real-world fit:** Reasonable. A manager on shift can fix a customer's phone number without calling HQ.

### Option 4 — Staff can edit, but only certain fields

Staff can edit contact info (phone, email). Only Manager+ can edit identity fields (name, birthday). Combines with the above.

- **Pros:** Practical — staff fix typos, managers fix real mistakes.
- **Cons:** Adds "which field, which role" complexity. Probably too fine-grained for a college project.

---

### My recommendation: Option 3

Manager and above can edit. Staff sees read-only. No approval flow.

**Why not Option 2 (the request queue):** it's a lot of work for a feature the rubric doesn't specifically demand, and it duplicates the point-adjustment workflow's shape without a compelling reason to. If you later find that staff need to edit, you can add Option 2 on top of Option 3 without redesigning.

**Why not Option 1 (admin only):** too restrictive for a real shop. The manager is the right person to fix customer data.

**If your defense insists on a request queue**, Option 2 is the honest answer — but it's a second entity, a second table, a second set of endpoints, and a second approval UI. Roughly the same work as the point-adjustment workflow we already built. So weigh it against your remaining time.

**Which do you want — 1, 2, 3, or 4?**

---

## Pagination

Yes. This is important, and it applies to every grid.

### What's happening now

Every grid fetches its full dataset in one call. `GET /customers` returns all customers. `GET /products/full-catalog` returns all 34 products. `GET /feedback` returns every ticket.

For 5 customers and 34 products, that's fine. **For real data it isn't.** A shop with 2000 customers, 5000 orders, 10,000 ledger entries — every grid load is 5-10 MB of JSON, and the grid tries to render every row.

**You're already feeling it** in the order list — every order ever made renders as a row. With 100 test orders that's fine; with 5000 it grinds.

### Where it matters most

- **Orders in the customer drawer** (order history) — biggest, grows fastest
- **Point ledger in the customer drawer** — grows with every sale
- **Feedback tab** — grows with every ticket
- **Customers tab** — grows with every registration
- **Products in the POS** — has 34, will eventually have more

### How to add pagination

Three parts:

**1. API side — accept `page` and `pageSize`:**

```csharp
[HttpGet]
public async Task<ActionResult<PagedResponse<CustomerResponseDto>>> GetCustomers(
    int companyId,
    [FromQuery] string? search,
    [FromQuery] int page = 1,
    [FromQuery] int pageSize = 50)
{
    // ... query ...
    var total = await query.CountAsync();
    var items = await query
        .OrderBy(c => c.CustomerId)
        .Skip((page - 1) * pageSize)
        .Take(pageSize)
        .Select(...)
        .ToListAsync();

    return Ok(new PagedResponse<CustomerResponseDto>
    {
        Items = items,
        TotalCount = total,
        Page = page,
        PageSize = pageSize
    });
}
```

**2. A `PagedResponse<T>` DTO** — carries `Items`, `TotalCount`, `Page`, `PageSize`. Client uses it to know how many pages exist.

**3. Client side — page controls:**

- Prev / Next buttons
- "Page X of Y"
- Page size selector (25 / 50 / 100)
- Optional: jump-to-page

For the DataGridView, it's `DataSource = response.Items` — the grid only sees the current page.

### Which grids to paginate first

Priority order (biggest → smallest data volume growth):

1. **Order history** in the customer drawer — highest growth rate. **Start here.**
2. **Point ledger** in the same drawer — same reason.
3. **Feedback grid** — grows with tickets.
4. **Customers grid** — grows with registrations.
5. **POS product cards** — only if the catalog grows beyond ~100 items.

**My recommendation: paginate the two drawer grids (orders, ledger) first.** Those are the ones that will visibly break first. The others can be paginated later if time allows.

### In `BuildLayout()`

Wrap the middle + right columns in a container so the overlay can sit on top of them without covering the left customer column (which needs to stay usable for searching). Replace the current `BuildLayout()` with:

```csharp
private void BuildLayout()
{
    Dock = DockStyle.Fill;
    BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfaceSecondary;

    var cardOuterPanel = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Fill, BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfaceSecondary, Padding = new Padding(24) };
    var tableCardPanel = new Panel

        BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
    };

    // Left column stays interactive at all times — it holds the customer search.
    var leftColumn = BuildCustomerColumn();

    // Middle + right go inside this container, so the overlay can sit on top of
    // them without covering the search box in the left column.
    var middleAndRightContainer = new Panel
    {
        Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
        BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
    };

    var middleArea = BuildDrinksArea();
    var rightColumn = BuildOrderColumn();

    middleAndRightContainer.Controls.Add(middleArea);
    middleAndRightContainer.Controls.Add(rightColumn);

    // Overlay — sits on top of the middle+right container, blends with the profile
    // card color (Tint90 / SurfaceCard), and hides once a customer is selected.
    _blockOverlayPanel = new Panel
    {
        Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
        BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfaceCard,
        Visible = true,
    };

    _blockOverlayMessageLabel = new Label
    {
        Text = "Search for a customer to begin.",
        Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
        TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleCenter,
        Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(12f),
        ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralTextMuted,
        BackColor = Color.Transparent,
    };

    _blockOverlayPanel.Controls.Add(_blockOverlayMessageLabel);
    middleAndRightContainer.Controls.Add(_blockOverlayPanel);

    tableCardPanel.Controls.Add(middleAndRightContainer);
    tableCardPanel.Controls.Add(leftColumn);

    cardOuterPanel.Controls.Add(tableCardPanel);
    Controls.Add(cardOuterPanel);
}
```

**Note on stacking:** in WinForms, later-added controls draw on top of earlier ones. So `middleArea` and `rightColumn` are added first (they render), then `_blockOverlayPanel` is added last — it renders on top and blocks clicks. That's what we want.

### Set the overlay visible in `SelectCustomerAsync`

At the very beginning of `SelectCustomerAsync`, right after the confirm-check, hide the overlay:

```csharp
private async Task SelectCustomerAsync(CustomerResponseDto dto)
{
    var employeeId = EmployeeSession.Current?.EmployeeId
        ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("No employee session — the Transaction view requires a logged-in employee.");

    if (_controller is not null && _controller.CartItems.Count > 0)
    {
        var currentCustomerName = _controller.Customer.FullName;
        var confirm = MessageBox.Show(
            FindForm(),
            $"Discard the in-progress order for {currentCustomerName} and start a new one for {dto.FullName}?",
            "Start New Transaction",
            MessageBoxButtons.YesNo,
            MessageBoxIcon.Warning);

        if (confirm != DialogResult.Yes)
        {
            _customerSearchTxtBx.Text = _controller.Customer.CustomerId.ToString();
            return;
        }
    }

    try
    {
        await EnsureCatalogLoadedAsync();

        // ... existing customer + campaign load ...

        _controller = new TransactionController(
            _cachedProducts!,
            _cachedCategories!,
            _cachedModifiers!,
            campaigns,
            entity,
            employeeId);

        // Reveal the POS now that a customer is loaded.
        _blockOverlayPanel.Visible = false;

        // ... rest of method ...
    }
    catch (Exception ex)
    {
        _customerSearchErrorLabel.Text = ex.Message;
        _customerProfilePanel.Visible = false;
        // Keep the overlay visible — nothing to interact with yet.
        _blockOverlayPanel.Visible = true;
    }
}
```

**Note:** I set `_blockOverlayPanel.Visible = false` **after** the controller is successfully created — so if the API call fails partway through, the overlay stays visible and the user can't click on a half-loaded POS.

Your changes are almost right — but there are three issues to fix.

## Issues

**1. The overlay is not on top.** In `BuildLayout()`, you're adding controls in this order:

```csharp
middleAndRightContainer.Controls.Add(middleArea);
middleAndRightContainer.Controls.Add(rightColumn);
// ...
middleAndRightContainer.Controls.Add(_blockOverlayPanel);
```

Actually that's correct — the overlay is added **last**, so it draws on top. Good.

**BUT** — one subtlety: `middleArea` is `Dock = Fill`. It fills the whole container. Then `rightColumn` is `Dock = Right`, which claims 380px on the right. `middleArea` shrinks. Then `_blockOverlayPanel` is `Dock = Fill`. It fills whatever's left — which is the same area as `middleArea` after `rightColumn` claimed its space. So the overlay **only covers the middle area, not the right column**.

Wait — no. That's not right either. Let me think again.

In WinForms, `Dock.Fill` fills the container's client area **minus** the space taken by edge-docked siblings. But the overlay is added **after** middleArea and rightColumn. That doesn't matter for Fill semantics — Fill always takes the leftover space after edge-docked siblings claim theirs.

But **`_blockOverlayPanel` is `Dock.Fill`**, and so is `middleArea`. They both want the same space. **The one that's on top (later-added, so higher z-order) wins visually**, but both take the same area. Which means the overlay covers the middle area but **not** the right column, because the right column is claimed by `Dock.Right`.

**So the overlay only covers the drinks area, not the order/payables/log-sale on the right.** That's the bug.

**Fix:** Don't dock the overlay to Fill. Instead, use a different approach — make it fill the **parent** on top of everything by giving the container panel a way to overlay. Simplest fix: after adding all children, use `BringToFront()`:

```csharp
middleAndRightContainer.Controls.Add(middleArea);
middleAndRightContainer.Controls.Add(rightColumn);
middleAndRightContainer.Controls.Add(_blockOverlayPanel);
_blockOverlayPanel.BringToFront();
```

But that still won't cover the right column if the overlay is docked Fill and loses the sizing war.

**The clean fix:** wrap `middleArea` and `rightColumn` in the container, then put the overlay in a **separate outer container**:

```csharp
var middleAndRightContainer = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Fill };
// ... add middleArea + rightColumn to middleAndRightContainer ...

// Overlay lives in its own outer panel that sits over the whole thing
var overlayContainer = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Fill };
overlayContainer.Controls.Add(middleAndRightContainer);
overlayContainer.Controls.Add(_blockOverlayPanel);
_blockOverlayPanel.BringToFront();
```

But `_blockOverlayPanel` still has `Dock.Fill` inside the overlay container, and `middleAndRightContainer` also has `Dock.Fill`. They fight again.

**The truly clean fix:** use `BringToFront()` on the overlay and don't dock it — set its bounds equal to the container's bounds on resize. OR — simpler — use `Dock.Fill` on the overlay and add it to the same container **with `BringToFront()`**, and don't worry about it dock-fighting.

Actually, the WinForms reality: **`Dock.Fill` controls in the same parent do NOT fight.** They all fill the same client area. `Dock.Right` and `Dock.Left` and `Dock.Top` and `Dock.Bottom` claim their edges **first** (in reverse z-order), and then all `Dock.Fill` controls fill the remaining space.

So in your layout:

- `middleArea` (Dock.Fill) and `rightColumn` (Dock.Right) — `rightColumn` claims 380px on the right, `middleArea` fills the rest.
- `_blockOverlayPanel` (Dock.Fill) — **also** fills the rest, on top of `middleArea`.
- **The right column is NOT covered by the overlay.**

**That's the bug.** Your overlay only covers the middle area. The right column (Order / Payables / Log Sale) is still usable.

## The fix

Set `_blockOverlayPanel.Dock = DockStyle.None` and give it bounds matching the container. Or — simplest — **don't use Dock at all for the overlay**, and instead make it fill via a resize handler:

Actually, the simplest and most reliable WinForms pattern:

```csharp
_blockOverlayPanel = new Panel
{
    Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
    BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfaceCard,
    Visible = true,
};

// Then, after adding all children to middleAndRightContainer:
middleAndRightContainer.Controls.Add(middleArea);
middleAndRightContainer.Controls.Add(rightColumn);
middleAndRightContainer.Controls.Add(_blockOverlayPanel);
_blockOverlayPanel.BringToFront();
```

But as analyzed, Dock.Fill on the overlay still loses the right column to `rightColumn.Dock = Right`.

**The working solution: put the overlay OUTSIDE the dock hierarchy.** Add it to `tableCardPanel` (or `cardOuterPanel`), not `middleAndRightContainer`. Position it after `leftColumn` is added so it covers everything to the right of the left column:

```csharp
tableCardPanel.Controls.Add(middleAndRightContainer);
tableCardPanel.Controls.Add(leftColumn);
tableCardPanel.Controls.Add(_blockOverlayPanel);   // added AFTER leftColumn

// Set overlay bounds to cover everything except the left column
_blockOverlayPanel.Dock = DockStyle.None;
_blockOverlayPanel.Bounds = new Rectangle(leftColumn.Width, 0,
    tableCardPanel.ClientSize.Width - leftColumn.Width,
    tableCardPanel.ClientSize.Height);
```

But then you'd need to reposition on resize. Annoying.

**Simplest working approach: give the middleAndRightContainer a padding trick.** No.

**Actually the cleanest:** make `_blockOverlayPanel` a child of `middleAndRightContainer` but **NOT** docked — instead, set `Dock = Fill` on it, and give it a **higher z-order than `rightColumn`**. Since `rightColumn` is edge-docked, it wins the edge. To make the overlay cover it, we need to change how the container is laid out:

**Change `rightColumn.Dock = Right` to being placed inside a sub-panel that also fills.** No, too complex.

**The real answer: don't use Dock.Right for the right column inside the middle+right container.** Instead:

- `middleArea` = Fill
- `rightColumn` = Dock.Right (as now)
- Overlay = added to the **outer card panel**, not the middle+right container, and positioned to cover only the middle+right area.

Too fiddly.

**The genuinely simple fix:** put the overlay inside `middleAndRightContainer`, but change `rightColumn` to be inside a wrapper. Actually no.

**OK, the actual simplest fix:** the overlay should **not** be docked. Give it fixed bounds that cover the container, and update on resize:

```csharp
middleAndRightContainer.Controls.Add(middleArea);
middleAndRightContainer.Controls.Add(rightColumn);

_blockOverlayPanel = new Panel
{
    Dock = DockStyle.None,
    BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfaceCard,
    Visible = true,
};

middleAndRightContainer.Controls.Add(_blockOverlayPanel);
_blockOverlayPanel.BringToFront();

// Cover the whole container, not just the Fill area
middleAndRightContainer.Resize += (s, e) =>
{
    _blockOverlayPanel.Bounds = new Rectangle(0, 0,
        middleAndRightContainer.ClientSize.Width,
        middleAndRightContainer.ClientSize.Height);
};
_blockOverlayPanel.Bounds = new Rectangle(0, 0,
    middleAndRightContainer.ClientSize.Width,
    middleAndRightContainer.ClientSize.Height);
```

That's what I should have sent. Not Docked — absolute bounds, updated on resize. `BringToFront()` ensures it's on top of both middleArea and rightColumn.

```csharp
                    middleAndRightContainer.ClientSize.Width,
                    middleAndRightContainer.ClientSize.Height);
            }
            middleAndRightContainer.Resize += (s, e) => FitOverlay();
            FitOverlay();

            tableCardPanel.Controls.Add(middleAndRightContainer);
            tableCardPanel.Controls.Add(leftColumn);

            cardOuterPanel.Controls.Add(tableCardPanel);
            Controls.Add(cardOuterPanel);
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // CATALOG LOADING
        // =====================================================================

        private async Task EnsureCatalogLoadedAsync()
        {
            if (_cachedProducts is not null) return;

            var catalog = await ProductCatalogCache.GetCatalogAsync();

            _cachedProducts = catalog.Products.Select(MapToProductEntity).ToList();
            _cachedCategories = catalog.Categories;
            _cachedModifiers = catalog.Modifiers.Select(MapToModifierEntity).ToList();
        }

        private static Product MapToProductEntity(ProductResponseDto dto)
        {
            var product = new Product
            {
                ProductId = dto.ProductId,
                ProductCode = dto.ProductCode,
                ProductName = dto.ProductName,
                ProductCategory = dto.ProductCategory,
                BasePrice = dto.BasePrice,
                ImageUrl = dto.ImageUrl,
                LocalImagePath = dto.LocalImagePath,
                IsAvailable = dto.IsAvailable,
            };

            foreach (var sizeDto in dto.Sizes)
            {
                product.ProductSizes.Add(new ProductSize
                {
                    ProductSizeId = sizeDto.ProductSizeId,
                    ProductId = dto.ProductId,
                    SizeName = sizeDto.SizeName,
                    Price = sizeDto.Price,
                });
            }

            return product;
        }

        private static ProductModifier MapToModifierEntity(ProductModifierResponseDto dto) => new()
        {
            ProductModifierId = dto.ProductModifierId,
            Name = dto.Name,
            Category = dto.Category,
            Price = dto.Price,
        };

        // =====================================================================
        // CUSTOMER SELECTION
        // =====================================================================

        private async void RunCustomerSearch()
        {
            var query = _customerSearchTxtBx.Text.Trim();
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(query))
                return;

            try
            {
                var customerApi = new CustomerApi();
                var match = await customerApi.FindCustomerAsync(query);

                if (match is null)
                {
                    _customerSearchErrorLabel.Text = $"No customer found for \"{query}\".";
                    _customerProfilePanel.Visible = false;
                    _blockOverlayPanel.Visible = true;
                    return;
                }

                _customerSearchErrorLabel.Text = string.Empty;
                ShowCustomerProfile(match);
                await SelectCustomerAsync(match);
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                _customerSearchErrorLabel.Text = ex.Message;
                _customerProfilePanel.Visible = false;
                _blockOverlayPanel.Visible = true;
            }
        }

        private void ShowCustomerProfile(CustomerResponseDto customer)
        {
            _customerProfileNameLabel.Text = customer.FullName;
            _customerProfileDetailLabel.Text = $"{customer.Tier} Tier   •   {customer.PointsBalance} pts\n{customer.ContactNumber}";
            _customerProfilePanel.Visible = true;
        }

        private async Task SelectCustomerAsync(CustomerResponseDto dto)
        {
            var employeeId = EmployeeSession.Current?.EmployeeId
                ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("No employee session — the Transaction view requires a logged-in employee.");

            if (_controller is not null && _controller.CartItems.Count > 0)
            {
                var currentCustomerName = _controller.Customer.FullName;
                var confirm = MessageBox.Show(
                    FindForm(),
                    $"Discard the in-progress order for {currentCustomerName} and start a new one for {dto.FullName}?",
                    "Start New Transaction",
                    MessageBoxButtons.YesNo,
                    MessageBoxIcon.Warning);

                if (confirm != DialogResult.Yes)
                {
                    _customerSearchTxtBx.Text = _controller.Customer.CustomerId.ToString();
                    return;
                }
            }

            try
            {
                await EnsureCatalogLoadedAsync();

                var entity = new Customer
                {
                    CustomerId = dto.CustomerId,
                    FirstName = dto.FirstName,
                    LastName = dto.LastName,
                    ContactNumber = dto.ContactNumber,
                    Email = dto.Email,
                    Birthday = dto.Birthday,
                    LastVisitDate = dto.LastVisitDate,
                    PointsBalance = dto.PointsBalance,
                    IsActive = dto.IsActive,
                };

                var campaignApi = new CampaignApi();
                var campaignDtos = await campaignApi.GetActiveCampaignsAsync();
                var campaigns = campaignDtos.Select(MapToCampaignEntity).ToList();

                _controller = new TransactionController(
                    _cachedProducts!,
                    _cachedCategories!,
                    _cachedModifiers!,
                    campaigns,
                    entity,
                    employeeId);

                _blockOverlayPanel.Visible = false;

                _pwdSeniorChk.CheckedChanged -= PwdSeniorChk_ProgrammaticReset;
                _pwdSeniorChk.CheckedChanged += PwdSeniorChk_ProgrammaticReset;

                BuildCategoryOptions();
                RefreshProductsPanel();
                RefreshCartLines();
                RefreshSummary();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                _customerSearchErrorLabel.Text = ex.Message;
                _customerProfilePanel.Visible = false;
                _blockOverlayPanel.Visible = true;
            }
        }

        private void PwdSeniorChk_ProgrammaticReset(object? sender, EventArgs e)
        {
            // No-op handler swapped in temporarily to suppress the toggle during resets.
        }

        private static Campaign MapToCampaignEntity(CampaignResponseDto dto) => new()
        {
            CampaignId = dto.CampaignId,
            PromoName = dto.PromoName,
            PromoCategory = dto.PromoCategory,
            DiscountType = dto.DiscountType,
            DiscountValue = dto.DiscountValue,
            TargetTier = dto.TargetTier,
            MinPurchaseAmount = dto.MinPurchaseAmount,
            MaxDiscountAmount = dto.MaxDiscountAmount,
            MaxRedemptionsPerCustomer = dto.MaxRedemptionsPerCustomer,
            StartDate = dto.StartDate,
            EndDate = dto.EndDate,
            IsActive = dto.IsActive,
        };

        // =====================================================================
        // PROMO
        // =====================================================================

        private void ShowPromoMenu()
        {
            if (_controller is null)
                return;

            var menu = new ContextMenuStrip();

            if (_controller.Order.CampaignRedeems.Count > 0)
            {
                var clear = menu.Items.Add("Clear applied promo");
                clear.Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(9f);
                clear.Click += (s, e) =>
                {
                    _controller.ClearPromos();
                    RefreshSummary();
                    RefreshPromoButton();
                };
                menu.Items.Add(new ToolStripSeparator());
            }

            var eligiblePromos = _controller.GetEligiblePromos();
            if (eligiblePromos.Count == 0)
            {
                var none = menu.Items.Add("No promos available for this order");
                none.Enabled = false;
            }
            else
            {
                foreach (var campaign in eligiblePromos)
                {
                    var alreadyApplied = _controller.Order.CampaignRedeems
                        .Any(r => r.CampaignId == campaign.CampaignId);

                    var label = campaign.DiscountType == "Percentage"
                        ? $"{campaign.PromoName} — {campaign.DiscountValue:0.##}% off"
                        : $"{campaign.PromoName} — ₱{campaign.DiscountValue:0.##} off";
                    if (alreadyApplied)
                        label += "  (applied)";

                    var item = menu.Items.Add(label);
                    item.Enabled = !alreadyApplied;
                    item.Click += (s, e) =>
                    {
                        try
                        {
                            _controller.ApplyPromo(campaign);
                            RefreshSummary();
                            RefreshPromoButton();
                        }
                        catch (Exception ex)
                        {
                            ShowCartStatus(ex.Message);
                        }
                    };
                }
            }

            menu.Show(_promoMenuBtn, new Point(0, -menu.PreferredSize.Height));
        }

        private void RefreshPromoButton()
        {
            if (_controller is null)
            {
                _promoMenuBtn.Text = "Select a Promo ▾";
                _promoMenuBtn.Enabled = false;
                return;
            }

            var applied = _controller.Order.CampaignRedeems.FirstOrDefault();

            if (applied is null)
            {
                _promoMenuBtn.Text = "Select a Promo ▾";
            }
            else
            {
                var campaign = _controller.GetEligiblePromos()
                                   .FirstOrDefault(c => c.CampaignId == applied.CampaignId);

                var name = campaign?.PromoName ?? $"Promo #{applied.CampaignId}";
                _promoMenuBtn.Text = $"{name} ▾";
            }

            _promoMenuBtn.Enabled = true;
        }

        private void RefreshSummary()
        {
            RefreshPromoButton();

            if (_controller is null)
            {
                _subTotalValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
                _discountValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
                _vatValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
                _pwdSeniorValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
                _totalValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
                _logSaleBtn.Enabled = false;
                _pwdSeniorChk.Enabled = false;
                return;
            }

            _pwdSeniorChk.Enabled = true;

            var subTotal = _controller.SubTotal;
            var afterPromo = subTotal - _controller.TotalDiscount;
            var vatAmount = afterPromo > 0 ? decimal.Round((afterPromo / 1.12m) * VatRate, 2) : 0m;

            _subTotalValueLabel.Text = $"₱{subTotal:0.00}";
            _discountValueLabel.Text = $"₱{_controller.TotalDiscount:0.00}";
            _vatValueLabel.Text = $"₱{vatAmount:0.00}";
            _pwdSeniorValueLabel.Text = $"₱{_controller.PwdSeniorDiscountAmount:0.00}";
            _totalValueLabel.Text = $"₱{_controller.TotalAmount:0.00}";
            _logSaleBtn.Enabled = _controller.HasItems;
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // DRINKS / CART
        // =====================================================================

        private void BuildCategoryOptions()
        {
            if (_cachedCategories is null) return;

            _categoryCombo.Items.Clear();
            _categoryCombo.Items.Add(AllCategoriesOption);
            foreach (var category in _cachedCategories)
                _categoryCombo.Items.Add(category);
            _categoryCombo.SelectedIndex = 0;
        }

        private void RefreshProductsPanel()
        {
            _productsFlowPanel.SuspendLayout();
            try
            {
                _productsFlowPanel.Controls.Clear();
                if (_controller is null) return;

                var products = _controller.GetProducts(_selectedCategory, _productSearchTxtBx.Text);
                foreach (var product in products)
                {
                    var card = new ProductCardControl(product);
                    card.CardClicked += (s, e) => OpenCustomizerForNewItem(product);
                    card.SizeQuickAdded += (s, size) => QuickAddToCart(product, size);
                    _productsFlowPanel.Controls.Add(card);
                }
            }
            finally
            {
                _productsFlowPanel.ResumeLayout();
            }
        }

        private void QuickAddToCart(Product product, ProductSize size)
        {
            if (_controller is null)
            {
                ShowCartStatus("Pick a customer on the left first.");
                return;
            }

            try
            {
                _controller.AddItemToCart(product, size, 1, Enumerable.Empty<ProductModifier>());
                RefreshCartLines();
                RefreshSummary();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                ShowCartStatus(ex.Message);
            }
        }

        private void OpenCustomizerForNewItem(Product product)
        {
            if (_controller is null)
            {
                ShowCartStatus("Pick a customer on the left first.");
                return;
            }

            using var form = new FrmItemCustomizer(product, _controller.GetModifiers());

            if (form.ShowDialog(FindForm()) == DialogResult.OK)
            {
                try
                {
                    _controller.AddItemToCart(product, form.SelectedSize, form.Quantity, form.SelectedModifiers);
                    RefreshCartLines();
                    RefreshSummary();
                }
                catch (Exception ex)
                {
                    ShowCartStatus(ex.Message);
                }
            }
        }

        private void RefreshCartLines()
        {
            _cartLinesPanel.Controls.Clear();

            if (_controller is null || _controller.CartItems.Count == 0)
            {
                _cartLinesPanel.Controls.Add(_cartEmptyLabel);
                return;
            }

            var lineWidth = Math.Max(200,
                _cartLinesPanel.ClientSize.Width - SystemInformation.VerticalScrollBarWidth - 8);

            foreach (var item in _controller.CartItems)
            {
                var line = new CartLineControl(item) { Width = lineWidth };
                line.QuantityIncreased += (s, e) => ChangeQuantity(item, +1);
                line.QuantityDecreased += (s, e) => ChangeQuantity(item, -1);
                line.RemoveClicked += (s, e) => RemoveFromCart(item);
                _cartLinesPanel.Controls.Add(line);
            }
        }

        private void RemoveFromCart(OrderItem item)
        {
            if (_controller is null) return;

            _controller.RemoveItem(item);
            RefreshCartLines();
            RefreshSummary();
        }

        private void ChangeQuantity(OrderItem item, int delta)
        {
            if (_controller is null || item.Product is null) return;

            var newQuantity = item.Quantity + delta;
            if (newQuantity <= 0)
            {
                RemoveFromCart(item);
                return;
            }

            var size = item.Product.ProductSizes.First(s => s.ProductSizeId == item.ProductSizeId);
            var modifiers = _controller.GetModifiers()
                .Where(m => item.OrderItemModifiers.Any(om => om.ProductModifierId == m.ProductModifierId));

            try
            {
                _controller.UpdateCartItem(item, size, newQuantity, modifiers);
                RefreshCartLines();
                RefreshSummary();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                ShowCartStatus(ex.Message);
            }
        }

        private void ShowCartStatus(string message) => _cartStatusLabel.Text = message;

        private async void CompleteSale()
        {
            if (_controller is null) return;

            try
            {
                _logSaleBtn.Enabled = false;
```

On the discount cap for PWD/Senior — let me answer directly.

---

## Should PWD/Senior have a ₱100 cap?

**No — and it's legally wrong to cap it that way in the Philippines.**

PWD and Senior Citizen discounts are **mandated by law** (RA 9994 for Senior Citizens, RA 10754 for PWDs). They cannot be capped, conditioned, or restricted by the establishment. The law says: 20% off the VAT-exempt amount, no upper limit. A ₱500 PWD order gets ₱89.29 off (20% of ₱446.43 net of VAT), not ₱100. A ₱5,000 order gets ₱892.86 off. There's no ceiling.

If you put a ₱100 cap on PWD/Senior:

- You'd be under-charging compliance — this is illegal in a real shop.
- In a defense, someone who knows the law will call it out.
- It doesn't match how the app is already coded (the PWD/Senior calculation has no cap in `RecalculateOrderTotals` or in `OrdersController`).

**My recommendation: no cap on PWD/Senior.** Leave the calculation as-is. The law is the law.

---

## For promo campaigns — the cap makes sense

**Promos** are the establishment's own choice. A ₱100 cap on a promo is fine and common:

- "10% off, max ₱100" — protects the shop from huge discounts on big orders
- "15% off, max ₱150" — same idea, higher ceiling

That's a business decision, not a legal one, and it's what `Campaign.MaxDiscountAmount` was designed for. **The field already exists and is already respected** in the discount math on both client and server. You just need a way to set it (currently seeded via SQL).

**My recommendation:**

- **PWD/Senior: no cap.**
- **Promos: cap whatever you want.** ₱100 is a reasonable default. But it's per-campaign, not global — some campaigns can have higher or lower caps depending on what the shop decides.

If you want to make ₱100 the default cap for **new campaigns** created through an admin UI (when that's built), that's a data default, not a code change. No work now.

---

## So what goes on the list?

Just this, as a **future admin-console task** (not now):

> **Admin console — Campaign management:** When the admin/manager surface is built to create and edit campaigns, include a `MaxDiscountAmount` field so the shop can set a per-campaign discount cap. Default to ₱100 if not specified. **PWD/Senior is not capped** (legally required).

That's it. Nothing to do this session.

That error is from placing the wrong code in the wrong handler. `KeyDown` provides a `KeyEventArgs` — which has `KeyCode`, not `KeyChar`. `KeyPress` provides a `KeyPressEventArgs` — which has `KeyChar`.

**You put the digits-only check inside `KeyDown`. It needs to be inside `KeyPress`.**

## Fix

Replace the whole `_customerSearchTxtBx` block with this:

```csharp
_customerSearchTxtBx = new TextBox
{
    Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
    PlaceholderText = "Customer ID or phone",
    Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9f),
    BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle,
};

_customerSearchTxtBx.KeyDown += (s, e) =>
{
    if (e.KeyCode == Keys.Enter) { RunCustomerSearch(); e.SuppressKeyPress = true; }
};

_customerSearchTxtBx.KeyPress += (s, e) =>
{
    // Only digits allowed — the POS search accepts Customer ID or phone, both numeric.
    if (!char.IsControl(e.KeyChar) && !char.IsDigit(e.KeyChar))
        e.Handled = true;
};
```

**Two separate handlers:**

- `KeyDown` — for Enter (uses `e.KeyCode`, `e.SuppressKeyPress`)
- `KeyPress` — for character filtering (uses `e.KeyChar`, `e.Handled`)

They can't be combined — different event args.

**Note the apostrophes** — there's an issue in your screenshot: `char.IsControl(e.KeyChar)` has weird quotes. Make sure it's the plain `'` character: `!char.IsControl(e.KeyChar) && !char.IsDigit(e.KeyChar)`.

## Fix — `FrmCustomerOnboarding`

The form has a two-step flow. Step 1 collects details; step 2 confirms. The user clicks **Next** to go from step 1 to step 2. That's the right moment to validate email.

Open `CRM_Morcaffein.winforms/Views/FrmCustomerOnboarding.cs`. Find the `NextBtn_Click` method:

```csharp
private void NextBtn_Click(object? sender, EventArgs e)
{
    if (CanSave())
    {
        errorLabel.Text = string.Empty;
        ShowConfirmStep();
    }
    else
    {
        errorLabel.Text = "Please fill in first name, last name, and phone number.";
    }
}
```

**Replace with:**

```csharp
private void NextBtn_Click(object? sender, EventArgs e)
{
    if (!CanSave())
    {
        errorLabel.Text = "Please fill in first name, last name, and phone number.";
        return;
    }

    // Email is optional, but if provided it must look like an email.
    var email = emailTxtBx.Text.Trim();
    if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(email) && !IsValidEmail(email))
    {
        errorLabel.Text = "Please enter a valid email address (e.g. name@example.com).";
        return;
    }

    errorLabel.Text = string.Empty;
    ShowConfirmStep();
}

private static bool IsValidEmail(string email)
{
    // Lightweight check: something@something.something with no whitespace.
    // The server does a stricter check (contains '@' and '.'); this is the UX-level
    // gate so the user sees the error before submitting.
    var atIdx = email.IndexOf('@');
    if (atIdx <= 0) return false;                        // must have @, and not at position 0
    if (atIdx != email.LastIndexOf('@')) return false;   // only one @

    var dotIdx = email.IndexOf('.', atIdx + 1);
    if (dotIdx < 0 || dotIdx == atIdx + 1) return false; // must have . after @, not immediately
    if (dotIdx == email.Length - 1) return false;        // must have something after the .

    return !email.Any(char.IsWhiteSpace);
}
```

**What it does:**

- Allows empty email (optional field).
- If filled, requires at least `x@y.z` — with a real character before `@`, at least one character between `@` and `.`, and at least one character after the last `.`.
- Rejects whitespace anywhere.
- Blocks progression to step 2 with an inline error if invalid.

The server still does its own check on submit — this is just the UX gate.

## What we're building

**Rule:** a ticket can only be cancelled by the employee who logged it, and only if it's still `Pending`. Once cancelled, `Status = "Cancelled"` and `IsActive = false` — the ticket disappears from the default grid (which filters by `IsActive == true`).

**Status choice:** you said "reuse Dismiss." But your existing `Dismiss()` method sets `Status = "Dismissed"`. Two options:

- **A. Reuse Dismiss** — status becomes "Dismissed", IsActive stays true, ticket still shows in grid with "Dismissed" status.
- **B. New method `Cancel()`** — status becomes "Cancelled", IsActive becomes false, ticket disappears from grid entirely (soft-delete).

You said "rename to Cancel" and "soft delete" earlier, which matches **B**. Going with B.

# File 1 — `CRM_Morcaffein.domain/entities/Feedback.cs`

Add a `Cancel` method next to `Dismiss`:

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Soft-deletes the ticket. The staff member who logged it cancels their own
/// ticket (e.g. logged in error). Ticket disappears from the default grid
/// (which filters by IsActive) but stays in the DB for audit.
/// </summary>
public void Cancel(int cancelledByEmployeeId, string? reason = null)
{
    if (cancelledByEmployeeId <= 0)
        throw new ArgumentException("Cancelling employee ID is required.");
    if (cancelledByEmployeeId != LoggedBy)
        throw new InvalidOperationException("Only the employee who logged this ticket can cancel it.");
    if (!Status.Equals("Pending", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
        throw new InvalidOperationException($"Only pending tickets can be cancelled (current status: {Status}).");

    Status = "Cancelled";
    IsActive = false;
    DecidedBy = cancelledByEmployeeId;
    DecidedAt = DateTime.UtcNow;
    DecisionNotes = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(reason) ? null : reason.Trim();
}
```

**What it does:**

- Enforces `cancelledByEmployeeId == LoggedBy` — only the logger can cancel.
- Enforces `Status == "Pending"` — can't cancel a resolved/dismissed ticket.
- Sets `IsActive = false` — the soft delete.
- Records who and when.

**Note:** `IsActive` is on `BaseEntity` and is settable (from the earlier refactor). If it's private-set in your version, change it to public-set first.

# File 2 — `CRM_Morcaffein.api/Controllers/FeedbackController.cs`

Add a new endpoint after `LogFeedback`:

```csharp
// POST api/tenant/{companyId}/feedback/{id}/cancel
[HttpPost("{id:int}/cancel")]
public async Task<ActionResult<FeedbackResponseDto>> CancelFeedback(
    int companyId,
    int id,
    [FromBody] CancelFeedbackRequest request)
{
    if (request.CancelledBy <= 0)
        return BadRequest(new { message = "Cancelling employee ID is required." });

    await using var tenant = await _tenantFactory.CreateAsync(companyId);

    var feedback = await tenant.Feedbacks
        .FirstOrDefaultAsync(f => f.TicketId == id);

    if (feedback is null)
        return NotFound(new { message = "Ticket not found." });

    try
    {
        feedback.Cancel(request.CancelledBy, request.Reason);
    }
    catch (InvalidOperationException ex)
    {
        return StatusCode(403, new { message = ex.Message });
    }

    try
    {
        await tenant.SaveChangesAsync();
    }
    catch (DbUpdateException ex)
    {
        return Conflict(new { message = ex.InnerException?.Message ?? ex.Message });
    }

    // Return updated ticket
    var result = await tenant.Feedbacks
        .AsNoTracking()
        .Where(f => f.TicketId == feedback.TicketId)
        .Select(f => new FeedbackResponseDto
        {
            TicketId = f.TicketId,
            CustomerId = f.CustomerId,
            CustomerName = f.Customer != null
                ? (f.Customer.FirstName + " " + f.Customer.LastName).Trim()
                : "—",
            LoggedBy = f.LoggedBy,
            LoggedByName = f.LoggedByEmployee != null
                ? (f.LoggedByEmployee.FirstName + " " + f.LoggedByEmployee.LastName).Trim()
                : "—",
            Rating = f.Rating,
            Category = f.Category,
            StaffNotes = f.StaffNotes,
            Status = f.Status,
            DateLogged = f.DateLogged,
            DecidedBy = f.DecidedBy,
            DecidedAt = f.DecidedAt,
            DecisionNotes = f.DecisionNotes
        })
        .FirstAsync();

    return Ok(result);
}
```

## The logic goes in the API controller instead

In `CRM_Morcaffein.api/Controllers/FeedbackController.cs`, the endpoint does the validation and mutation directly:

```csharp
// POST api/tenant/{companyId}/feedback/{id}/cancel
[HttpPost("{id:int}/cancel")]
public async Task<ActionResult<FeedbackResponseDto>> CancelFeedback(
    int companyId,
    int id,
    [FromBody] CancelFeedbackRequest request)
{
    if (request.CancelledBy <= 0)
        return BadRequest(new { message = "Cancelling employee ID is required." });

    await using var tenant = await _tenantFactory.CreateAsync(companyId);

    var feedback = await tenant.Feedbacks
        .FirstOrDefaultAsync(f => f.TicketId == id);

    if (feedback is null)
        return NotFound(new { message = "Ticket not found." });

    // ---- Business rules (moved here from the entity) ----
    if (feedback.LoggedBy != request.CancelledBy)
        return StatusCode(403, new { message = "Only the employee who logged this ticket can cancel it." });

    if (!feedback.Status.Equals("Pending", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
        return StatusCode(403, new { message = $"Only pending tickets can be cancelled (current status: {feedback.Status})." });

    // ---- Apply the cancellation ----
    feedback.Status = "Cancelled";
    feedback.IsActive = false;
    feedback.DecidedBy = request.CancelledBy;
    feedback.DecidedAt = DateTime.UtcNow;
    feedback.DecisionNotes = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(request.Reason) ? null : request.Reason.Trim();
    feedback.UpdatedAt = DateTime.UtcNow;

    try
    {
        await tenant.SaveChangesAsync();
    }
    catch (DbUpdateException ex)
    {
        return Conflict(new { message = ex.InnerException?.Message ?? ex.Message });
    }

    // Return updated ticket
    var result = await tenant.Feedbacks
        .AsNoTracking()
        .Where(f => f.TicketId == feedback.TicketId)
        .Select(f => new FeedbackResponseDto
        {
            TicketId = f.TicketId,
            CustomerId = f.CustomerId,
            CustomerName = f.Customer != null
                ? (f.Customer.FirstName + " " + f.Customer.LastName).Trim()
                : "—",
            LoggedBy = f.LoggedBy,
            LoggedByName = f.LoggedByEmployee != null
                ? (f.LoggedByEmployee.FirstName + " " + f.LoggedByEmployee.LastName).Trim()
                : "—",
            Rating = f.Rating,
            Category = f.Category,
            StaffNotes = f.StaffNotes,
            Status = f.Status,
            DateLogged = f.DateLogged,
            DecidedBy = f.DecidedBy,
            DecidedAt = f.DecidedAt,
            DecisionNotes = f.DecisionNotes
        })
        .FirstAsync();

    return Ok(result);
}
```

**What changed:**

- The `Cancel` method is gone from the entity.
- The ownership check, pending check, and mutation all happen inline in the controller.
- Same pattern as everything else we've done — the entity is a data bag, the controller owns the rules.

**Files 2–6 from my previous message stay the same** (the DTO, the API client method, the WinForms controller passthrough, and the View button). Only File 1 changes: **don't add a method to `Feedback.cs`.** The controller does it all.

```csharp
using CRM_Morcaffein.Controllers;
using CRM_Morcaffein.api.DTOs;
using CRM_Morcaffein.Session;
using CRM_Morcaffein.Theme;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.winforms.Views.Controls
{
    /// <summary>
    /// The Feedback tab: ticket grid + read-only drawer. Staff log and view; deciding
    /// (resolve/dismiss/award) is a manager concern on a future surface.
    ///
    /// Staff can also CANCEL their own pending tickets (soft-delete, only the employee
    /// who logged it). Cancelling hides the ticket from the grid.
    ///
    /// API-backed: all ticket data comes from the API. No mock.
    /// </summary>
    public partial class FeedbackManagementView : UserControl
    {
        private readonly FeedbackController _controller;
        private readonly BindingSource _ticketsBindingSource = new();

        private FeedbackResponseDto? _selectedTicket;
        private Button _cancelTicketBtn = null!;

        public FeedbackManagementView()
        {
            _controller = new FeedbackController();
            InitializeComponent();

            ConfigureTicketsGridColumns();

            ticketsGrid.DataSource = _ticketsBindingSource;
            ticketsGrid.SelectionChanged += TicketsGrid_SelectionChanged;

            searchTxtBx.TextChanged += (s, e) => ReloadTickets();
            logFeedbackBtn.Click += (s, e) => OpenLogFeedbackModal();

            cardHeaderPanel.Resize += (s, e) => PositionActionButton();
            PositionActionButton();

            BuildCancelButton();

            Load += async (s, e) => await ReloadTicketsAsync();
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Adds the "Cancel Ticket" button to the drawer's bottom. Built here in code
        /// rather than the Designer so the drawer layout doesn't need to be touched.
        /// </summary>
        private void BuildCancelButton()
        {
            _cancelTicketBtn = new Button
            {
                Text = "Cancel Ticket",
                Dock = DockStyle.Bottom,
                Height = 36,
                FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat,
                BackColor = BrandPalette.ButtonSecondaryFill,
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.ButtonSecondaryText,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9.5f),
                Cursor = Cursors.Hand,
                Visible = false,
            };
            _cancelTicketBtn.FlatAppearance.BorderSize = 0;
            _cancelTicketBtn.Click += CancelTicketBtn_Click;

            // Add to the drawer content panel; Dock=Bottom pins it below the flow content.
            drawerContentPanel.Controls.Add(_cancelTicketBtn);
            _cancelTicketBtn.BringToFront();
        }

        private void PositionActionButton()
        {
            logFeedbackBtn.Left = cardHeaderPanel.ClientSize.Width - logFeedbackBtn.Width - 16;
            logFeedbackBtn.Top = 14;
        }

        private async Task ReloadTicketsAsync()
        {
            var previousId = _selectedTicket?.TicketId;
            var tickets = await _controller.GetTicketsAsync(searchTxtBx.Text);
            _ticketsBindingSource.DataSource = tickets;

            ticketsGrid.ClearSelection();
            try { ticketsGrid.CurrentCell = null; } catch { /* not always allowed; ignore */ }

            var stillPresent = previousId.HasValue
                ? tickets.FirstOrDefault(t => t.TicketId == previousId.Value)
                : null;

            if (stillPresent != null)
            {
                SelectTicketRowById(stillPresent.TicketId);
            }
            else
            {
                _selectedTicket = null;
                RefreshDrawer();
            }
        }

        private async void ReloadTickets()
        {
            try { await ReloadTicketsAsync(); }
            catch (Exception ex) { MessageBox.Show(FindForm(), ex.Message, "Error loading tickets"); }
        }

        private void TicketsGrid_SelectionChanged(object? sender, EventArgs e)
        {
            _selectedTicket = ticketsGrid.CurrentRow?.DataBoundItem as FeedbackResponseDto;
            RefreshDrawer();
        }

        private async void OpenLogFeedbackModal()
        {
            using var form = new FrmLogFeedback(_controller, EmployeeSession.Current!.EmployeeId);

            if (form.ShowDialog(FindForm()) == DialogResult.OK && form.CreatedFeedback != null)
            {
                await ReloadTicketsAsync();
                SelectTicketRowById(form.CreatedFeedback.TicketId);
            }
        }

        private void RefreshDrawer()
        {
            var ticket = _selectedTicket;
            if (ticket is null)
            {
                drawerEmptyLabel.Visible = true;
                drawerContentPanel.Visible = false;
                _cancelTicketBtn.Visible = false;
                return;
            }

            drawerEmptyLabel.Visible = false;
            drawerContentPanel.Visible = true;

            ticketCustomerLabel.Text = ticket.CustomerName;
            ticketRatingLabel.Text = new string('★', ticket.Rating) + new string('☆', 5 - ticket.Rating);
            ticketCategoryLabel.Text = $"Category: {ticket.Category}";
            ticketStatusLabel.Text = $"Status: {ticket.Status}";
            ticketDateLabel.Text = $"Logged {ticket.DateLogged:yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm} by {ticket.LoggedByName}";
            ticketNotesLabel.Text = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(ticket.StaffNotes) ? "(no notes)" : ticket.StaffNotes;

            // Cancel button is visible only when:
            //   - ticket status is Pending (not already resolved/dismissed/cancelled)
            //   - the currently logged-in employee is the one who logged the ticket
            var currentEmployeeId = EmployeeSession.Current?.EmployeeId;
            _cancelTicketBtn.Visible =
                ticket.Status.Equals("Pending", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) &&
                ticket.LoggedBy == currentEmployeeId;
        }

        private async void CancelTicketBtn_Click(object? sender, EventArgs e)
        {
            if (_selectedTicket is null) return;

            var confirm = MessageBox.Show(
                FindForm(),
                $"Cancel ticket #{_selectedTicket.TicketId}? It will be hidden from the grid.",
                "Cancel Ticket",
                MessageBoxButtons.YesNo,
                MessageBoxIcon.Warning);

            if (confirm != DialogResult.Yes)
                return;

            try
            {
                var employeeId = EmployeeSession.Current?.EmployeeId
                    ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("No employee session.");

                await _controller.CancelTicketAsync(_selectedTicket.TicketId, employeeId);

                // The ticket is now IsActive=false, so it drops off the next fetch.
                await ReloadTicketsAsync();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                MessageBox.Show(FindForm(), ex.Message, "Cancel failed");
            }
        }

        private void SelectTicketRowById(int ticketId)
        {
            foreach (DataGridViewRow row in ticketsGrid.Rows)
            {
                if (row.DataBoundItem is FeedbackResponseDto t && t.TicketId == ticketId)
                {
                    ticketsGrid.ClearSelection();
                    row.Selected = true;
                    ticketsGrid.CurrentCell = row.Cells[0];
                    _selectedTicket = t;
                    RefreshDrawer();
                    break;
                }
            }
        }

        private void ConfigureTicketsGridColumns()
        {
            ticketsGrid.Columns.Clear();
            ticketsGrid.Columns.Add(new DataGridViewTextBoxColumn
            {
                Name = nameof(FeedbackResponseDto.TicketId),
                DataPropertyName = nameof(FeedbackResponseDto.TicketId),
                HeaderText = "Ticket #",
                Width = 70,
            });
            ticketsGrid.Columns.Add(new DataGridViewTextBoxColumn
            {
                Name = nameof(FeedbackResponseDto.CustomerName),
                DataPropertyName = nameof(FeedbackResponseDto.CustomerName),
                HeaderText = "Customer",
                Width = 160,
                AutoSizeMode = DataGridViewAutoSizeColumnMode.Fill,
            });
            ticketsGrid.Columns.Add(new DataGridViewTextBoxColumn
            {
                Name = nameof(FeedbackResponseDto.Rating),
                DataPropertyName = nameof(FeedbackResponseDto.Rating),
                HeaderText = "Rating",
                Width = 60,
            });
            ticketsGrid.Columns.Add(new DataGridViewTextBoxColumn
            {
                Name = nameof(FeedbackResponseDto.Category),
                DataPropertyName = nameof(FeedbackResponseDto.Category),
                HeaderText = "Category",
                Width = 90,
            });
            ticketsGrid.Columns.Add(new DataGridViewTextBoxColumn
            {
                Name = nameof(FeedbackResponseDto.Status),
                DataPropertyName = nameof(FeedbackResponseDto.Status),
                HeaderText = "Status",
                Width = 90,
            });
            ticketsGrid.Columns.Add(new DataGridViewTextBoxColumn
            {
                Name = nameof(FeedbackResponseDto.DateLogged),
                DataPropertyName = nameof(FeedbackResponseDto.DateLogged),
                HeaderText = "Logged",
                Width = 130,
                DefaultCellStyle = new DataGridViewCellStyle { Format = "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm" },
            });
        }
    }
}
```

Good questions. Let me answer the database one first, because it's the more important one.

---

## What "cancel" does in the database

The `Cancel` endpoint I wrote does **not delete anything**. It updates the `Feedbacks` row:

```csharp
feedback.Status = "Cancelled";      // status changes from "Pending" to "Cancelled"
feedback.IsActive = false;          // BaseEntity flag → hides the row from queries
feedback.DecidedBy = request.CancelledBy;
feedback.DecidedAt = DateTime.UtcNow;
feedback.DecisionNotes = "...";     // whatever reason was given
feedback.UpdatedAt = DateTime.UtcNow;
```

So in the DB:

- The row is **still there**. All fields — customer, rating, category, original staff notes, date logged — are unchanged.
- Two fields changed: `Status` (now `"Cancelled"`) and `IsActive` (now `0`).
- Three audit fields added: `DecidedBy`, `DecidedAt`, `DecisionNotes`.

**Nothing is deleted. It's a soft-delete via `IsActive = false`.**

## Why it "disappears" from the grid

The API's `GetTickets` endpoint filters by:

```csharp
.Where(f => f.IsActive)
```

Since `IsActive = false` after cancel, the cancelled ticket is excluded. The grid never sees it. **But it's still in the database.**

## How to see cancelled tickets

In SSMS, run:

```sql
SELECT * FROM Feedbacks WHERE IsActive = 0;
```

You'll see every cancelled ticket, with `Status = 'Cancelled'` and the cancellation notes.

If you ever want a "Show cancelled" toggle in the UI, you'd add a query parameter to `GetTickets` like `?includeInactive=true` and remove the `IsActive` filter when set. **Not building it now** unless you want it.

## Why soft-delete and not hard-delete

- **Audit trail.** You can prove what was cancelled, by whom, when, and why. Important for a system that awards points and tracks customer interactions.
- **Reversible.** If a staff member cancels by mistake, an admin can flip `IsActive` back to `true`. Hard delete would lose the data forever.
- **FK safety.** `Feedback` has relationships (to `Customer`, `Employee`) that would break with a hard delete in some scenarios.
- **Standard practice.** Most production systems soft-delete for these reasons.

---

```text
The record is kept for audit but is no longer actionable.
```

## File 1 — `CRM_Morcaffein.api/DTOs/PagedResponse.cs` (new)

```csharp
namespace CRM_Morcaffein.api.DTOs;

/// <summary>
/// Standard shape for any paginated list endpoint. Reused by Feedback, Customers,
/// Products — anything that returns rows in pages.
/// </summary>
public class PagedResponse<T>
{
    public List<T> Items { get; set; } = new();
    public int TotalCount { get; set; }
    public int Page { get; set; }
    public int PageSize { get; set; }

    public int TotalPages => PageSize <= 0
        ? 0
        : (int)Math.Ceiling((double)TotalCount / PageSize);

    public bool HasPrevious => Page > 1;
    public bool HasNext => Page < TotalPages;
}
```

**Note:** `TotalPages`, `HasPrevious`, `HasNext` are computed properties. They serialize to JSON too (which the client can just as easily ignore and recompute). Harmless.

```csharp
[HttpGet]
public async Task<ActionResult<List<FeedbackResponseDto>>> GetTickets(
    int companyId,
    [FromQuery] string? search)
{
```
