---

Got it — you want the drinks panel to **paint instantly** when a customer is searched, not "load progressively" or "appear over 200-500ms." That's a specific goal, and it has a specific cause.

## Why it doesn't appear all at once

Every card renders independently. When the panel is added to the visible form, WinForms paints each card as it lays it out — card 1 paints, card 2 paints, etc. If any individual card is slow to paint (image decode, anti-aliased drawing), the panel appears to "fill in" progressively rather than appearing whole.

There are three ways to make it appear **all at once**:

**Option 1 — Pre-render the panel off-screen, then swap it in.** Build the new flow panel entirely in memory (all 34 cards created, laid out, painted once to a buffer), then replace the old one in a single `Controls.Add`. The user never sees the intermediate state.

**Option 2 — Delay painting until all cards are ready.** Suspend painting on the flow panel while cards are being added, resume after. WinForms has `SuspendLayout()` (already used) but not `SuspendPaint()`. You'd need to hook the WM_SETREDRAW message to freeze the panel while building.

**Option 3 — Reduce each card's paint time.** Most cards paint fast; the slow ones are those loading images on first paint. If images are pre-loaded, cards paint in ~1ms each, and the "progressive" appearance disappears because 34ms is imperceptible.

**My recommendation: Option 2.** It's the cleanest "appears all at once" fix, and it's a well-known WinForms pattern (freeze the control with `WM_SETREDRAW`, build, unfreeze).

## Fix — freeze the panel while building, unfreeze when done

Add this helper somewhere in `TransactionView`:

```csharp
[System.Runtime.InteropServices.DllImport("user32.dll")]
private static extern int SendMessage(IntPtr hWnd, int wMsg, bool wParam, int lParam);

private const int WM_SETREDRAW = 0x000B;

private static void SuspendRedraw(Control control)
{
    SendMessage(control.Handle, WM_SETREDRAW, false, 0);
}

private static void ResumeRedraw(Control control)
{
    SendMessage(control.Handle, WM_SETREDRAW, true, 0);
    control.Refresh();
}
```

Then in `RefreshProductsPanel()`:

```csharp
private void RefreshProductsPanel()
{
    _productsFlowPanel.SuspendLayout();
    SuspendRedraw(_productsFlowPanel);   // ← freeze painting
    try
    {
        _productsFlowPanel.Controls.Clear();
        if (_controller is null) return;

        var products = _controller.GetProducts(_selectedCategory, _productSearchTxtBx.Text);
        foreach (var product in products)
        {
            var card = new ProductCardControl(product);
            card.CardClicked += (s, e) => OpenCustomizerForNewItem(product);
            card.SizeQuickAdded += (s, size) => QuickAddToCart(product, size);
            _productsFlowPanel.Controls.Add(card);
        }
    }
    finally
    {
        ResumeRedraw(_productsFlowPanel);   // ← unfreeze + single refresh
        _productsFlowPanel.ResumeLayout();
    }
}
```

## What this does

- `SuspendRedraw` tells Windows: don't paint this control, no matter how many times it's invalidated.
- All 34 cards are added and laid out. Windows doesn't render any of them yet.
- `ResumeRedraw` turns painting back on and forces a single `Refresh()`, which paints the entire panel in one pass.
- The user sees an all-at-once appearance — nothing progressive.

**Same trick applies to any panel where you build a lot of controls.** It's the WinForms standard for "build a big batch, then show it."

## One more thing that helps

The images are still loading lazily on each card's first paint. With `SuspendRedraw`, they load **during the frozen phase**, then all paint at once when resumed. So the freeze also covers the image loads.

**But** — the very first time you search, the images have to load from disk (34 files). That's still slow (maybe 200-500ms for all of them). Subsequent searches reuse the same in-memory images? **No** — the images are cached per card instance, and we clear all cards on refresh. So every refresh re-reads the images from disk.

**The real fix for that:** cache images at the file-path level. But that's more code, and it's not needed if `SuspendRedraw` gets you "all at once" — because the user doesn't see the interim state, only the final painted panel.

**Do this:**

1. Add the `SuspendRedraw`/`ResumeRedraw` helpers and the two calls in `RefreshProductsPanel`.
2. Rebuild, test — search a customer, see if the drinks panel now appears whole.

**Report.** If it appears whole → done, move to tab order (A). If it still "fills in" progressively, then the paint itself is the issue, and we go to Option 1 (build off-screen) or Option 3 (cache images globally).

OK, that rules out the painting-freeze being sufficient. The progressive fill means cards are **painted** one at a time as they become visible, not that they're slow to build. Freezing suppress only helps if the paint work is what's slow — but if the paint work is fast and the *layout* is what's showing up incrementally, we need to look elsewhere.

## Let me diagnose before writing more code

The progressive fill could be one of three things:

**A. Cards are added one at a time and each addition triggers a layout + partial paint.**
Even with `SuspendRedraw`, WinForms may still be processing layout events and painting the visible slice of the flow panel as cards are appended. The freeze doesn't cover everything.

**B. The images are loading per-card during paint.**
Each card's `OnPaint` calls `TryLoadImage` on first paint. That reads a JPG from disk (~5-15ms per file). 34 images = ~200-500ms of disk I/O across the panel's paint pass. So the first card paints, then the next, etc., and the user sees them appear progressively because each paint pass is doing disk I/O.

**C. The cards themselves aren't the issue — the panel is just being added and repainted because the flow panel grows as cards are added.**
Even with layout suspended, adding a control triggers `ControlAdded`, which can trigger repaint scheduling.

**The most likely culprit is B.** Loading images lazily during paint is exactly the pattern that produces progressive appearance.

## Fix — preload all images before adding cards

If images are loaded **before** the cards are added (or if we pre-warm them at the file cache level), the paint pass is pure GDI drawing with no disk I/O, and 34 cards paint in one fast pass.

**Two ways to do it:**

**Option 1 — Preload the images for the specific product list before building cards.**

In `RefreshProductsPanel`, before the loop, iterate the products and touch their images:

```csharp
// Preload all product images before adding any card. Otherwise each card's
// first paint reads its JPG from disk (~5-15ms each), and the panel fills in
// progressively as they load.
foreach (var product in products)
{
    if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(product.LocalImagePath))
    {
        var fullPath = Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, product.LocalImagePath);
        if (File.Exists(fullPath))
        {
            // Load bytes into memory now; the OS file cache keeps them warm for the
            // card's own load, which will hit the cache instead of disk.
            try { _ = File.ReadAllBytes(fullPath); } catch { }
        }
    }
}
```

**What this does:** reads every image file into memory once, before the cards are built. The cards' `TryLoadImage` calls still run, but they now hit the OS file cache instead of the physical disk. That alone eliminates most of the progressive-fill delay.

**Option 2 — A proper image cache keyed by path.**

A static `Dictionary<string, Image>` that returns the same `Image` instance for the same file path. The first load reads from disk; every subsequent card that references the same file (and every subsequent refresh) reuses the cached bitmap.

**Bigger change, but it makes even the first load fast on the second search.**

## Which one do you want?

- **Option 1** — 5-minute change, hit the OS cache, keeps cards self-contained.
- **Option 2** — 20-minute change, proper image cache, faster across the board.

**My recommendation: Option 2.** It's the right way to do it, and it eliminates the progressive fill permanently. The extra 15 minutes is worth it.

**Confirm Option 2, and I'll write it** — a small `ProductImageCache` static class, plus a change in `ProductCardControl` to use it instead of `TryLoadImage` directly. About 60 lines total across two files.

**Or confirm Option 1** if you want the smaller change first.

**Which one?**

Pick one:

1. **The drinks panel is blank** — no cards at all.
2. **The cards appear, but no images** — cards render, images show the ☕ placeholder.
3. **The app crashes or hangs** when you search a customer.

## Most likely causes for each

**If (1) — drinks panel blank:**
The `_controller` is null, or `GetProducts` returned nothing, or the product loop threw and was swallowed. Also possible: the `SuspendRedraw`/`ResumeRedraw` didn't get paired correctly, and the panel was suspended and never resumed. **Check `RefreshProductsPanel` — is `ResumeRedraw` inside the `finally`?** If it's after the `try`, an exception in the `try` skips it, and the panel stays frozen forever.

**If (2) — cards show but no images:**
The preload loop is failing silently (the `catch { }` swallows everything), and then the cards fall back to the placeholder. Or the preload succeeded but the cards still can't find the file at paint time — meaning `AppContext.BaseDirectory` differs between the preload context and the card's own context. **Both should be the same** since they're the same process. So this is unlikely unless the images themselves are broken.

**If (3) — crash/hang:**
Could be `File.ReadAllBytes` throwing on a locked file, or the preload loop iterating over a null product list, or something downstream. **The `catch { }` should swallow file errors** — if there's a crash, it's elsewhere.

**If (4) — search fails:**
Unrelated to the image preload. Something else broke.

## The most common mistake here

**Look at where you placed the preload loop.** It has to be **after** `products` is fetched from the controller but **before** the loop that creates cards.

Correct order in `RefreshProductsPanel`:

```csharp
private void RefreshProductsPanel()
{
    _productsFlowPanel.SuspendLayout();
    SuspendRedraw(_productsFlowPanel);
    try
    {
        _productsFlowPanel.Controls.Clear();
        if (_controller is null) return;

        var products = _controller.GetProducts(_selectedCategory, _productSearchTxtBx.Text);

        // ← preload loop goes HERE — after products is fetched, before cards are made

        foreach (var product in products)
        {
            // ... create cards ...
        }
    }
    finally
    {
        ResumeRedraw(_productsFlowPanel);
        _productsFlowPanel.ResumeLayout();
    }
}
```

**If the preload loop is before `var products = ...`, or if `products` isn't in scope there, that's the bug.**

**If the preload loop accidentally replaced the card-creation loop instead of going above it**, then no cards get created. That would produce "nothing is loading."

Right — the freeze trick isn't enough because the actual paint cost is still there. Let me diagnose it properly instead of guessing.

## What's actually happening

When `RefreshProductsPanel` runs:

1. Old cards cleared
2. New 34 cards created (each a `Panel` with child controls, an image, and custom `OnPaint`)
3. Added to the flow panel
4. Panel unfreezes → Windows paints the whole panel once

**The freeze makes it *one* paint instead of many.** But that one paint still has to draw 34 cards × ~5-6 controls each = ~200 controls. Windows paints them in z-order, one after another. Even at 1ms per control, that's 200ms of visible progressive rendering.

**The real problem is that each `ProductCardControl` has child controls** (the size-row Panel with N Buttons). Every child is a real HWND-backed WinForms control, and each one paints independently. Even on a frozen parent, WinForms paints children as it iterates through them.

**What "appears all at once" requires:** the cards must NOT be built from child controls. They need to be **pure `OnPaint` drawings** — one `Panel` per card, all visuals drawn in `OnPaint`. Then there's one control per card instead of 5-6. 34 controls instead of 200.

That's the fundamental reason you're seeing progressive fill. Not the freeze technique — the control count.

## And why "changing the customer repaints the whole thing"

Because `SelectCustomerAsync` calls `RefreshProductsPanel()` every time. That clears and rebuilds 34 cards. There's no reason to.

The cards only depend on:

- `_selectedCategory` (which the user can change)
- `_productSearchTxtBx.Text` (which the user can change)

If neither changed since the last build, **skip the rebuild**. Same signature = same cards = don't touch.

That's the "Fix B" I mentioned a while back. It eliminates the customer-change repaint entirely.

## Two fixes, both needed

**Fix B (the cheap one):** Skip `RefreshProductsPanel` when the category + search haven't changed.

**Fix C (the actual "all at once" fix):** Make `ProductCardControl` control-less — draw everything in `OnPaint`, no child Panel, no child Buttons.

**Do B first.** It's a 3-line change and it stops the repaint on customer change. Then decide whether C is worth it.

## Fix B — skip the rebuild when the filter hasn't changed

Add a field near the top of `TransactionView`:

```csharp
private string _lastProductFilterSignature = string.Empty;
```

Replace `RefreshProductsPanel` with:

```csharp
private void RefreshProductsPanel()
{
    // Skip the rebuild if neither the category nor the search text has changed
    // since the last build. The products list is identical — no reason to
    // clear and rebuild 34 cards, which is what makes customer changes feel slow.
    var signature = $"{_selectedCategory}|{_productSearchTxtBx.Text}";
    if (signature == _lastProductFilterSignature && _productsFlowPanel.Controls.Count > 0)
        return;

    _lastProductFilterSignature = signature;

    _productsFlowPanel.SuspendLayout();
    SuspendRedraw(_productsFlowPanel);
    try
    {
        _productsFlowPanel.Controls.Clear();
        if (_controller is null) return;

        var products = _controller.GetProducts(_selectedCategory, _productSearchTxtBx.Text);

        foreach (var product in products)
        {
            if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(product.LocalImagePath))
            {
                var fullPath = Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, product.LocalImagePath);
                if (File.Exists(fullPath))
                {
                    try { _ = File.ReadAllBytes(fullPath); } catch { }
                }
            }
        }

        foreach (var product in products)
        {
            var card = new ProductCardControl(product);
            card.CardClicked += (s, e) => OpenCustomizerForNewItem(product);
            card.SizeQuickAdded += (s, size) => QuickAddToCart(product, size);
            _productsFlowPanel.Controls.Add(card);
        }
    }
    finally
    {
        ResumeRedraw(_productsFlowPanel);
        _productsFlowPanel.ResumeLayout();
    }
}
```

**Effect:** on the second customer search, if category and search text are unchanged, the method returns immediately. No rebuild. No repaint. Instant.

**When you change category or type in search** — the signature changes, so it rebuilds (correctly, because the products are different).

## What Fix C does

Each card becomes a **single Panel with NO child controls.** Everything is drawn in `OnPaint`:

- Product image (from `LocalImagePath`)
- Product name (ellipsized)
- "from ₱X" price line
- Size buttons — drawn as rectangles in `OnPaint`, not real `Button` controls
- Hover highlight — drawn by tracking `MouseMove`

**Result:** each card is 1 control instead of 5-6. 34 cards = 34 controls instead of ~200. Paint pass is dramatically faster, and the panel appears all at once.

- **Size buttons are no longer real Buttons.** They're just drawn rectangles. Same visual result, but no WinForms Button behavior (no keyboard focus, no default button hover effects).
- **Hover state is manual.** We draw a lighter shade when the mouse is over a size rect. It works fine, just more code.

**What you keep:**

- Same card size, same layout
- Same click behavior on the size buttons
- Same card-body-click → customizer modal
- Same image, same placeholder glyph fallback
- Same fonts, colors, borders

**What you gain:**

- 34 controls instead of ~200
- All-at-once rendering
- Faster refresh

Here's the full control-less rewrite. Single Panel, no child controls, everything drawn in `OnPaint`, size buttons hit-tested manually. Same visual result.

```csharp
using CRM_Morcaffein.domain.entities;
using CRM_Morcaffein.Theme;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.winforms.Views.Controls
{
    /// <summary>
    /// A single drink card: product image + name + "from ₱price", with a row of size
    /// quick-add buttons pinned to the bottom. Tapping a size adds that size, qty 1, no
    /// modifiers, straight to the cart. Clicking the card body opens the full customizer.
    ///
    /// Control-less by design: NO child controls. Everything (image, text, size buttons)
    /// is drawn in OnPaint, and size-button clicks are hit-tested in OnMouseDown. This
    /// reduces each card from ~5-6 controls to 1, which is what makes the whole drinks
    /// panel paint fast and appear all at once instead of filling in progressively.
    /// </summary>
    public class ProductCardControl : Panel
    {
        public Product Product { get; }

        /// <summary>Card body clicked (not a size button) — host opens the full customizer modal.</summary>
        public event EventHandler? CardClicked;

        /// <summary>A size button was tapped — host adds that size directly to the cart.</summary>
        public event EventHandler<ProductSize>? SizeQuickAdded;

        private const int SizeRowHeight = 26;
        private const int ImageBandHeight = 64;
        private const int Padding = 8;

        private static readonly string[] SizeLabels = { "S", "M", "L", "XL" };

        private readonly List<ProductSize> _sizes;
        private Image? _cachedImage;
        private bool _imageLoadAttempted;

        // The rects of the size buttons, computed once (their position doesn't change).
        private Rectangle[] _sizeButtonRects = Array.Empty<Rectangle>();

        // Index of the size button currently under the mouse, or -1.
        private int _hoveredSizeIndex = -1;

        public ProductCardControl(Product product)
        {
            Product = product;
            _sizes = product.ProductSizes.ToList();

            Size = new Size(150, 156);
            Margin = new Padding(8);
            BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary;
            Cursor = Cursors.Hand;

            SetStyle(ControlStyles.UserPaint | ControlStyles.AllPaintingInWmPaint
                   | ControlStyles.OptimizedDoubleBuffer | ControlStyles.ResizeRedraw, true);

            // Compute the size-button rects once. They're laid out evenly across the
            // full width of the row at the bottom.
            if (_sizes.Count > 0)
            {
                _sizeButtonRects = new Rectangle[_sizes.Count];
                var buttonWidth = Width / _sizes.Count;
                for (int i = 0; i < _sizes.Count; i++)
                {
                    var x = i * buttonWidth;
                    var w = (i == _sizes.Count - 1) ? Width - x : buttonWidth;
                    _sizeButtonRects[i] = new Rectangle(x, Height - SizeRowHeight, w, SizeRowHeight);
                }
            }

            // Hover on the card itself (tint background). Size-button hover is handled
            // separately below via mouse-move over their rects.
            MouseEnter += (s, e) => { BackColor = BrandPalette.Tint90; Invalidate(); };
            MouseLeave += (s, e) =>
            {
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary;
                if (_hoveredSizeIndex != -1) { _hoveredSizeIndex = -1; Invalidate(); }
                else { Invalidate(); }
            };
        }

        protected override void Dispose(bool disposing)
        {
            if (disposing)
            {
                _cachedImage?.Dispose();
                _cachedImage = null;
            }
            base.Dispose(disposing);
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // PAINTING
        // =====================================================================

        protected override void OnPaint(PaintEventArgs e)
        {
            var g = e.Graphics;
            g.SmoothingMode = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.SmoothingMode.AntiAlias;
            g.InterpolationMode = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.InterpolationMode.HighQualityBicubic;

            // Card border
            using (var borderPen = new Pen(BrandPalette.Border))
                g.DrawRectangle(borderPen, 0, 0, Width - 1, Height - 1);

            // Image band
            var imageRect = new Rectangle(Padding, Padding, Width - Padding * 2, ImageBandHeight);
            DrawProductImage(g, imageRect);

            // Product name (single line, ellipsized if needed)
            using (var nameFont = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(9.5f))
            using (var nameBrush = new SolidBrush(BrandPalette.NeutralText))
            {
                var nameRect = new RectangleF(Padding, imageRect.Bottom + 6, Width - Padding * 2, 32);
                var sf = new StringFormat { Trimming = StringTrimming.EllipsisCharacter, FormatFlags = StringFormatFlags.NoWrap };
                g.DrawString(Product.ProductName, nameFont, nameBrush, nameRect, sf);
            }

            // "from ₱X" price
            using (var priceFont = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9f))
            using (var priceBrush = new SolidBrush(BrandPalette.NeutralTextMuted))
            {
                g.DrawString($"from ₱{Product.BasePrice:0}", priceFont, priceBrush,
                    Padding, Height - SizeRowHeight - 20);
            }

            // Size buttons (drawn, not real controls)
            DrawSizeRow(g);
        }

        private void DrawSizeRow(Graphics g)
        {
            if (_sizes.Count == 0) return;

            for (int i = 0; i < _sizes.Count; i++)
            {
                var rect = _sizeButtonRects[i];

                // Hover state: lighten the fill for the hovered button.
                var fill = (i == _hoveredSizeIndex) ? BrandPalette.Shade10 : BrandPalette.Brand;

                using (var brush = new SolidBrush(fill))
                    g.FillRectangle(brush, rect);

                var label = i < SizeLabels.Length ? SizeLabels[i] : (i + 1).ToString();

                using var font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(8f);
                var textSize = g.MeasureString(label, font);
                g.DrawString(label, font, Brushes.White,
                    rect.X + (rect.Width - textSize.Width) / 2,
                    rect.Y + (rect.Height - textSize.Height) / 2);

                // Thin separator line between buttons (not after the last one)
                if (i < _sizes.Count - 1)
                {
                    using var sepPen = new Pen(BrandPalette.Tint25);
                    g.DrawLine(sepPen, rect.Right, rect.Top + 4, rect.Right, rect.Bottom - 4);
                }
            }
        }

        private void DrawProductImage(Graphics g, Rectangle imageRect)
        {
            if (!_imageLoadAttempted)
            {
                _imageLoadAttempted = true;
                _cachedImage = TryLoadImage(Product.LocalImagePath);
            }

            if (_cachedImage is not null)
            {
                var targetRatio = (float)imageRect.Width / imageRect.Height;
                var imageRatio = (float)_cachedImage.Width / _cachedImage.Height;

                int drawWidth, drawHeight;
                if (imageRatio > targetRatio)
                {
                    drawWidth = imageRect.Width;
                    drawHeight = (int)(imageRect.Width / imageRatio);
                }
                else
                {
                    drawHeight = imageRect.Height;
                    drawWidth = (int)(imageRect.Height * imageRatio);
                }

                var drawX = imageRect.X + (imageRect.Width - drawWidth) / 2;
                var drawY = imageRect.Y + (imageRect.Height - drawHeight) / 2;

                g.DrawImage(_cachedImage, drawX, drawY, drawWidth, drawHeight);
                return;
            }

            // Placeholder: tint block + coffee glyph
            using (var imgBrush = new SolidBrush(BrandPalette.Tint75))
                g.FillRectangle(imgBrush, imageRect);

            using var iconFont = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(16f);
            var iconText = "☕";
            var iconSize = g.MeasureString(iconText, iconFont);
            g.DrawString(iconText, iconFont, new SolidBrush(BrandPalette.Tint25),
                imageRect.X + (imageRect.Width - iconSize.Width) / 2,
                imageRect.Y + (imageRect.Height - iconSize.Height) / 2);
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // INTERACTION (mouse)
        // =====================================================================

        protected override void OnMouseDown(MouseEventArgs e)
        {
            base.OnMouseDown(e);

            // If the click landed on a size button, fire that event and stop.
            for (int i = 0; i < _sizeButtonRects.Length; i++)
            {
                if (_sizeButtonRects[i].Contains(e.Location))
                {
                    SizeQuickAdded?.Invoke(this, _sizes[i]);
                    return;
                }
            }

            // Otherwise, the card body was clicked.
            CardClicked?.Invoke(this, EventArgs.Empty);
        }

        protected override void OnMouseMove(MouseEventArgs e)
        {
            base.OnMouseMove(e);

            int newHover = -1;
            for (int i = 0; i < _sizeButtonRects.Length; i++)
            {
                if (_sizeButtonRects[i].Contains(e.Location)) { newHover = i; break; }
            }

            if (newHover != _hoveredSizeIndex)
            {
                _hoveredSizeIndex = newHover;
                Invalidate();
            }
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // IMAGE LOADING
        // =====================================================================

        private static Image? TryLoadImage(string? relativePath)
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(relativePath))
                return null;

            try
            {
                var fullPath = Path.IsPathRooted(relativePath)
                    ? relativePath
                    : Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, relativePath);

                if (!File.Exists(fullPath))
                    return null;

                using var stream = File.OpenRead(fullPath);
                return Image.FromStream(stream);
            }
            catch
            {
                return null;
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## What changed

- **No `BuildSizeRow()` method.** No child controls at all.
- **Size buttons are drawn in `DrawSizeRow`.**
- **Click detection is in `OnMouseDown`** — the first loop checks whether the click was inside a size button rect; if yes, fires `SizeQuickAdded`; if no, fires `CardClicked`.
- **Hover detection is in `OnMouseMove`** — tracks which size button the mouse is over, redraws on change so the hovered button shows a lighter shade.
- **`_sizeButtonRects` computed once in the constructor** (they don't move after the card is sized).

## Notes on behavior

- **Card body click**: still opens the customizer. Handled in `OnMouseDown`, so the whole card responds to left-click.
- **Size buttons**: still work identically. Hover state is a lighter brand shade. Click fires the same event.
- **Hover on the card body**: still tints the background (unchanged behavior).
- **What's missing vs. a real Button**: keyboard tab focus, mouse-down visual "pressed" state. Both are minor for a POS.

There it is — the `Padding` name collision I warned about. Your `ProductCardControl` still has the constant named `Padding`, which collides with the inherited `Panel.Padding` property. The compiler is resolving `Padding` to the inherited property (a `System.Windows.Forms.Padding` struct), not your `int` constant. So `Padding * 2` becomes `Padding-struct * 2` → error.

**73ms to build 34 cards.** That's fast. Building is not the problem.

So the 73ms is just:

- Clearing old controls
- Preloading images
- Creating 34 `ProductCardControl` objects
- Adding them to the flow panel

That's well within "instant" — under 100ms isn't perceptible.

**The progressive loading you're seeing is happening AFTER `RefreshProductsPanel` returns, during the paint pass.**

## So what's actually progressive?

Two possibilities remain:

**A. The paint pass itself is slow.** WinForms queues a paint for the flow panel after it's unfrozen. That paint draws all 34 cards. If each card's `OnPaint` takes ~10-20ms (image drawing, anti-aliased text), 34 × 15ms = ~500ms of paint time, and the user sees the cards fill in as each is drawn.

**B. Layout is being recalculated per card.** When you unfreeze the flow panel with `ResumeRedraw` (which calls `Refresh()`), the panel might be doing a full layout pass, positioning 34 children one at a time, and the paint happens as each position settles.

**A is more likely.**

## The actual fix — make each card's `OnPaint` cheaper

If 34 cards take ~500ms of paint, that's ~15ms per card. What's expensive in the card's `OnPaint`:

1. **`SmoothingMode = AntiAlias`** — expensive for text rendering. Setting it affects the whole Graphics context and every `DrawString` call after.
2. **`InterpolationMode = HighQualityBicubic`** — expensive for image scaling. Every `DrawImage` with this mode does expensive resampling.
3. **Two `DrawString` calls with new fonts per paint** — creating `Font` objects per paint is wasteful.
4. **`MeasureString` on every paint** — used for centering text.
5. **The image** — if images need to be scaled (e.g. a 400×400 source drawn into a 134×64 band), HighQualityBicubic is doing real work.

## The fix

**Replace the expensive painting operations with cheaper equivalents:**

- **Drop `HighQualityBicubic` → use `Bilinear`.** Visually indistinguishable at small sizes, much faster.
- **Drop `AntiAlias` on text.** Use `ClearTypeGridFit` or default. Anti-aliased text is nice but expensive.
- **Cache fonts as static fields** instead of allocating them per paint. Fonts are disposable — creating and disposing 34× (2 fonts per card) per paint cycle is wasteful.
- **Skip `MeasureString` for text centering** — compute it once and cache, or use `TextRenderer.DrawText` which handles centering with `TextFormatFlags.HorizontalCenter`.

**Concretely — the biggest single win is probably the image draw.** Let me show what I mean.

## The optimized `OnPaint`

Replace the current `OnPaint` and `DrawProductImage` with these versions:

```csharp
// Cache these as static readonly — creating Fonts per paint is a real cost.
private static readonly Font NameFont = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(9.5f);
private static readonly Font PriceFont = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9f);
private static readonly Font SizeButtonFont = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(8f);
private static readonly Font IconFont = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(16f);
private static readonly StringFormat EllipsisFormat = new()
{
    Trimming = StringTrimming.EllipsisCharacter,
    FormatFlags = StringFormatFlags.NoWrap,
};
private static readonly SolidBrush NameBrush = new(BrandPalette.NeutralText);
private static readonly SolidBrush PriceBrush = new(BrandPalette.NeutralTextMuted);
private static readonly SolidBrush IconBrush = new(BrandPalette.Tint25);
private static readonly SolidBrush BrandBrush = new(BrandPalette.Brand);
private static readonly SolidBrush HoverBrush = new(BrandPalette.Shade10);
private static readonly SolidBrush PlaceholderBrush = new(BrandPalette.Tint75);
private static readonly SolidBrush WhiteBrush = new(Color.White);
private static readonly Pen BorderPen = new(BrandPalette.Border);
private static readonly Pen SeparatorPen = new(BrandPalette.Tint25);

protected override void OnPaint(PaintEventArgs e)
{
    var g = e.Graphics;

    // Cheaper than AntiAlias for text — ClearTypeGridFit draws crisper text faster.
    g.TextRenderingHint = System.Drawing.Text.TextRenderingHint.ClearTypeGridFit;

    // Border
    g.DrawRectangle(BorderPen, 0, 0, Width - 1, Height - 1);

    // Image band
    var imageRect = new Rectangle(CardPadding, CardPadding, Width - CardPadding * 2, ImageBandHeight);
    DrawProductImage(g, imageRect);

    // Product name
    var nameRect = new RectangleF(CardPadding, imageRect.Bottom + 6, Width - CardPadding * 2, 32);
    g.DrawString(Product.ProductName, NameFont, NameBrush, nameRect, EllipsisFormat);

    // Price
    g.DrawString($"from ₱{Product.BasePrice:0}", PriceFont, PriceBrush,
        CardPadding, Height - SizeRowHeight - 20);

    // Size row
    DrawSizeRow(g);
}

private void DrawSizeRow(Graphics g)
{
    if (_sizes.Count == 0) return;

    for (int i = 0; i < _sizes.Count; i++)
    {
        var rect = _sizeButtonRects[i];
        var fill = (i == _hoveredSizeIndex) ? HoverBrush : BrandBrush;

        g.FillRectangle(fill, rect);

        var label = i < SizeLabels.Length ? SizeLabels[i] : (i + 1).ToString();

        // TextRenderer.DrawText is faster than DrawString and handles centering natively.
        TextRenderer.DrawText(g, label, SizeButtonFont, rect, Color.White,
            TextFormatFlags.HorizontalCenter | TextFormatFlags.VerticalCenter);

        if (i < _sizes.Count - 1)
            g.DrawLine(SeparatorPen, rect.Right, rect.Top + 4, rect.Right, rect.Bottom - 4);
    }
}

private void DrawProductImage(Graphics g, Rectangle imageRect)
{
    if (!_imageLoadAttempted)
    {
        _imageLoadAttempted = true;
        _cachedImage = TryLoadImage(Product.LocalImagePath);
    }

    if (_cachedImage is not null)
    {
        // Bilinear is far cheaper than HighQualityBicubic and looks identical at small sizes.
        g.InterpolationMode = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.InterpolationMode.Bilinear;

        // Preserve aspect ratio, centered.
        var targetRatio = (float)imageRect.Width / imageRect.Height;
        var imageRatio = (float)_cachedImage.Width / _cachedImage.Height;

        int drawWidth, drawHeight;
        if (imageRatio > targetRatio)
        {
            drawWidth = imageRect.Width;
            drawHeight = (int)(imageRect.Width / imageRatio);
        }
        else
        {
            drawHeight = imageRect.Height;
            drawWidth = (int)(imageRect.Height * imageRatio);
        }

        var drawX = imageRect.X + (imageRect.Width - drawWidth) / 2;
        var drawY = imageRect.Y + (imageRect.Height - drawHeight) / 2;

        g.DrawImage(_cachedImage, drawX, drawY, drawWidth, drawHeight);
        return;
    }

    // Placeholder
    g.FillRectangle(PlaceholderBrush, imageRect);

    TextRenderer.DrawText(g, "☕", IconFont, imageRect, BrandPalette.Tint25,
        TextFormatFlags.HorizontalCenter | TextFormatFlags.VerticalCenter);
}
```

**What this changes:**

- **Fonts, brushes, pens are `static readonly`** — created once per process, not per paint per card. This alone is huge. Currently 34 cards × 2 fonts per paint = 68 Font allocations per paint pass. Now: 0.
- **`TextRenderer.DrawText`** instead of `Graphics.DrawString` for the size button labels and placeholder glyph. It's meaningfully faster and handles centering.
- **`Bilinear`** instead of `HighQualityBicubic` for image scaling. Nearly identical visually at these sizes, dramatically faster.
- **`ClearTypeGridFit`** for text rendering. Faster than default anti-aliased rendering and crisper.
- **No `SmoothingMode = AntiAlias`** — it's the main perf killer for GDI+ drawing.

**One caveat:** the static fonts/brushes/pens live for the process lifetime. Don't dispose them. That's fine for a WinForms app — they're small and reused everywhere. (If you ever have a form with a custom font that should differ, we'd need to scope them differently — but for now, one shared palette is correct.)

Full replacement with the optimized painting:

```csharp
using CRM_Morcaffein.domain.entities;
using CRM_Morcaffein.Theme;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.winforms.Views.Controls
{
    /// <summary>
    /// A single drink card: product image + name + "from ₱price", with a row of size
    /// quick-add buttons pinned to the bottom. Tapping a size adds that size, qty 1, no
    /// modifiers, straight to the cart. Clicking the card body opens the full customizer.
    ///
    /// Control-less by design: NO child controls. Everything is drawn in OnPaint, and
    /// size-button clicks are hit-tested in OnMouseDown. This reduces each card from
    /// ~5-6 controls to 1, which is what makes the drinks panel paint fast and appear
    /// all at once instead of filling in progressively.
    ///
    /// All Fonts, Brushes, and Pens are static readonly — creating them per-paint is
    /// wasteful, and painting 34 cards per customer search means those allocations
    /// pile up fast.
    /// </summary>
    public class ProductCardControl : Panel
    {
        public Product Product { get; }

        public event EventHandler? CardClicked;
        public event EventHandler<ProductSize>? SizeQuickAdded;

        private const int SizeRowHeight = 26;
        private const int ImageBandHeight = 64;
        private const int CardPadding = 8;

        private static readonly string[] SizeLabels = { "S", "M", "L", "XL" };

        // ============ SHARED PAINT RESOURCES (created once for the whole process) ============
        private static readonly Font NameFont = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(9.5f);
        private static readonly Font PriceFont = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9f);
        private static readonly Font SizeButtonFont = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(8f);
        private static readonly Font IconFont = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(16f);

        private static readonly SolidBrush NameBrush = new(BrandPalette.NeutralText);
        private static readonly SolidBrush PriceBrush = new(BrandPalette.NeutralTextMuted);
        private static readonly SolidBrush IconBrush = new(BrandPalette.Tint25);
        private static readonly SolidBrush BrandBrush = new(BrandPalette.Brand);
        private static readonly SolidBrush HoverBrush = new(BrandPalette.Shade10);
        private static readonly SolidBrush PlaceholderBrush = new(BrandPalette.Tint75);

        private static readonly Pen BorderPen = new(BrandPalette.Border);
        private static readonly Pen SeparatorPen = new(BrandPalette.Tint25);

        private static readonly StringFormat EllipsisFormat = new()
        {
            Trimming = StringTrimming.EllipsisCharacter,
            FormatFlags = StringFormatFlags.NoWrap,
        };

        // =====================================================================

        private readonly List<ProductSize> _sizes;
        private Image? _cachedImage;
        private bool _imageLoadAttempted;

        private Rectangle[] _sizeButtonRects = Array.Empty<Rectangle>();
        private int _hoveredSizeIndex = -1;

        public ProductCardControl(Product product)
        {
            Product = product;
            _sizes = product.ProductSizes.ToList();

            Size = new Size(150, 156);
            Margin = new Padding(8);
            BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary;
            Cursor = Cursors.Hand;

            SetStyle(ControlStyles.UserPaint | ControlStyles.AllPaintingInWmPaint
                   | ControlStyles.OptimizedDoubleBuffer | ControlStyles.ResizeRedraw, true);

            if (_sizes.Count > 0)
            {
                _sizeButtonRects = new Rectangle[_sizes.Count];
                var buttonWidth = Width / _sizes.Count;
                for (int i = 0; i < _sizes.Count; i++)
                {
                    var x = i * buttonWidth;
                    var w = (i == _sizes.Count - 1) ? Width - x : buttonWidth;
                    _sizeButtonRects[i] = new Rectangle(x, Height - SizeRowHeight, w, SizeRowHeight);
                }
            }

            MouseEnter += (s, e) => { BackColor = BrandPalette.Tint90; Invalidate(); };
            MouseLeave += (s, e) =>
            {
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary;
                if (_hoveredSizeIndex != -1) { _hoveredSizeIndex = -1; Invalidate(); }
                else { Invalidate(); }
            };
        }

        protected override void Dispose(bool disposing)
        {
            if (disposing)
            {
                _cachedImage?.Dispose();
                _cachedImage = null;
            }
            base.Dispose(disposing);
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // PAINTING
        // =====================================================================

        protected override void OnPaint(PaintEventArgs e)
        {
            var g = e.Graphics;

            // ClearTypeGridFit is measurably faster than default anti-aliased text
            // rendering, and crisper for small UI text.
            g.TextRenderingHint = System.Drawing.Text.TextRenderingHint.ClearTypeGridFit;

            // Border
            g.DrawRectangle(BorderPen, 0, 0, Width - 1, Height - 1);

            // Image band
            var imageRect = new Rectangle(CardPadding, CardPadding, Width - CardPadding * 2, ImageBandHeight);
            DrawProductImage(g, imageRect);

            // Product name (single line, ellipsized)
            var nameRect = new RectangleF(CardPadding, imageRect.Bottom + 6, Width - CardPadding * 2, 32);
            g.DrawString(Product.ProductName, NameFont, NameBrush, nameRect, EllipsisFormat);

            // "from ₱X" price
            g.DrawString($"from ₱{Product.BasePrice:0}", PriceFont, PriceBrush,
                CardPadding, Height - SizeRowHeight - 20);

            // Size buttons
            DrawSizeRow(g);
        }

        private void DrawSizeRow(Graphics g)
        {
            if (_sizes.Count == 0) return;

            for (int i = 0; i < _sizes.Count; i++)
            {
                var rect = _sizeButtonRects[i];

                g.FillRectangle(i == _hoveredSizeIndex ? HoverBrush : BrandBrush, rect);

                var label = i < SizeLabels.Length ? SizeLabels[i] : (i + 1).ToString();

                // TextRenderer.DrawText handles centering natively and is faster than
                // Graphics.DrawString + MeasureString.
                TextRenderer.DrawText(g, label, SizeButtonFont, rect, Color.White,
                    TextFormatFlags.HorizontalCenter | TextFormatFlags.VerticalCenter);

                if (i < _sizes.Count - 1)
                    g.DrawLine(SeparatorPen, rect.Right, rect.Top + 4, rect.Right, rect.Bottom - 4);
            }
        }

        private void DrawProductImage(Graphics g, Rectangle imageRect)
        {
            if (!_imageLoadAttempted)
            {
                _imageLoadAttempted = true;
                _cachedImage = TryLoadImage(Product.LocalImagePath);
            }

            if (_cachedImage is not null)
            {
                // Bilinear is dramatically cheaper than HighQualityBicubic and looks
                // identical at this scale.
                g.InterpolationMode = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.InterpolationMode.Bilinear;

                var targetRatio = (float)imageRect.Width / imageRect.Height;
                var imageRatio = (float)_cachedImage.Width / _cachedImage.Height;

                int drawWidth, drawHeight;
                if (imageRatio > targetRatio)
                {
                    drawWidth = imageRect.Width;
                    drawHeight = (int)(imageRect.Width / imageRatio);
                }
                else
                {
                    drawHeight = imageRect.Height;
                    drawWidth = (int)(imageRect.Height * imageRatio);
                }

                var drawX = imageRect.X + (imageRect.Width - drawWidth) / 2;
                var drawY = imageRect.Y + (imageRect.Height - drawHeight) / 2;

                g.DrawImage(_cachedImage, drawX, drawY, drawWidth, drawHeight);
                return;
            }

            // Placeholder: tint block + coffee glyph
            g.FillRectangle(PlaceholderBrush, imageRect);

            TextRenderer.DrawText(g, "☕", IconFont, imageRect, BrandPalette.Tint25,
                TextFormatFlags.HorizontalCenter | TextFormatFlags.VerticalCenter);
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // INTERACTION
        // =====================================================================

        protected override void OnMouseDown(MouseEventArgs e)
        {
            base.OnMouseDown(e);

            for (int i = 0; i < _sizeButtonRects.Length; i++)
            {
                if (_sizeButtonRects[i].Contains(e.Location))
                {
                    SizeQuickAdded?.Invoke(this, _sizes[i]);
                    return;
                }
            }

            CardClicked?.Invoke(this, EventArgs.Empty);
        }

        protected override void OnMouseMove(MouseEventArgs e)
        {
            base.OnMouseMove(e);

            int newHover = -1;
            for (int i = 0; i < _sizeButtonRects.Length; i++)
            {
                if (_sizeButtonRects[i].Contains(e.Location)) { newHover = i; break; }
            }

            if (newHover != _hoveredSizeIndex)
            {
                _hoveredSizeIndex = newHover;
                Invalidate();
            }
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // IMAGE LOADING
        // =====================================================================

        private static Image? TryLoadImage(string? relativePath)
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(relativePath))
                return null;

            try
            {
                var fullPath = Path.IsPathRooted(relativePath)
                    ? relativePath
                    : Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, relativePath);

                if (!File.Exists(fullPath))
                    return null;

                using var stream = File.OpenRead(fullPath);
                return Image.FromStream(stream);
            }
            catch
            {
                return null;
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## What changed vs. your version

**Shared paint resources as `static readonly`:**

- `NameFont`, `PriceFont`, `SizeButtonFont`, `IconFont` — 4 fonts instead of 2 per card per paint.
- `NameBrush`, `PriceBrush`, `IconBrush`, `BrandBrush`, `HoverBrush`, `PlaceholderBrush` — 6 brushes instead of allocating 1-3 per paint per card.
- `BorderPen`, `SeparatorPen` — 2 pens instead of allocating 1-2 per paint.
- `EllipsisFormat` — 1 StringFormat instead of allocating 1 per paint.

**In `OnPaint`:**

- Set `TextRenderingHint = ClearTypeGridFit` (fast + crisp).
- **Removed** `SmoothingMode = AntiAlias` — that was the biggest single cost.
- **Removed** `InterpolationMode = HighQualityBicubic` from the outer OnPaint — moved into `DrawProductImage` as `Bilinear`.

**In `DrawSizeRow`:**

- Uses `TextRenderer.DrawText` with `HorizontalCenter | VerticalCenter` instead of `MeasureString` + `DrawString` + manual centering.
- Uses the shared `BrandBrush`/`HoverBrush` instead of allocating new brushes per button.

**In `DrawProductImage`:**

- Uses `Bilinear` instead of `HighQualityBicubic`.
- Uses `TextRenderer.DrawText` for the placeholder glyph.

**Net effect:** the per-paint allocation count drops from ~70 objects (across 34 cards) to zero. Paint time should drop meaningfully.

You're right — it's the FlowLayoutPanel with AutoScroll. Let me stop guessing about paint and address the actual structure.

## What's actually happening

The `FlowLayoutPanel` with `AutoScroll = true` recalculates scroll bounds **every time a child is added.** Even with `SuspendLayout`, WinForms still does layout work per-child because the panel has to know if the scroll range changed. And it triggers repaints on the visible cards as the scroll region grows.

So the "34 cards added one at a time and painted one at a time" is really "34 cards added, and each addition triggers a re-layout + repaint." No amount of freezing stops the layout work.

## Two ways to fix it

**Option 1 — Replace the FlowLayoutPanel with a TableLayoutPanel.**

`TableLayoutPanel` with a fixed grid (say, 4 columns × N rows) doesn't do the same scroll-bound recalculation on each add. Cards get placed into cells; the layout is computed once for the whole grid. This is how it *should* be done for a fixed-grid card layout.

**Downside:** you lose the "wrap dynamically based on panel width" behavior. If the panel is 400px wide, you'd get 2 columns; if 1000px wide, 4 or 5. With a fixed TableLayoutPanel grid, you'd commit to a column count and re-build the grid if the panel resizes. That's a real change.

**Option 2 — Keep FlowLayoutPanel but disable AutoScroll and use a separate scrollable parent.**

Or — better — put the FlowLayoutPanel inside a Panel with AutoScroll = true, and the flow panel itself with AutoScroll = false. The outer panel handles scrolling; the flow panel just lays out cards.

**Option 3 — The one you proposed: paginate.**

Instead of all 34 cards at once, show 8 or 12 per page, with a pager. Only 8-12 cards get built and rendered at a time. The panel appears instantly because there are only 8-12 of them.

You mentioned earlier you weren't thrilled about pagination friction, but if instant appearance matters more than scrolling, this is the guaranteed fix.

## My honest recommendation

Given all the work we've put into this, **Option 3 (pagination) is the guaranteed "instant" fix.** Because:

- 8-12 cards = guaranteed fast build + fast paint
- No FlowLayoutPanel scroll overhead
- The panel *cannot* be progressive when there are only 8-12 items

**Option 1 (TableLayoutPanel)** is the "right" way if you want to keep the full scroll. But it's a bigger refactor and I can't promise it'll be instant — it depends on whether the TableLayoutPanel does its own scroll recalculation, which it does but less aggressively than FlowLayoutPanel.

**Option 2** is a middle ground — outer panel scrolls, inner flow doesn't. Cheap to try.

## Which do you want?

- **Option 1** — TableLayoutPanel grid (keeps scroll, more work, might not be instant)
- **Option 2** — outer scroll container (5-minute try, might help, might not)
- **Option 3** — paginate the drinks panel (guaranteed instant, adds click friction)

**My recommendation: try Option 2 first.** It's a 5-minute change and it directly addresses the FlowLayoutPanel scroll overhead. If it doesn't help, go to Option 3 (pagination), which is the guaranteed fix.

**If you want to try Option 2:**

In `BuildDrinksArea()` in `TransactionView.cs`, change:

```csharp
_productsFlowPanel = new FlowLayoutPanel
{
    Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
    FlowDirection = FlowDirection.LeftToRight,
    WrapContents = true,
    AutoScroll = true,
    Padding = new Padding(12),
    BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
};

area.Controls.Add(_productsFlowPanel);
area.Controls.Add(header);
```

to:

```csharp
_productsFlowPanel = new FlowLayoutPanel
{
    Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
    FlowDirection = FlowDirection.LeftToRight,
    WrapContents = true,
    AutoScroll = false,   // ← the flow panel doesn't scroll
    Padding = new Padding(12),
    BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
};

// Wrap it in a scrolling container. The outer panel handles the scroll, the
// inner flow panel just lays out cards without recalculating scroll bounds
// every time a child is added — which was forcing a repaint per card.
var scrollContainer = new Panel
{
    Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
    AutoScroll = true,
    BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
};

// The flow panel is Dock=Top and sized to its preferred height as children
// are added. That's what makes the outer panel scroll correctly.
_productsFlowPanel.Dock = DockStyle.Top;
_productsFlowPanel.AutoSize = true;
_productsFlowPanel.AutoSizeMode = AutoSizeMode.GrowAndShrink;

scrollContainer.Controls.Add(_productsFlowPanel);

area.Controls.Add(scrollContainer);   // ← instead of _productsFlowPanel
area.Controls.Add(header);
```

**What this changes:**

- Flow panel no longer manages its own scroll. It's `Dock = Top`, `AutoSize = true` — it grows to fit its children.
- An outer `Panel` with `AutoScroll = true` handles the scroll. It scrolls the tall flow panel inside it.
- When cards are added, the flow panel grows, but the outer panel just adjusts its scrollbar range — it doesn't repaint every card.

**Caveat:** FlowLayoutPanel with `AutoSize = true` and `WrapContents = true` inside a fixed-width container needs the **width** to be constrained so it knows where to wrap. `Dock = Top` gives it the outer panel's width. Good.

**Try Option 2.** If it doesn't help, we go to Option 3 (pagination).

## Now — Option 3: paginate the drinks panel

Honest statement first: **this is the guaranteed fix for "appears all at once."** 8-12 cards per page can't render progressively because there aren't enough of them to fill in.

You said earlier you were wary of pagination friction, but nothing else has worked. This is the answer. And with only 8-12 cards visible, a cashier can find what they want by category or search, which is already how the panel works.

**Page size: 8.** 4 columns × 2 rows on a typical middle-column width. Fast to render, everything visible without scrolling in most window sizes.

**Structure:**

- Same `PaginationControl` you already built for Feedback and Customers.
- Reuse it in the drinks panel.
- The page slice happens client-side, from the already-cached product list — no API change.

**Where the pager goes:**

```text
[Header: Drinks + search + category]
[Flow panel — cards for current page]
[Pager: ◀ Page X of Y ▶]
```

## The changes

**1. Add fields** to `TransactionView`:

```csharp
private PaginationControl _drinksPager = null!;
private int _drinksPage = 1;
private const int DrinksPageSize = 8;
```

**2. In `BuildDrinksArea()`**, after creating `_productsFlowPanel` and before adding it to `area`, create the pager:

```csharp
_drinksPager = new PaginationControl
{
    Dock = DockStyle.Bottom,
};
_drinksPager.PageChanged += (s, newPage) =>
{
    _drinksPage = newPage;
    RefreshProductsPanel(forceRebuild: true);
};
```

Then add it to `area` **before** the flow panel:

```csharp
area.Controls.Add(_productsFlowPanel);
area.Controls.Add(_drinksPager);   // ← new: bottom-docked
area.Controls.Add(header);
```

**Order matters:** Fill control added first, then edge-docked (Bottom) added after. That's the WinForms docking convention.

**3. Update `RefreshProductsPanel`** to accept a `forceRebuild` flag and slice the product list by page:

```csharp
private void RefreshProductsPanel(bool forceRebuild = false)
{
    var signature = $"{_selectedCategory}|{_productSearchTxtBx.Text}";

    // Skip only if filter AND page haven't changed. When forced (pager click), rebuild.
    if (!forceRebuild && signature == _lastProductFilterSignature && _productsFlowPanel.Controls.Count > 0)
        return;

    // A new filter resets to page 1.
    if (!forceRebuild && signature != _lastProductFilterSignature)
    {
        _drinksPage = 1;
        _drinksPager.ResetToFirstPage();
    }

    _lastProductFilterSignature = signature;

    _productsFlowPanel.SuspendLayout();
    SuspendRedraw(_productsFlowPanel);
    try
    {
        _productsFlowPanel.Controls.Clear();
        if (_controller is null) return;

        var allProducts = _controller.GetProducts(_selectedCategory, _productSearchTxtBx.Text);

        // Update pager with the FULL count (across all pages).
        _drinksPager.UpdatePageInfo(allProducts.Count, _drinksPage, DrinksPageSize);

        // Slice out just this page's products.
        var pagedProducts = allProducts
            .Skip((_drinksPage - 1) * DrinksPageSize)
            .Take(DrinksPageSize)
            .ToList();

        // Preload images for just this page — much cheaper.
        foreach (var product in pagedProducts)
        {
            if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(product.LocalImagePath))
            {
                var fullPath = Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, product.LocalImagePath);
                if (File.Exists(fullPath))
                {
                    try { _ = File.ReadAllBytes(fullPath); } catch { }
                }
            }
        }

        // Build cards for just this page.
        foreach (var product in pagedProducts)
        {
            var card = new ProductCardControl(product);
            card.CardClicked += (s, e) => OpenCustomizerForNewItem(product);
            card.SizeQuickAdded += (s, size) => QuickAddToCart(product, size);
            _productsFlowPanel.Controls.Add(card);
        }
    }
    finally
    {
        ResumeRedraw(_productsFlowPanel);
        _productsFlowPanel.ResumeLayout();
    }
}
```

**4. Reset the page on customer change.** In `SelectCustomerAsync`, when a new customer is selected, we call `RefreshProductsPanel()` — which will detect the filter signature change and reset to page 1 automatically. Good.

But if the same filter signature somehow persists (unlikely), force it:

```csharp
_drinksPage = 1;
_drinksPager.ResetToFirstPage();
RefreshProductsPanel(forceRebuild: true);
```

Just to be safe, add those two lines before the `RefreshProductsPanel()` call in `SelectCustomerAsync`.

**5. Also reset on sale complete.** In `CompleteSale`, after `_controller = null;`, add:

```csharp
_drinksPage = 1;
_drinksPager.ResetToFirstPage();
```

That way the next customer starts on page 1.

A carousel is a genuinely different solution. Let me lay out what it means before you commit, because it changes the interaction model, not just the layout.

## What a carousel is here

Instead of a grid of 8-34 cards, you'd have:

- **One row** of cards visible at a time (say, 4-5 cards in a horizontal strip).
- **Left/right arrows** to slide to the next set of cards.
- **Or** one full-width card at a time with big previous/next.

Basically, pagination but horizontal, with smooth scroll animation instead of a page flip.

## What it changes

**Good:**

- Even fewer cards rendered at once. **4-5 instead of 8-12.** Guaranteed instant.
- Feels modern.
- Takes up less vertical space — could free up room for the Order column.

**Bad:**

- **Fewer cards visible.** A cashier sees 4-5 drinks at a time instead of 8-12. More clicks to browse the menu.
- **Horizontal scrolling is unusual on a POS.** People expect grids of products (Starbucks, McDonald's kiosks, every coffee shop POS). Carousels are for marketing sites, not tills.
- **Slower to find a specific item.** "I want Cold Brew" becomes 5 clicks through a carousel instead of 1 glance at a grid.
- **More code.** Animation, scroll state, arrow positioning.

## My honest read

**The carousel is a downgrade for POS usability.** It solves the render problem (fewer cards), but it costs you the thing POS interfaces actually optimize for: seeing many options at once.

**A grid of 8 cards** (my previous recommendation) is the same render cost as a carousel row of 8 cards. The difference is only in how you navigate to the next 8:

- **Grid + pager:** press "Next Page" → new 8 cards appear in the same grid. Familiar. Fast.
- **Carousel:** swipe/click arrows → new 8 cards slide in from the side. Novel. Slower.

**Same render cost. Different interaction. The grid wins for a till.**

## If you want the "one glance, no paging" experience

Then the real answer is: **make the cards cheap enough to render all 34 at once.** We tried freezing, caching, control-less cards, and it's still progressive — but the reason it's still progressive isn't that each card is expensive. Each card paints in maybe 2-5ms now (the optimizations landed). **34 cards × 3ms = ~100ms of paint time.** That's not progressive-fill territory — that's borderline instant.

So if it *still* feels progressive after all those optimizations, something else is going on. Let me be specific:

**The FlowLayoutPanel with AutoScroll is still the culprit.** Every card add triggers a layout pass. `SuspendLayout` reduces it but doesn't eliminate it. And Windows paints the visible slice after each layout pass. That's what you're seeing.

**The way to keep the full grid AND make it instant is to stop using FlowLayoutPanel.**

Use a **`TableLayoutPanel` with a fixed column count**. It computes its layout once when children are added, in one pass. No scroll-bound recalc per child. No per-child layout event.

**Column count:** pick based on the width. If the panel is ~800px and each card is 150px + 8px margin, that's 5 columns. You can hardcode 5 or compute it once and rebuild the grid if the panel resizes.

**Row count:** however many rows you need. 34 cards ÷ 5 columns = 7 rows.

**One-time layout, then done.** No progressive.

## So your three real options are:

**1. TableLayoutPanel grid — 5 columns × 7 rows, all 34 cards, no scrolling, no pagination, no carousel.**

This is what I'd do. It keeps the full catalog visible, it's how a POS grid should look, and TableLayoutPanel's layout is computed once.

**Code change:** swap `FlowLayoutPanel` for `TableLayoutPanel`. About 30 lines of change in `BuildDrinksArea` and `RefreshProductsPanel`.

**2. Pagination on the existing grid — 8 cards per page with Prev/Next.**

Works, guaranteed instant, adds clicks. Already wrote you the code for this.

**3. Carousel — 4-5 cards, arrows.**

Same render cost as #2, worse UX, more code. **I don't recommend it.**

## My recommendation

**Option 1 — TableLayoutPanel grid.** It's the actual fix. Same visual layout, all 34 cards, no scrolling overhead, instant paint. The change is contained — two methods in `TransactionView.cs`.

**Do you want me to write the TableLayoutPanel version?** It's a real code change but it's the answer to what you've been asking for since you first said "progressive."

**Or** — if you're not interested in more card-rendering work and just want to move on, we can do pagination (Option 2) which is already written and known to work.

**Which one — 1 (grid, all 34) or 2 (paginate)?**

```csharp
_productsFlowPanel = new FlowLayoutPanel
{
    Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
    FlowDirection = FlowDirection.LeftToRight,
    WrapContents = true,
    AutoScroll = true,
    Padding = new Padding(12),
    BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
};

area.Controls.Add(_productsFlowPanel);
area.Controls.Add(header);

return area;
```

**Replace with:**

```csharp
// TableLayoutPanel instead of FlowLayoutPanel: computes its layout ONCE when children
// are added, in a single pass. FlowLayoutPanel re-evaluates scroll bounds and
// re-layouts on every child add, which is what caused the drinks panel to render
// progressively. This renders the whole grid in one shot.
_productsGrid = new TableLayoutPanel
{
    Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
    ColumnCount = DrinksColumnCount,
    RowCount = 0,                       // rows added dynamically by RefreshProductsPanel
    AutoScroll = true,                  // still scrollable if 34 cards don't fit
    Padding = new Padding(12),
    BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
    GrowStyle = TableLayoutPanelGrowStyle.AddRows,
};

// Equal-width columns for the cards.
for (int i = 0; i < DrinksColumnCount; i++)
    _productsGrid.ColumnStyles.Add(new ColumnStyle(SizeType.Percent, 100f / DrinksColumnCount));

area.Controls.Add(_productsGrid);
area.Controls.Add(header);

return area;
```

**Notes:**

- `ColumnCount = 5` columns, equal width.
- `RowCount = 0` and `GrowStyle = AddRows` — rows are added automatically as we place cards.
- `AutoScroll = true` still works if the total height exceeds the visible area. Scrolling the whole grid is a single operation, not per-card.

## Change 3 — `RefreshProductsPanel()` — build the grid

Replace the entire method with:

```csharp
private void RefreshProductsPanel()
{
    var signature = $"{_selectedCategory}|{_productSearchTxtBx.Text}";
    if (signature == _lastProductFilterSignature && _productsGrid.Controls.Count > 0)
        return;

    _lastProductFilterSignature = signature;

    _productsGrid.SuspendLayout();
    SuspendRedraw(_productsGrid);
    try
    {
        _productsGrid.Controls.Clear();
        _productsGrid.RowStyles.Clear();
        _productsGrid.RowCount = 0;

        if (_controller is null) return;

        var products = _controller.GetProducts(_selectedCategory, _productSearchTxtBx.Text);

        // Preload all images for this batch before building cards.
        foreach (var product in products)
        {
            if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(product.LocalImagePath))
            {
                var fullPath = Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, product.LocalImagePath);
                if (File.Exists(fullPath))
                {
                    try { _ = File.ReadAllBytes(fullPath); } catch { }
                }
            }
        }

        // Compute the number of rows needed.
        var rows = (products.Count + DrinksColumnCount - 1) / DrinksColumnCount;
        _productsGrid.RowCount = rows;
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++)
            _productsGrid.RowStyles.Add(new RowStyle(SizeType.Absolute, 172f));   // card height + margin

        // Place each card in its cell.
        for (int i = 0; i < products.Count; i++)
        {
            var product = products[i];
            var card = new ProductCardControl(product)
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                Margin = new Padding(4),
            };
            card.CardClicked += (s, e) => OpenCustomizerForNewItem(product);
            card.SizeQuickAdded += (s, size) => QuickAddToCart(product, size);

            var row = i / DrinksColumnCount;
            var col = i % DrinksColumnCount;
            _productsGrid.Controls.Add(card, col, row);
        }
    }
    finally
    {
        ResumeRedraw(_productsGrid);
        _productsGrid.ResumeLayout();
    }
}
```

**What this does:**

- Clears the grid, computes row count from product count.
- Adds `RowStyles` for each row (fixed height 172px — 156 for card + 16 for margin).
- Places each card into `(col, row)` cells.
- The TableLayoutPanel computes layout **once** after `ResumeLayout` — no per-card recalculation.

**Notes on sizing:**

- **Row height 172** = card height 156 + 16 for top/bottom margin. If cards look too tall or too short, adjust.
- **Card `Dock = Fill`** so it fills its cell (width is set by the column percent, height by the row).
- **Card `Margin = 4`** for spacing between cards.

## Change 4 — remove references to `_productsFlowPanel`

The field `_productsFlowPanel` is still declared at the top of the class. Two options:

- **Delete the field** and update the `DoubleBuffered` reflection call in the constructor.
- **Or leave it** unused (adds a compiler warning).

**Delete it.** Then in the constructor, replace:

```csharp
        System.Reflection.BindingFlags.Instance | System.Reflection.BindingFlags.NonPublic)
```

with:

```csharp
        System.Reflection.BindingFlags.Instance | System.Reflection.BindingFlags.NonPublic)
    ?.SetValue(_productsGrid, true);
```

The `System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine($"[PERF] ...");` line references `products.Count`, which is now out of scope (it's inside the try block). Either delete the line or move it inside the try. **Simplest: delete it.**

The buttons are drawn at x=0..30, x=30..60, etc., using their old `Width / count` math, so they line up on the left and leave empty space to the right.

Let me address all three in one rewrite. Here's the updated `ProductCardControl.cs`:

```csharp
using CRM_Morcaffein.domain.entities;
using CRM_Morcaffein.Theme;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.winforms.Views.Controls
{
    public class ProductCardControl : Panel
    {
        public Product Product { get; }

        public event EventHandler? CardClicked;
        public event EventHandler<ProductSize>? SizeQuickAdded;

        private const int SizeRowHeight = 28;
        private const int CardPadding = 8;
        private const int NameAreaHeight = 26;
        private const int PriceAreaHeight = 18;

        private static readonly string[] SizeLabels = { "S", "M", "L", "XL" };

        // ============ SHARED PAINT RESOURCES ============
        private static readonly Font NameFont = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(9.5f);
        private static readonly Font PriceFont = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(8.5f);
        private static readonly Font SizeButtonFont = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(8.5f);
        private static readonly Font IconFont = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(28f);

        private static readonly SolidBrush NameBrush = new(BrandPalette.NeutralText);
        private static readonly SolidBrush PriceBrush = new(BrandPalette.NeutralTextMuted);
        private static readonly SolidBrush IconBrush = new(BrandPalette.Tint25);
        private static readonly SolidBrush BrandBrush = new(BrandPalette.Brand);
        private static readonly SolidBrush HoverBrush = new(BrandPalette.Shade10);
        private static readonly SolidBrush PlaceholderBrush = new(BrandPalette.Tint75);

        private static readonly Pen BorderPen = new(BrandPalette.Border);
        private static readonly Pen SeparatorPen = new(BrandPalette.Tint25);

        private static readonly StringFormat EllipsisFormat = new()
        {
            Trimming = StringTrimming.EllipsisCharacter,
            FormatFlags = StringFormatFlags.NoWrap,
        };

        // =====================================================================

        private readonly List<ProductSize> _sizes;
        private Image? _cachedImage;
        private bool _imageLoadAttempted;

        private Rectangle[] _sizeButtonRects = Array.Empty<Rectangle>();
        private int _hoveredSizeIndex = -1;

        public ProductCardControl(Product product)
        {
            Product = product;
            _sizes = product.ProductSizes.ToList();

            Size = new Size(150, 200);      // taller card — image gets more room
            Margin = new Padding(4);
            BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary;
            Cursor = Cursors.Hand;

            SetStyle(ControlStyles.UserPaint | ControlStyles.AllPaintingInWmPaint
                   | ControlStyles.OptimizedDoubleBuffer | ControlStyles.ResizeRedraw, true);

            // Computed here AND on every resize — the card's actual width is set by the
            // TableLayoutPanel cell it's placed in, not by the constructor's Size.
            RecomputeSizeButtonRects();

            MouseEnter += (s, e) => { BackColor = BrandPalette.Tint90; Invalidate(); };
            MouseLeave += (s, e) =>
            {
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary;
                if (_hoveredSizeIndex != -1) { _hoveredSizeIndex = -1; Invalidate(); }
                else { Invalidate(); }
            };
        }

        protected override void OnResize(EventArgs e)
        {
            base.OnResize(e);
            RecomputeSizeButtonRects();
            Invalidate();
        }

        private void RecomputeSizeButtonRects()
        {
            if (_sizes.Count == 0)
            {
                _sizeButtonRects = Array.Empty<Rectangle>();
                return;
            }

            _sizeButtonRects = new Rectangle[_sizes.Count];
            var buttonWidth = Width / _sizes.Count;
            for (int i = 0; i < _sizes.Count; i++)
            {
                var x = i * buttonWidth;
                var w = (i == _sizes.Count - 1) ? Width - x : buttonWidth;
                _sizeButtonRects[i] = new Rectangle(x, Height - SizeRowHeight, w, SizeRowHeight);
            }
        }

        protected override void Dispose(bool disposing)
        {
            if (disposing)
            {
                _cachedImage?.Dispose();
                _cachedImage = null;
            }
            base.Dispose(disposing);
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // PAINTING
        // =====================================================================

        protected override void OnPaint(PaintEventArgs e)
        {
            var g = e.Graphics;
            g.TextRenderingHint = System.Drawing.Text.TextRenderingHint.ClearTypeGridFit;

            using var borderPen = new Pen(BrandPalette.Border);
            g.DrawRectangle(borderPen, 0, 0, Width - 1, Height - 1);

            // Layout:
            //   [   large image area with rounded top    ]  (fills most of the card)
            //   [   product name                         ]
            //   [   from ₱price                          ]
            //   [   S | M | L | XL   size buttons         ]
            var nameTop = Height - SizeRowHeight - NameAreaHeight - PriceAreaHeight - CardPadding;
            var imageHeight = nameTop - CardPadding;

            var imageRect = new Rectangle(CardPadding, CardPadding, Width - CardPadding * 2, imageHeight);
            DrawProductImage(g, imageRect);

            // Product name
            var nameRect = new RectangleF(CardPadding, nameTop, Width - CardPadding * 2, NameAreaHeight);
            g.DrawString(Product.ProductName, NameFont, NameBrush, nameRect, EllipsisFormat);

            // Price
            var priceRect = new RectangleF(CardPadding, nameTop + NameAreaHeight, Width - CardPadding * 2, PriceAreaHeight);
            g.DrawString($"from ₱{Product.BasePrice:0}", PriceFont, PriceBrush, priceRect, EllipsisFormat);

            // Size buttons
            DrawSizeRow(g);
        }

        private void DrawSizeRow(Graphics g)
        {
            if (_sizes.Count == 0) return;

            for (int i = 0; i < _sizes.Count; i++)
            {
                var rect = _sizeButtonRects[i];
                g.FillRectangle(i == _hoveredSizeIndex ? HoverBrush : BrandBrush, rect);

                var label = i < SizeLabels.Length ? SizeLabels[i] : (i + 1).ToString();
                TextRenderer.DrawText(g, label, SizeButtonFont, rect, Color.White,
                    TextFormatFlags.HorizontalCenter | TextFormatFlags.VerticalCenter);

                if (i < _sizes.Count - 1)
                    g.DrawLine(SeparatorPen, rect.Right, rect.Top + 4, rect.Right, rect.Bottom - 4);
            }
        }

        private void DrawProductImage(Graphics g, Rectangle imageRect)
        {
            if (!_imageLoadAttempted)
            {
                _imageLoadAttempted = true;
                _cachedImage = TryLoadImage(Product.LocalImagePath);
            }

            if (_cachedImage is not null)
            {
                g.InterpolationMode = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.InterpolationMode.Bilinear;

                // "Cover" fit — fill the entire image area, crop the overflow. This is
                // what you want for a modern-looking card: image fills the space, no
                // letterboxing, no empty bands.
                var scaleX = (float)imageRect.Width / _cachedImage.Width;
                var scaleY = (float)imageRect.Height / _cachedImage.Height;
                var scale = Math.Max(scaleX, scaleY);

                var drawWidth = (int)(_cachedImage.Width * scale);
                var drawHeight = (int)(_cachedImage.Height * scale);
                var drawX = imageRect.X + (imageRect.Width - drawWidth) / 2;
                var drawY = imageRect.Y + (imageRect.Height - drawHeight) / 2;

                // Clip to the image rect so the "cover" doesn't bleed over the card.
                var saved = g.Clip;
                g.SetClip(imageRect, System.Drawing.Drawing2D.CombineMode.Replace);
                g.DrawImage(_cachedImage, drawX, drawY, drawWidth, drawHeight);
                g.Clip = saved;
                return;
            }

            // Placeholder: tint block + large coffee glyph
            g.FillRectangle(PlaceholderBrush, imageRect);
            TextRenderer.DrawText(g, "☕", IconFont, imageRect, BrandPalette.Tint25,
                TextFormatFlags.HorizontalCenter | TextFormatFlags.VerticalCenter);
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // INTERACTION
        // =====================================================================

        protected override void OnMouseDown(MouseEventArgs e)
        {
            base.OnMouseDown(e);

            for (int i = 0; i < _sizeButtonRects.Length; i++)
            {
                if (_sizeButtonRects[i].Contains(e.Location))
                {
                    SizeQuickAdded?.Invoke(this, _sizes[i]);
                    return;
                }
            }

            CardClicked?.Invoke(this, EventArgs.Empty);
        }

        protected override void OnMouseMove(MouseEventArgs e)
        {
            base.OnMouseMove(e);

            int newHover = -1;
            for (int i = 0; i < _sizeButtonRects.Length; i++)
            {
                if (_sizeButtonRects[i].Contains(e.Location)) { newHover = i; break; }
            }

            if (newHover != _hoveredSizeIndex)
            {
                _hoveredSizeIndex = newHover;
                Invalidate();
            }
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // IMAGE LOADING
        // =====================================================================

        private static Image? TryLoadImage(string? relativePath)
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(relativePath))
                return null;

            try
            {
                var fullPath = Path.IsPathRooted(relativePath)
                    ? relativePath
                    : Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, relativePath);

                if (!File.Exists(fullPath))
                    return null;

                using var stream = File.OpenRead(fullPath);
                return Image.FromStream(stream);
            }
            catch
            {
                return null;
            }
        }
    }
}
```
